-- This recipe holds each Roc module to a size: 500 lines is our most, the
-- whole file counted, its expects, blank lines and comments included.
-- Someone composing a program from ours should be able to take a module
-- whole, and a module big enough that they would take half of it is the
-- smell. A small module may keep its expects inside it, one-stop shopping;
-- a module with extensive tests moves them to a `*Spec.roc` beside it.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_module_size.shale glob='app/**/*.roc'
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_module_size.shale tests='*Spec.roc,gates/'
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_module_size.shale exempt=tools/module_size.txt all=1
--   cd <shale> && shale cookbook:roc/check_module_size.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob       the files to read, several separated by commas, `**/*.roc` by
--              default; a path holding `zig-out/` or `node_modules/` is left out;
--   tests      the project's test roots, separated by commas, `*Spec.roc,test/`
--              by default: an entry ending in `/` is a folder anywhere in a
--              path, `*X` a file name ending in `X`, anything else a whole
--              file name;
--   exempt     the project's exemptions file, below;
--   limit      the most lines a module may have, 500 by default;
--   all        with `all=1`, each module's count too;
--   self_test  with `self_test=1`, check the plants in
--              `cookbook/roc/plants/check_module_size/` (run from the shale
--              checkout's root).
--
-- Tests have no limit (Steve, 2026-11-19), so a file of a test root is
-- left out of the check by rule, not by an exemption line: a Spec is where a
-- module's extensive tests go once they would crowd it, and what someone
-- takes whole is the module, not its tests. A module's own expects count,
-- since they are part of what is taken.
--
-- The exemptions file names the modules that may be bigger, one `path --
-- reason` a line, the path as this recipe prints it (from the root the run
-- starts at). A blank line or one starting with `#` is skipped. A line with
-- no reason, a path that isn't there, or a path given twice stops the run,
-- and an exempt module now within the limit is a finding. Exemptions are
-- rare: a module that properly shows the workhorse pattern.
--
-- The findings, between two copies of the summary (cookbook/findings.shale):
--   path: module_size: N lines (limit L)
--   path: unneeded_exemption: N lines (limit L) needs no exemption
-- The run fails on any finding.
-- budget: steps=50000000 reads=100000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const TESTS = arg("tests", "*Spec.roc,test/")
const EXEMPT_FILE = arg("exempt", "")
const LIMIT = arg("limit", 500)
const ALL = arg("all", "") == "1"
const PLANTS = "cookbook/roc/plants/check_module_size/"
use("cookbook:findings.shale")

function comma_items(s)
  local out = {}
  for x in split(s, ",") do
    if trim(x) ~= "" then push(out, trim(x)) end
  end
  return out
end

-- Whether `path` is in one of the test roots `roots`, as the header says.
function in_test_root(path, roots)
  local base = basename(path)
  for r in roots do
    if ends_with(r, "/") then
      if starts_with(path, r) or contains(path, "/" .. r) or contains(path, ":" .. r) then return true end
    elseif starts_with(r, "*") then
      if ends_with(base, sub(r, 2)) then return true end
    elseif base == r then
      return true
    end
  end
  return false
end

-- The exemptions by path, each `{path, reason, line}`.
function exemptions_of(file)
  local by_path = {}
  if file == "" then return by_path end
  if not exists(file) then fail("check_module_size: no exemptions file " .. file) end
  local number = 0
  for raw in lines(read(file)) do
    number = number + 1
    local l = trim(raw)
    if l ~= "" and not starts_with(l, "#") then
      local at = find(l, " -- ")
      local where = file .. ":" .. number .. ": "
      if at == nil or trim(sub(l, at + 4)) == "" then fail("check_module_size: " .. where .. "expected `path -- reason`, got `" .. l .. "`") end
      local path = trim(sub(l, 1, at - 1))
      if not exists(path) then fail("check_module_size: " .. where .. "`" .. path .. "` is no file") end
      if has_key(by_path, path) then fail("check_module_size: " .. where .. "`" .. path .. "` is exempted twice") end
      by_path[path] = {path = path, reason = trim(sub(l, at + 4)), line = number}
    end
  end
  return by_path
end

-- The paths `globs` names, each once, sorted, build output left out.
function module_paths(globs)
  local seen = {}
  for g in comma_items(globs) do
    for p in glob(g) do
      if not contains(p, "zig-out/") and not contains(p, "node_modules/") then seen[p] = true end
    end
  end
  local out = keys(seen)
  sort(out)
  return out
end

-- The whole check, as `{summary, found, listing}`.
function module_sizes(opts)
  local exemptions = exemptions_of(opts.exempt)
  local roots = comma_items(opts.tests)
  local limit = opts.limit
  local found = {}
  local listing = {}
  local counts = {modules = 0, tests = 0, over = 0, exempt = 0, unneeded = 0}
  for path in module_paths(opts.glob) do
    local n = count_lines(path)
    if in_test_root(path, roots) then
      counts.tests = counts.tests + 1
      push(listing, path .. ": " .. n .. " lines, a test root's, no limit")
    else
      counts.modules = counts.modules + 1
      local exemption = get(exemptions, path)
      local note = ""
      if exemption ~= nil then
        counts.exempt = counts.exempt + 1
        note = " (exempt: " .. exemption.reason .. ")"
        if n <= limit then
          counts.unneeded = counts.unneeded + 1
          push(found, path .. ": unneeded_exemption: " .. n .. " lines (limit " .. limit .. ") needs no exemption")
        end
      elseif n > limit then
        counts.over = counts.over + 1
        push(found, path .. ": module_size: " .. n .. " lines (limit " .. limit .. ")")
      end
      push(listing, path .. ": " .. n .. " lines" .. note)
    end
  end
  local summary = "check_module_size (Roc): " .. counts.modules .. " modules, " .. counts.tests .. " test files left out; module_size " .. counts.over .. " over " .. limit .. " lines, " .. counts.exempt .. " exempt, unneeded_exemption " .. counts.unneeded
  return {summary = summary, found = found, listing = listing}
end

-- One self-test row: `{name, opts, found, says, stops}`. `found` is how many
-- findings it must give; `says` literals its output must hold, or its stop
-- with `stops`.
function self_test_row(row)
  local opts = {glob = PLANTS .. "*.roc", tests = "*Spec.roc,test/", exempt = "", limit = 20}
  for k in keys(get(row, "opts", {})) do opts[k] = row.opts[k] end
  local r = attempt(module_sizes, opts)
  local faults = {}
  local said = ""
  if get(row, "stops", false) then
    if r.ok then push(faults, "it didn't stop") else said = r.error end
  elseif not r.ok then
    push(faults, "it stopped: " .. r.error)
  else
    said = r.value.summary .. "\n" .. join(r.value.found, "\n") .. "\n" .. join(r.value.listing, "\n")
    if #r.value.found ~= get(row, "found", 0) then push(faults, #r.value.found .. " findings, not " .. get(row, "found", 0)) end
  end
  for literal in get(row, "says", {}) do
    if not contains(said, literal) then push(faults, "it lacks `" .. literal .. "`") end
  end
  print((#faults == 0 and "ok   " or "FAIL ") .. row.name .. (#faults == 0 and "" or ": " .. join(faults, "; ")))
  if #faults > 0 then print(said) end
  return #faults
end

function self_test()
  local at = PLANTS
  local rows = {
    {name = "a module one line over the limit is caught, one at it left alone", found = 1, says = {at .. "Over.roc: module_size: 21 lines (limit 20)", at .. "Under.roc: 20 lines"}},
    {name = "a Spec over the limit is a test root's, with no limit", found = 1, says = {at .. "OverSpec.roc: 22 lines, a test root's, no limit", "1 test files left out"}},
    {name = "an exempt module is left alone", opts = {exempt = at .. "exempt.txt"}, found = 0, says = {at .. "Over.roc: 21 lines (exempt: a plant past the limit on purpose)"}},
    {name = "an exemption of a module within the limit is a finding", opts = {exempt = at .. "exempt_unneeded.txt"}, found = 1, says = {at .. "Under.roc: unneeded_exemption: 20 lines (limit 20) needs no exemption"}},
    {name = "an exemption with no reason stops the run", opts = {exempt = at .. "exempt_no_reason.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"exempt_no_reason.txt:1: expected `path -- reason`"}},
    {name = "an exemption of a file that isn't there stops the run", opts = {exempt = at .. "exempt_missing.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"Gone.roc` is no file"}},
  }
  local wrong = 0
  for row in rows do wrong = wrong + self_test_row(row) end
  if wrong > 0 then fail("check_module_size self_test: " .. wrong .. " wrong") end
  print("check_module_size self_test: PASS (" .. #rows .. " rows)")
  return nil
end

function run_check()
  local r = module_sizes({glob = GLOB, tests = TESTS, exempt = EXEMPT_FILE, limit = LIMIT})
  if ALL then
    for l in r.listing do print(l) end
  end
  print_findings(r.summary, r.found)
  return r
end

-- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a
-- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it.
if SELF_TEST then
  self_test()
else
  local r = run_check()
  if #r.found > 0 then fail(r.summary) end
end

check_families

Modules that look alike but are spelled unlike, and one type name declared in two shapes, read from Roc's own parse trees across a whole tree, a gate with its plants' self-test in Roc too.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.print!, Shale.re_lines!, Shale.read!, Shale.roc_tree!, Shale.run!.
Roc: 718 lines in 4 files. Shale original: 183 lines, plus 1,328 lines in the 5 libraries it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Declarations, Finding, Text, Tree from the shared Roc library.

cookbook/roc/check_families/check_families.roc, 178 lines

## check_families, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## modules that look alike but are spelled unlike, and one type name with two
## meanings. A reader who knows `TreeSighting.trees_in_view` looks for
## `RailSighting.rails_in_view`, and one who knows `Cat.Pose` reads
## `Geom.Pose` as the same thing, so a family spelled unlike or a twin of
## another shape costs every reader a wrong guess. Its launcher,
## cookbook/roc/check_families.shale, is how it is run, and its header says
## the rules, `family` and `twin_name`. check_goldens.shale, beside this,
## holds its output on the plants to its goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/check_families.shale roles=tools/type_roles.txt
##   shale cookbook:roc/check_families.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`), `roles` (a file of type names each
## module may declare for itself) and `self_test` (`self_test=1` runs the
## plants, each through the launcher).
##
## This root globs the files (`Shale.glob!`), has Roc's parser read them
## (`Shale.roc_tree!`) and each one's text (`Shale.read!`), reads the roles
## file, and prints the verdict (`Shale.print!`, `Shale.fail!`). Its modules
## are beside it, a module a check (Family, Twin) and SelfTest; what they read
## (Tree, Declarations, Text) and Finding are the cookbook's Roc library,
## cookbook/roc/lib/.
## budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000 programs=100
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import lib.Declarations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree
import Family
import SelfTest
import Twin

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	if Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1" {
		SelfTest.run!(checks)
	} else {
		run_check!({})
	}
}

## What one parsed file gives the checks.
ParsedFile : { is_app : Bool, read : Family.FileRead }

## The check over the glob's files: the verdict printed, then a stop when a
## file didn't parse, or when there are findings, the summary the last line
## a caller reads.
run_check! : {} => {}
run_check! = |{}| {
	paths = Shale.glob!(Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc"))
	var $files = []
	var $refused = []
	for file in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
		if file.err == "" {
			source_lines = read_text!(file.path).split_on("\n")
			read = {
				path: file.path,
				declared: Declarations.from_file({ path: file.path, nodes: file.nodes, source_lines }),
				source_lines,
			}
			$files = $files.append({ is_app: Tree.is_app(file.nodes), read })
		} else if file.err.starts_with(file.path) {
			$refused = $refused.append(file.err)
		} else {
			$refused = $refused.append("${file.path}: ${file.err}")
		}
	}
	findings = run_checks!($files)
	found = findings.sort_with(Finding.order).map(Finding.line_of)
	summary = summary_of(findings, paths.len())
	print_findings!(summary, found)
	if !($refused.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in $refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		refusals = "roc-ast refused ${$refused.len().to_str()} files (named above)"
		why = "which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged"
		Shale.fail!("check_families: ${refusals}, ${why}")
	}
	if !(found.is_empty()) {
		Shale.fail!(summary)
	}
}

## Both checks over the files that parsed, the roles file read for
## `twin_name`.
run_checks! : List(ParsedFile) => List(Finding)
run_checks! = |files| {
	family_findings = Family.findings(modules_of(files))
	roles_file = Shale.arg!("roles", "")
	roles = if roles_file == "" {
		Set.empty()
	} else {
		read_word_set!(roles_file)
	}
	twin_files = files
		.keep_if(|file| !(file.is_app))
		.map(|file| { path: file.read.path, types: file.read.declared.types })
	family_findings.concat(Twin.findings(twin_files, roles))
}

## The modules among the files read, in their order.
modules_of : List(ParsedFile) -> List(Family.Module)
modules_of = |files| {
	var $modules = []
	for file in files {
		match Family.module_of(file.read) {
			IsModule(found) => {
				$modules = $modules.append(found)
			}
			NoModule => {}
		}
	}
	$modules
}

## The file's text. A file the parser read and the read finds gone stops the
## run.
read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("check_families: ${path} went missing during the check")
			""
		}
	}

## A list of one word a line, any note after `--` cut off, as a set
## (cookbook/roc/declared.shale's `word_set`). A missing file, a word listed
## twice, or a line of two words stops the run.
read_word_set! : Str => Set(Str)
read_word_set! = |path| {
	text = match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(found) => found
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("no word list ${path}")
			""
		}
	}
	var $words = Set.empty()
	for line in Text.lines(text) {
		word = Text.trim(Text.before_first(line, "--"))
		if word.contains(" ") or $words.contains(word) {
			Shale.fail!("${path}: `${word}` is no single new word")
		}
		if word != "" {
			$words = $words.insert(word)
		}
	}
	$words
}

## The checks, in the order the summary counts them.
checks : List(Str)
checks = ["family", "twin_name"]

## The counts, `check_families (Roc): N files; family N, twin_name N`.
summary_of : List(Finding), U64 -> Str
summary_of = |findings, file_count| {
	"check_families (Roc): ${file_count.to_str()} files; ${Finding.counts_of(findings, checks)}"
}

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/check_families/Family.roc, 238 lines

## The `family` check. Modules whose names end in the same word form a family
## when there are three or more of them (`CatSighting`, `TreeSighting`,
## `RailSighting`). A public name that more than half of a family's members
## have is the family's, and each member without it is a finding, unless the
## member names the missing name in its file's opening comment or the doc
## above its type, to say why it differs. A reader who knows one member then
## finds the others' names without looking.
import lib.Declarations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

Family := [].{

	## A module: a file that declares a type named for itself at the top
	## level, with the names of that type's members, and the text its doc
	## gives (the file's opening comment and the comment above its type).
	Module : {
		name : Str,
		path : Str,
		line : U64,
		members : Set(Str),
		doc : Str,
	}

	## A file as the check reads it: its path, what it declares, and its lines.
	FileRead : {
		path : Str,
		declared : Declarations,
		source_lines : List(Str),
	}

	## The file's module, when it declares one with any member that isn't a
	## method Roc calls by name.
	module_of : Family.FileRead -> [IsModule(Family.Module), NoModule]
	module_of = |file| {
		name = Tree.module_name(file.path)
		line = module_line(file.declared.types, name)
		is_member = |value| value.owner == name and !(language_fixed_names.contains(value.name))
		members = Set.from_list(file.declared.values.keep_if(is_member).map(|value| value.name))
		if line == 0 or members.is_empty() {
			NoModule
		} else {
			opening = Str.join_with(opening_comment(file.source_lines), " ")
			doc = "${opening} ${doc_above(file.source_lines, line)}"
			IsModule({
				name,
				path: file.path,
				line,
				members,
				doc,
			})
		}
	}

	## Each member that lacks a name most of its family has, a finding.
	findings : List(Family.Module) -> List(Finding)
	findings = |modules| {
		var $families = Dict.empty()
		for member in modules {
			match last_word(member.name) {
				Ok(word) => {
					$families = $families.insert(word, ($families.get(word) ?? []).append(member))
				}
				Err(OneWord) => {}
			}
		}
		$families
			.to_list()
			.sort_with(|(a, _), (b, _)| Text.byte_order(a, b))
			.map(|(word, members)| family_findings(word, members))
			.join()
	}
}

## The smallest family.
smallest_family : U64
smallest_family = 3

## The line of the last top-level type named `name`, the module's own, or 0.
module_line : List(Declarations.TypeDeclared), Str -> U64
module_line = |types, name| {
	var $line = 0
	for declared in types {
		if declared.name == name and declared.owner == "" {
			$line = declared.line
		}
	}
	$line
}

## How many of `members` have each name, by name.
holder_counts : List(Family.Module) -> Dict(Str, U64)
holder_counts = |members| {
	var $counts = Dict.empty()
	for member in members {
		for name in member.members.to_list() {
			counted = match $counts.get(name) {
				Ok(count) => count + 1
				Err(_) => 1
			}
			$counts = $counts.insert(name, counted)
		}
	}
	$counts
}

## The findings of the family whose names end in `word`.
family_findings : Str, List(Family.Module) -> List(Finding)
family_findings = |word, members| {
	if members.len() < smallest_family {
		return []
	}
	var $found = []
	counts = holder_counts(members).to_list().sort_with(|(a, _), (b, _)| Text.byte_order(a, b))
	for (name, holder_count) in counts {
		if holder_count * 2 > members.len() {
			for member in members {
				if !(member.members.contains(name)) and !(member.doc.contains("`${name}`")) {
					gap = {
						member,
						name,
						holder_count,
						member_count: members.len(),
						word,
					}
					$found = $found.append(missing_name(gap))
				}
			}
		}
	}
	$found
}

## A member without a name its family has: the name, how many of the
## family's members have it, and the family's last word.
Gap : {
	member : Family.Module,
	name : Str,
	holder_count : U64,
	member_count : U64,
	word : Str,
}

## The finding of a member without its family's `name`.
missing_name : Gap -> Finding
missing_name = |gap| {
	who = "`${gap.member.name}` has no `${gap.name}`"
	counted = "${gap.holder_count.to_str()} of the ${gap.member_count.to_str()}"
	which = "which ${counted} `*${gap.word}` modules have"
	advice = "spell it alike, or name it in the module's doc to say why not"
	{
		path: gap.member.path,
		line: gap.member.line,
		check: "family",
		what: "${who}, ${which}: ${advice}",
	}
}

## The last word of a name of two or more words.
last_word : Str -> Try(Str, [OneWord])
last_word = |name|
	match Text.name_words(name) {
		[_, .., last] => Ok(last)
		_ => Err(OneWord)
	}

## The comment lines that open a file, trimmed.
opening_comment : List(Str) -> List(Str)
opening_comment = |source_lines| {
	var $out = []
	for line in source_lines {
		trimmed = Text.trim(line)
		if !(trimmed.starts_with("#")) {
			return $out
		}
		$out = $out.append(trimmed)
	}
	$out
}

## The comment lines directly above line `line`, nearest first, lowercased
## and joined: a declaration's doc.
doc_above : List(Str), U64 -> Str
doc_above = |source_lines, line| {
	var $parts = []
	var $above = line - 1
	while $above >= 1 {
		trimmed = Text.trim(Text.line_at(source_lines, $above))
		if !(trimmed.starts_with("#")) {
			return Str.join_with($parts, " ")
		}
		$parts = $parts.append(Text.lower(trimmed))
		$above = $above - 1
	}
	Str.join_with($parts, " ")
}

## The methods Roc calls by name, from Roc's docs/langref/static-dispatch.md
## and operators.md, with the encoders' `encode` and `decode`: a module that
## declares one has it because Roc asks, not as a name of its own. The same
## list is cookbook/roc/headers.shale's LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES.
language_fixed_names : Set(Str)
language_fixed_names = Set.from_list([
	"to_inspect",
	"is_eq",
	"to_hash",
	"plus",
	"minus",
	"times",
	"div_by",
	"div_trunc_by",
	"rem_by",
	"is_lt",
	"is_lte",
	"is_gt",
	"is_gte",
	"range_exclusive_to",
	"range_inclusive_to",
	"range_exclusive_from",
	"range_inclusive_from",
	"range_iter",
	"range_len_if_known",
	"negate",
	"not",
	"from_numeral",
	"from_quote",
	"from_interpolation",
	"iter",
	"next",
	"parser_for",
	"encoder_for",
	"map",
	"map!",
	"subscript",
	"encode",
	"decode",
])

cookbook/roc/check_families/SelfTest.roc, 210 lines

## The recipe's self-test: each plant under
## cookbook/roc/plants/check_families/ run through the launcher, held to its
## findings, its exit and what it says (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `check_plants`).
import pf.Shale

SelfTest := [].{

	## Each row run as a child of its own, through `launcher`; a check of
	## `checks` no row fires fails too, since it could be blind.
	run! : List(Str) => {}
	run! = |checks| {
		var $wrong = 0
		var $fired = Set.empty()
		for row in rows {
			command = ["shale", launcher, "glob=${row.plant}"].concat(row.arguments)
			result = Shale.run!({
				argv: command,
				keep: Whole(4000000),
				timeout_ms: 120000,
				want: "",
			})
			faults = find_faults!(row, result, checks)
			for (check, _) in row.counts {
				$fired = $fired.insert(check)
			}
			if faults.is_empty() {
				Shale.print!("ok   ${row.plant}")
			} else {
				Shale.print!("FAIL ${row.plant}: ${Str.join_with(faults, "; ")}")
				$wrong = $wrong + 1
				Shale.print!(result.out)
			}
		}
		for check in checks {
			if !($fired.contains(check)) {
				Shale.print!("FAIL `${check}` has no plant")
				$wrong = $wrong + 1
			}
		}
		if $wrong > 0 {
			Shale.fail!("check_families self_test: ${$wrong.to_str()} wrong")
		}
		row_count = rows.len().to_str()
		proof = "each plant gives its findings and a nonzero exit, each clean case none and exit 0"
		Shale.print!("check_families self_test: PASS (${row_count} rows: ${proof})")
	}
}

## The launcher, which the self-test runs each plant through.
launcher : Str
launcher = "cookbook:roc/check_families.shale"

plants : Str
plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_families/"

## A plant's run: its files (a glob below `plants`) and its other arguments,
## the findings each check must print, the literals its output must hold,
## and whether it must stop without a finding.
Row : {
	plant : Str,
	arguments : List(Str),
	counts : List((Str, U64)),
	says : List(Str),
	stops : Bool,
}

## A plant, given as a glob below `plants`, with no finding to give.
quiet : Str, List(Str) -> Row
quiet = |plant, arguments| {
	plant: "${plants}${plant}",
	arguments,
	counts: [],
	says: [],
	stops: Bool.False,
}

## What a plant that fires is run with and must give.
Firing : {
	plant : Str,
	arguments : List(Str),
	counts : List((Str, U64)),
	says : List(Str),
}

## What a plant that stops is run with and must say.
Stopping : {
	plant : Str,
	arguments : List(Str),
	says : List(Str),
}

## A plant with findings, and what they say.
fires : Firing -> Row
fires = |wanted| {
	plant: "${plants}${wanted.plant}",
	arguments: wanted.arguments,
	counts: wanted.counts,
	says: wanted.says,
	stops: Bool.False,
}

## A plant that must stop before any finding, saying what it says.
stops : Stopping -> Row
stops = |wanted| {
	plant: "${plants}${wanted.plant}",
	arguments: wanted.arguments,
	counts: [],
	says: wanted.says,
	stops: Bool.True,
}

rows : List(Row)
rows = [
	fires({
		plant: "family/*.roc",
		arguments: [],
		counts: [("family", 1)],
		says: [
			"RailSighting.roc:4: family: `RailSighting` has no `in_view`, "
				.concat("which 3 of the 4 `*sighting` modules have"),
		],
	}),
	quiet("family_answered/*.roc", []),
	quiet("family_small/*.roc", []),
	quiet("family_half/*.roc", []),
	fires({
		plant: "twin_name/*.roc",
		arguments: [],
		counts: [("twin_name", 1)],
		says: ["Bird.roc:4: twin_name: `Pose` is also declared at", "Cat.roc:4"],
	}),
	quiet("twin_name/*.roc", ["roles=${plants}roles.txt"]),
	fires({
		plant: "twin_name/*.roc",
		arguments: ["roles=${plants}other_roles.txt"],
		counts: [("twin_name", 1)],
		says: ["`Pose` is also declared at"],
	}),
	stops({
		plant: "twin_name/*.roc",
		arguments: ["roles=${plants}no_such.txt"],
		says: ["no word list"],
	}),
	quiet("twin_app/*.roc", []),
	quiet("twin_copy/*.roc", []),
	quiet("twin_namespace/*.roc", []),
	fires({
		plant: "twin_namespace_clash/*.roc",
		arguments: [],
		counts: [("twin_name", 1)],
		says: ["`Lamp` is also declared at"],
	}),
	stops({ plant: "broken/*.roc", arguments: [], says: ["refused: "] }),
]

## The last line of `out` that isn't one of Shale's `──` lines.
last_said : Str -> Str
last_said = |out|
	out.trim().split_on("\n").fold(
		"",
		|last, line|
			if line.starts_with("──") or line.trim() == "" {
				last
			} else {
				line
			},
	)

## The findings `row` wants of `check`.
wanted_count : Row, Str -> U64
wanted_count = |row, check| {
	var $wanted = 0
	for (counted, count) in row.counts {
		if counted == check {
			$wanted = count
		}
	}
	$wanted
}

## What is wrong with one row's run (cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale's
## `row_faults`).
find_faults! : Row, { code : I64, out : Str }, List(Str) => List(Str)
find_faults! = |row, result, checks| {
	must_fail = row.stops or !(row.counts.is_empty())
	var $faults = []
	if must_fail and result.code == 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited 0")
	}
	if !(must_fail) and result.code != 0 {
		$faults = $faults.append("it exited ${result.code.to_str()}")
	}
	for check in checks {
		found = Shale.re_lines!(result.out, "^[^ ]+:[0-9]+: ${check}: ").len()
		wanted = wanted_count(row, check)
		if found != wanted {
			$faults = $faults.append("${check} printed ${found.to_str()}, not ${wanted.to_str()}")
		}
	}
	if !(row.stops) and !(last_said(result.out).contains(" files; ")) {
		$faults = $faults.append("its last line is no summary: ${last_said(result.out)}")
	}
	for literal in row.says {
		if !(result.out.contains(literal)) {
			$faults = $faults.append("its output lacks `${literal}`")
		}
	}
	$faults
}

## The `twin_name` check: one type name declared in two modules with two
## different shapes, such as `Cat.Pose` and `Geom.Pose`, one word with two
## meanings, so a reader who knows one guesses the other wrong. It is
## reported once, at its first declaration, with the others listed. Twins of
## one shape are copies, as when a package can't import its platform's type,
## so they are no finding. A namespace module (`Collider := [].{ ... }`)
## builds a type and declares none, and so does an alias of the twin
## (`Pose : Geom.Pose`). App files are left out by the caller, because every
## app declares what its platform asks for.
import lib.Declarations
import lib.Finding
import lib.Text

Twin := [].{

	## Where a type is declared, and its shape.
	Place : {
		path : Str,
		line : U64,
		shape : Str,
	}

	## A file's path and the types it declares.
	FileTypes : { path : Str, types : List(Declarations.TypeDeclared) }

	## The twins among the files' types, in the order the files were read.
	## A name in `roles` is each module's own to declare, so it has no twin.
	findings : List(Twin.FileTypes), Set(Str) -> List(Finding)
	findings = |files, roles| {
		is_role = |name| roles.contains(name)
		is_twin = |(name, places)| places.len() > 1 and !(is_role(name)) and has_two_shapes(places)
		files
			.fold(Dict.empty(), with_places)
			.to_list()
			.sort_with(|(a, _), (b, _)| Text.byte_order(a, b))
			.keep_if(is_twin)
			.map(|(name, places)| twin_finding(name, places))
	}
}

## `places_by_name` with the file's types added, each name once a file, at
## its first declaration, and only where the type declares a shape of its
## own.
with_places : Dict(Str, List(Twin.Place)), Twin.FileTypes -> Dict(Str, List(Twin.Place))
with_places = |places_by_name, file| {
	var $places = places_by_name
	var $seen = Set.empty()
	for declared in file.types {
		if !($seen.contains(declared.name)) and !(is_type_elsewhere(declared)) {
			$seen = $seen.insert(declared.name)
			place = {
				path: file.path,
				line: declared.line,
				shape: declared.shape,
			}
			named_so_far = $places.get(declared.name) ?? []
			$places = $places.insert(declared.name, named_so_far.append(place))
		}
	}
	$places
}

## Whether the type declares nothing of its own: a namespace module, or an
## alias of a type of its own name.
is_type_elsewhere : Declarations.TypeDeclared -> Bool
is_type_elsewhere = |declared| {
	shape = declared.shape
	shape == "" or shape == "[]" or shape == declared.name
}

has_two_shapes : List(Twin.Place) -> Bool
has_two_shapes = |places|
	match places {
		[first, .. as rest] => rest.any(|place| place.shape != first.shape)
		[] => Bool.False
	}

## The finding at the name's first place, naming the others.
twin_finding : Str, List(Twin.Place) -> Finding
twin_finding = |name, places|
	match places {
		[first, .. as rest] => {
			others = Str.join_with(rest.map(|place| "${place.path}:${place.line.to_str()}"), ", ")
			{
				path: first.path,
				line: first.line,
				check: "twin_name",
				what: "`${name}` is also declared at ${others}, in another shape",
			}
		}
		[] => crash "check_families: a twin with no place"
	}

The libraries it loads: cookbook/roc/declared.shale (1,075 lines), cookbook/findings.shale (21 lines), cookbook/roc/parsed.shale (34 lines), cookbook/roc/gate_recipe.shale (102 lines), cookbook/roc/headers.shale (96 lines).

-- This recipe checks that modules which look alike are spelled alike, and
-- that one type name means one thing.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/check_families.shale
--   shale cookbook:roc/check_families.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob       the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default;
--   roles      a project's file of type names, one a line, that each module
--              may declare for itself, as `Id` in `Message.Id`: read with its
--              module it is a two-part name, so `twin_name` leaves it alone;
--   self_test  with `self_test=1`, check the plants in
--              `cookbook/roc/plants/check_families/`.
--
-- The checks:
--
--   family     Modules whose names end in the same word form a family when
--              there are three or more (`CatSighting`, `TreeSighting`,
--              `RailSighting`). A public name that more than half of a
--              family's members have is the family's, and each member
--              without it is a finding. A member that differs for a good
--              reason says so by naming the missing name in the `##` doc
--              above its type, or in the file's opening comment.
--   twin_name  One public type name declared in two modules with different
--              shapes, such as `Cat.Pose` and `Geom.Pose`: one word, two
--              meanings. It is reported once, at its first declaration, with
--              the others listed. Twins of one shape are copies, as when a
--              package can't import its platform's type, so they are no
--              finding. A shape ignores what a name is qualified by, and the
--              order of fields and tags. A namespace module
--              (`Collider := [].{ ... }`) builds a type and declares none, and
--              so does an alias of the twin (`Pose : Geom.Pose`). App files are
--              left out, because every app declares what its platform asks for.
--
-- `twin_name` sees only the files read, so give it the whole tree: run by
-- folder, it misses twins in two folders.
--
-- A module is a file that declares a type named for itself, and its public
-- names are that type's members. The output is the counts, one line per
-- finding, and the counts again (cookbook/findings.shale).
-- The run fails if there are findings, or if any file doesn't parse, and the
-- files that do parse are judged either way.
-- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 output_bytes=4000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const GLOB = arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const ROLES_FILE = arg("roles", "")
use("./declared.shale")
use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
use("./gate_recipe.shale")
use("./headers.shale")
const CHECKS = {"family", "twin_name"}
const SMALLEST_FAMILY = 3

-- The file's opening comment and the doc above line `line`, as one text.
function module_doc_text(path, line)
  local src = split(read(path), "\n")
  return join(opening_comment(src), " ") .. " " .. doc_above(src, line)
end

-- Each module in the files read, as `{name, path, line, members}`, where
-- `members` is the set of its type's member names.
function modules_of(declared_by_file)
  local out = {}
  for one in declared_by_file do
    local name = module_name(one.path)
    local module = {name = name, path = one.path, line = 0, members = {}}
    for d in one.declared do
      if d.kind == "type" and d.name == name and d.owner == "" then module.line = d.line end
      if d.kind == "value" and d.owner == name and not has_key(LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES, d.name) then module.members[d.name] = true end
    end
    if module.line ~= 0 and #keys(module.members) > 0 then push(out, module) end
  end
  return out
end

function judge_families(modules, report)
  local family_of = {}
  for m in modules do
    local ws = name_words(m.name)
    if #ws > 1 then push_at(family_of, ws[#ws], m) end
  end
  for word in sort(keys(family_of)) do
    local members = family_of[word]
    if #members >= SMALLEST_FAMILY then
      local holders = {}
      for m in members do
        for name in keys(m.members) do incr(holders, name) end
      end
      for name in sort(keys(holders)) do
        if holders[name] * 2 > #members then
          for m in members do
            if not has_key(m.members, name) and not contains(module_doc_text(m.path, m.line), "`" .. name .. "`") then
              push(report, {path = m.path, line = m.line, check = "family", what = "`" .. m.name .. "` has no `" .. name .. "`, which " .. holders[name] .. " of the " .. #members .. " `*" .. word .. "` modules have: spell it alike, or name it in the module's doc to say why not"})
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return nil
end

-- Whether the type `d` declares nothing of its own: a namespace module, or an
-- alias of a type of its own name.
function is_type_elsewhere(d)
  return d.shape == "" or d.shape == "[]" or d.shape == d.name
end

function has_two_shapes(places)
  for p in drop(places, 1) do
    if p.shape ~= places[1].shape then return true end
  end
  return false
end

function judge_twins(declared_by_file, roles, report)
  local places_of = {}
  for one in declared_by_file do
    if not one.is_app then
      local seen = {}
      for d in one.declared do
        if d.kind == "type" and not has_key(seen, d.name) and not is_type_elsewhere(d) then
          seen[d.name] = true
          push_at(places_of, d.name, d)
        end
      end
    end
  end
  for name in sort(keys(places_of)) do
    local places = places_of[name]
    if #places > 1 and not has_key(roles, name) and has_two_shapes(places) then
      local others = {}
      for p in drop(places, 1) do push(others, p.path .. ":" .. p.line) end
      push(report, {path = places[1].path, line = places[1].line, check = "twin_name", what = "`" .. name .. "` is also declared at " .. join(others, ", ") .. ", in another shape"})
    end
  end
  return nil
end

function self_test()
  local at = "cookbook:roc/plants/check_families/"
  check_plants("check_families", "cookbook:roc/check_families.shale", CHECKS, {
    {glob = at .. "family/*.roc", counts = {family = 1}, says = {"RailSighting.roc:4: family: `RailSighting` has no `in_view`, which 3 of the 4 `*sighting` modules have"}},
    {glob = at .. "family_answered/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "family_small/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "family_half/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", counts = {twin_name = 1}, says = {"Bird.roc:4: twin_name: `Pose` is also declared at", "Cat.roc:4"}},
    {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", args = {"roles=" .. at .. "roles.txt"}},
    {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", args = {"roles=" .. at .. "other_roles.txt"}, counts = {twin_name = 1}, says = {"`Pose` is also declared at"}},
    {glob = at .. "twin_name/*.roc", args = {"roles=" .. at .. "no_such.txt"}, stops = true, says = {"no word list"}},
    {glob = at .. "twin_app/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "twin_copy/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "twin_namespace/*.roc"},
    {glob = at .. "twin_namespace_clash/*.roc", counts = {twin_name = 1}, says = {"`Lamp` is also declared at"}},
    {glob = at .. "broken/*.roc", stops = true, says = {"refused: "}},
  })
  return nil
end

function run_check()
  local paths = glob(GLOB)
  local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths)
  local declared_by_file = {}
  for f in parsed.files do push(declared_by_file, {path = f.path, is_app = is_app(f), declared = declarations_of(f)}) end
  local report = {}
  judge_families(modules_of(declared_by_file), report)
  judge_twins(declared_by_file, ROLES_FILE == "" and {} or word_set(ROLES_FILE), report)
  local verdict = verdict_of("check_families", CHECKS, report, #paths)
  print_findings(verdict.summary, verdict.found)
  fail_if_refused("check_families", parsed.refused)
  return verdict
end

-- This `fail` stands at the top level so the summary is the last line a
-- caller reads: a stop inside a function prints the calls after it.
if SELF_TEST then
  self_test()
else
  local verdict = run_check()
  if #verdict.found > 0 then fail(verdict.summary) end
end

find_deep_calls

Calls nested three or more deep, read inside out, found from Roc's own parse tree: each node's call depth worked out from its kids, the outermost call of each nest reported with the call at its bottom.

cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls/find_deep_calls.roc, 224 lines

## find_deep_calls, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md):
## calls nested three or more deep, like `f(g(h(x)))`, which have to be read
## from the inside out, where Roc's style guide (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md)
## asks for code that reads left to right: a method chain, a pipe or a named
## middle step. Its launcher, cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls.shale, is how it
## is run, and its header says the rule. check_goldens.shale, beside this,
## holds its output on the plants to its goldens, line for line.
##
##   cd <repo> && shale cookbook:roc/find_deep_calls.shale glob=app/**/*.roc min=4
##   shale cookbook:roc/find_deep_calls.shale self_test=1
##
## The arguments: `glob` (`**/*.roc`), `min` (3), `loose` (`loose=1` passes a
## record's, list's or tuple's depth through), `house` (`house=0` leaves out
## the house style, which here is the whole check) and `self_test`
## (`self_test=1` checks the plants' marks).
##
## The effects: `Shale.arg!` for the arguments, `Shale.glob!` for the files,
## `Shale.roc_tree!` for Roc's own parser's tree of each, `Shale.read!` for
## a finding's source line, and `Shale.print!` and `Shale.fail!` for the
## verdict. Nest, beside this, is the rule, over Tree; NestFinding is how a
## finding prints; SelfTest checks the plants.
## budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000 roc_cpu_ms=600000
app [main!] { lib: "../lib/main.roc", pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc" }

import pf.Shale
import NestFinding
import Nest
import SelfTest
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

## What a run checks: the files a glob names, and the rule, or the plants
## at the self-test's own `min`.
Settings : {
	pattern : Str,
	rule : Nest.Rule,
	house : [Kept, LeftOut],
}

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	is_self_test = Shale.arg!("self_test", "") == "1"
	settings = read_settings!(is_self_test)
	checked = run_check!(settings)
	if is_self_test {
		SelfTest.run!(checked)
	}
}

# ── The arguments

## The settings the arguments give. `min` is read before the files are
## globbed and `house` after, as the Shale original read them, so a run
## given two bad values stops on the same one.
read_settings! : Bool => Settings
read_settings! = |is_self_test| {
	pattern = if is_self_test {
		"${SelfTest.plants}*.roc"
	} else {
		Shale.arg!("glob", "**/*.roc")
	}
	strictness = if Shale.arg!("loose", "") == "1" {
		Loose
	} else {
		Strict
	}
	min = if is_self_test {
		3
	} else {
		read_min!({})
	}
	{
		pattern,
		rule: { min, strictness },
		house: Kept,
	}
}

## The `min=` depth: 3 unless given, and any integer.
read_min! : {} => I64
read_min! = |{}| {
	given = Shale.arg!("min", "3")
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(min) => min
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("find_deep_calls: min=${given} is not an integer")
			0
		}
	}
}

## Whether `house=0` leaves the house style out (cookbook/roc/house.shale):
## here that is every finding, since `nested` is house style.
read_house! : {} => [Kept, LeftOut]
read_house! = |{}| {
	house = Shale.arg!("house", "1")
	if house != "0" and house != "1" {
		Shale.fail!("house must be 1 (the default) or 0, not ${house}")
	}
	if house == "0" {
		LeftOut
	} else {
		Kept
	}
}

# ── The run

## The check over the glob's files: the verdict printed, then a stop when a
## file didn't parse. The findings are a report, not a failure, so a run
## that parses every file exits 0; a caller holds the count.
run_check! : Settings => { paths : List(Str), findings : List(NestFinding) }
run_check! = |given| {
	paths = Shale.glob!(given.pattern)
	settings = { ..given, house: read_house!({}) }
	var $findings = []
	var $refused = []
	for file in Shale.roc_tree!(paths) {
		if file.err == "" {
			parsed = { path: file.path, syntax_nodes: file.nodes }
			$findings = $findings.concat(find_file_findings!(parsed, settings))
		} else if file.err.starts_with(file.path) {
			$refused = $refused.append(file.err)
		} else {
			$refused = $refused.append("${file.path}: ${file.err}")
		}
	}
	summary_line = summary($findings, { file_count: paths.len(), settings })
	print_findings!(summary_line, $findings.map(NestFinding.finding_line))
	if !($refused.is_empty()) {
		for refusal in $refused {
			Shale.print!("refused: ${refusal}")
		}
		refusals = "roc-ast refused ${$refused.len().to_str()} files (named above)"
		why = "which have no tree to judge; every other file was judged"
		Shale.fail!("find_deep_calls: ${refusals}, ${why}")
	}
	{ paths, findings: $findings }
}

## A parsed file's findings. Its text is read only when it has a nest, for
## the source lines; a file the parser read and the read finds gone stops
## the run.
find_file_findings! : { path : Str, syntax_nodes : List(Tree.Node) }, Settings => List(NestFinding)
find_file_findings! = |file, settings| {
	nests = match settings.house {
		Kept => Nest.nests_in(file.syntax_nodes, settings.rule)
		LeftOut => []
	}
	if nests.is_empty() {
		[]
	} else {
		source_lines = match Shale.read!(file.path) {
			Found(text) => text.split_on("\n")
			Missing => {
				Shale.fail!("find_deep_calls: ${file.path} went missing during the check")
				[]
			}
		}
		nests.map(
			|nest| {
				source_line = match source_lines.get(nest.line - 1) {
					Ok(text) => text
					Err(_) => crash "find_deep_calls: a nest starts past its file's last line"
				}
				{ path: file.path, nest, source_line }
			},
		)
	}
}

# ── The verdict

## `find_deep_calls (Roc): 9 files; nested 14 (min 3, strict); depth 3 11,
## depth 4 3`: the files, the findings, the rule, and how many at each depth,
## the depths in the order of their text, as the Shale original sorted them.
summary : List(NestFinding), { file_count : U64, settings : Settings } -> Str
summary = |findings, { file_count, settings }| {
	rule = settings.rule
	strictness = match rule.strictness {
		Strict => "strict"
		Loose => "loose"
	}
	counted = "nested ${findings.len().to_str()} (min ${rule.min.to_str()}, ${strictness})"
	depths = findings.map(|finding| finding.nest.depth.to_str())
	by_depth = distinct(depths).sort_with(Text.byte_order).map(
		|depth| "depth ${depth} ${depths.count_if(|d| d == depth).to_str()}",
	)
	counts = if by_depth.is_empty() {
		""
	} else {
		"; ${Str.join_with(by_depth, ", ")}"
	}
	house_note = match settings.house {
		Kept => ""
		LeftOut => "; left out as house style: nested"
	}
	"find_deep_calls (Roc): ${file_count.to_str()} files; ${counted}${counts}${house_note}"
}

distinct : List(Str) -> List(Str)
distinct = |texts|
	texts.fold(
		[],
		|seen, text|
			if seen.contains(text) {
				seen
			} else {
				seen.append(text)
			},
	)

## The summary, each finding, then the summary again (cookbook/findings.shale):
## the first copy survives a cut output, and a gate reads the last line.
print_findings! : Str, List(Str) => {}
print_findings! = |summary_line, finding_lines| {
	Shale.print!(summary_line)
	if !(finding_lines.is_empty()) {
		for line in finding_lines {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
		Shale.print!(summary_line)
	}
}

cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls/NestFinding.roc, 27 lines

## A finding: one nest of calls in a file, and the source line its outermost
## call starts on, printed as
## `path:line:column: nested: depth N, <outermost> to <deepest>: <line>`.
import Nest
import lib.Text

NestFinding := {
	path : Str,
	nest : Nest,
	source_line : Str,
}.{

	## The finding up to its source line: where it is, how deep, and which
	## calls it runs between. The self-test reads this part.
	head : NestFinding -> Str
	head = |finding| {
		nest = finding.nest
		place = "${finding.path}:${nest.line.to_str()}:${nest.column.to_str()}"
		span = "${nest.outermost} to ${nest.deepest}"
		"${place}: nested: depth ${nest.depth.to_str()}, ${span}"
	}

	## The finding's whole line, its source line trimmed.
	finding_line : NestFinding -> Str
	finding_line = |finding|
		"${NestFinding.head(finding)}: ${Text.trim(finding.source_line)}"
}

cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls/Nest.roc, 253 lines

## A nest of calls: the outermost call of calls nested in each other's
## arguments, like `f(g(h(x)))`, with its depth and the names of its
## outermost and deepest calls. `Nest.nests_in` finds a file's nests from
## Roc's tree of it; the launcher's header says the rule.
import lib.Tree

Nest := {
	line : U64,
	column : U64,
	depth : U64,
	outermost : Str,
	deepest : Str,
}.{

	## Whether a record, a list or a tuple argument starts the depth again
	## (`Strict`, the default) or passes its parts' depth through (`Loose`).
	Strictness : [Strict, Loose]

	## What to report: nests at least `min` deep, judged as `strictness` says.
	Rule : { min : I64, strictness : Nest.Strictness }

	## The file's nests at least the rule's `min` deep, in source order, each
	## named by its outermost call.
	nests_in : List(Tree.Node), Nest.Rule -> List(Nest)
	nests_in = |syntax_nodes, rule| {
		reading = {
			syntax_nodes,
			depths: call_depths(syntax_nodes, rule.strictness),
			strictness: rule.strictness,
		}
		var $nests = []
		var $place = 1
		while $place <= syntax_nodes.len() {
			is_deep_enough = depth_at(reading, $place).to_i64_wrap() >= rule.min
			is_nest = is_call(Tree.node_at(syntax_nodes, $place)) and is_outermost(reading, $place)
			if is_deep_enough and is_nest {
				$nests = $nests.append(nest_at(reading, $place))
			}
			$place = $place + 1
		}
		$nests
	}
}

## A tree read for nests: each node's call depth beside it, by place.
Reading : {
	syntax_nodes : List(Tree.Node),
	depths : List(U64),
	strictness : Nest.Strictness,
}

nest_at : Reading, U64 -> Nest
nest_at = |reading, place| {
	node = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, place)
	{
		line: node.line,
		column: node.col,
		depth: depth_at(reading, place),
		outermost: call_name(reading.syntax_nodes, place),
		deepest: call_name(reading.syntax_nodes, deepest_call(reading, place)),
	}
}

# ── Depth

## The node kinds that pass their parts' depth through: what reads left to
## right, a wrapper, an operator, an access, a string's interpolation. `unary`
## is `!x` or `-x`, `receiver` holds the value whose method is called, and
## `mapper` is the right side of `x |> f`.
pass_through_kinds : List(Str)
pass_through_kinds = [
	"e-arrow-call",
	"e-question-suffix",
	"e-nominal-apply",
	"mapper",
	"e-binop",
	"unary",
	"e-field-access",
	"e-tuple-access",
	"receiver",
	"e-string",
]

## The kinds that pass their parts' depth through only when the rule is
## `Loose`.
loose_pass_through_kinds : List(Str)
loose_pass_through_kinds = ["e-record", "e-list", "e-tuple", "field"]

passes_depth_through : Str, Nest.Strictness -> Bool
passes_depth_through = |kind, strictness|
	match strictness {
		Strict => pass_through_kinds.contains(kind)
		Loose => pass_through_kinds.contains(kind) or loose_pass_through_kinds.contains(kind)
	}

is_call : Tree.Node -> Bool
is_call = |node| node.kind == "e-apply" or node.kind == "e-method-call"

## Every node's call depth, by place. A node's depth is its kids', so the
## places are taken from the last, whose kids come after them all.
call_depths : List(Tree.Node), Nest.Strictness -> List(U64)
call_depths = |syntax_nodes, strictness| {
	var $depths = List.repeat(0, syntax_nodes.len())
	var $place = syntax_nodes.len()
	while $place > 0 {
		depth = depth_from_kids({ syntax_nodes, depths: $depths, strictness }, $place)
		$depths = $depths.set(
			$place - 1,
			depth,
		) ?? crash "find_deep_calls: a place past the last node"
		$place = $place - 1
	}
	$depths
}

## A node's call depth from its kids' depths, which `reading` already has.
## A call is one more than its deepest argument; a method call is at least
## as deep as its receiver, which reads left to right; a tag's payload, as
## in `Ok(...)`, adds no level; what passes depth through, and a one-item
## tuple, which is a pair of parentheses, is as deep as its deepest part;
## anything else (a lambda, a record) starts again at zero.
depth_from_kids : Reading, U64 -> U64
depth_from_kids = |reading, place| {
	node = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, place)
	if node.kind == "e-apply" {
		deepest_argument = deepest_of(reading, node.kids.drop_first(1))
		function = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, Tree.first_kid(node))
		if function.kind == "e-tag" {
			deepest_argument
		} else {
			1 + deepest_argument
		}
	} else if node.kind == "e-method-call" {
		method_call_depth(reading, node)
	} else if passes_depth_through(node.kind, reading.strictness) or is_parenthesized(node) {
		deepest_of(reading, node.kids)
	} else {
		0
	}
}

method_call_depth : Reading, Tree.Node -> U64
method_call_depth = |reading, node| {
	var $receiver_depth = 0
	var $deepest_argument = 0
	for kid in node.kids {
		part = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, kid)
		if part.kind == "receiver" {
			$receiver_depth = depth_at(reading, Tree.first_kid(part))
		}
		if part.kind == "args" {
			$deepest_argument = U64.max($deepest_argument, deepest_of(reading, part.kids))
		}
	}
	U64.max(1 + $deepest_argument, $receiver_depth)
}

## A tuple of one item, which is a pair of parentheses.
is_parenthesized : Tree.Node -> Bool
is_parenthesized = |node| node.kind == "e-tuple" and node.kids.len() == 1

deepest_of : Reading, List(U64) -> U64
deepest_of = |reading, places|
	places.fold(0, |deepest, place| U64.max(deepest, depth_at(reading, place)))

depth_at : Reading, U64 -> U64
depth_at = |reading, place|
	match reading.depths.get(place - 1) {
		Ok(depth) => depth
		Err(_) => crash "find_deep_calls: no depth for node ${place.to_str()}"
	}

# ── The nest around a call

## Whether a call nested under this node still belongs to the nest of the
## call above it.
continues_nest : Tree.Node, Nest.Strictness -> Bool
continues_nest = |node, strictness| {
	is_part = node.kind == "args" or node.kind == "e-tuple"
	is_call(node) or is_part or passes_depth_through(node.kind, strictness)
}

## Whether the call at `place` is the outermost of its nest: the first call
## above it, through nodes that continue the nest, is not as deep.
is_outermost : Reading, U64 -> Bool
is_outermost = |reading, place| {
	depth = depth_at(reading, place)
	var $above = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, place).parent
	while $above > 0 {
		node = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, $above)
		if is_call(node) {
			return depth_at(reading, $above) < depth
		}
		if !(continues_nest(node, reading.strictness)) {
			return Bool.True
		}
		$above = node.parent
	}
	Bool.True
}

## Whether the call at `place` is inside the nest of the call at `top`:
## every node between them continues the nest.
is_in_nest : Reading, { top : U64, place : U64 } -> Bool
is_in_nest = |reading, { top, place }| {
	var $above = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, place).parent
	while $above > 0 and $above != top {
		node = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, $above)
		if !(continues_nest(node, reading.strictness)) {
			return Bool.False
		}
		$above = node.parent
	}
	$above == top
}

## The deepest call of the nest under the call at `top`: the first call of
## depth 1 inside it, in source order, or `top` itself when it has none.
## The nodes inside it are those after it that are deeper in the tree.
deepest_call : Reading, U64 -> U64
deepest_call = |reading, top| {
	top_depth = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, top).depth
	is_inside = |place| Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, place).depth > top_depth
	var $place = top + 1
	while $place <= reading.syntax_nodes.len() and is_inside($place) {
		node = Tree.node_at(reading.syntax_nodes, $place)
		is_deepest = is_call(node) and depth_at(reading, $place) == 1
		if is_deepest and is_in_nest(reading, { top, place: $place }) {
			return $place
		}
		$place = $place + 1
	}
	top
}

## A call's name: an apply's function as written (`List.concat`, else its
## name, else its kind), or a method call's method (`.concat`).
call_name : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Str
call_name = |syntax_nodes, place| {
	node = Tree.node_at(syntax_nodes, place)
	if node.kind == "e-method-call" {
		match Tree.find_attribute(node, "method") {
			Ok(method) => method
			Err(_) => crash "find_deep_calls: a method call with no method"
		}
	} else {
		function = Tree.node_at(syntax_nodes, Tree.first_kid(node))
		match Tree.find_attribute(function, "raw") {
			Ok(raw) => raw
			Err(_) => Tree.find_attribute(function, "name") ?? function.kind
		}
	}
}

## The recipe's self-test: the plants in cookbook/roc/plants/find_deep_calls/,
## checked at `min=3` against the marks they carry. A line ending
## `# depth N` must give one finding of depth N, and one ending
## `# depth N, M` a finding for each, left to right; an added `from A to B`
## means the line's first finding must say `A to B`. No unmarked line may
## give a finding, no two findings may print the same line, and a
## `quiet_*.roc` plant may hold no mark.
import pf.Shale
import NestFinding

SelfTest := [].{

	## Where the plants are.
	plants : Str
	plants = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_deep_calls/"

	## Each plant's marks held to the findings the run printed: every fault
	## said, then a stop, or the PASS line.
	run! : { paths : List(Str), findings : List(NestFinding) } => {}
	run! = |{ paths, findings }| {
		var $faults = []
		var $mark_count = 0
		for path in paths {
			text = match Shale.read!(path) {
				Found(found) => found
				Missing => {
					Shale.fail!("find_deep_calls self_test: ${path} went missing")
					""
				}
			}
			var $number = 1
			for line in text.split_on("\n") {
				mark = read_mark!(line)
				if mark != Unmarked {
					$mark_count = $mark_count + 1
				}
				judged = {
					place: "${path}:${$number.to_str()}",
					path,
					mark,
					line_findings: findings_at_line(findings, { path, line: $number }),
				}
				$faults = $faults.concat(line_faults(judged))
				$number = $number + 1
			}
		}
		$faults = $faults.concat(duplicate_line_faults(findings))
		if $mark_count == 0 {
			$faults = $faults.append("no plant holds a `# depth` mark")
		}
		for fault in $faults {
			Shale.print!("FAIL ${fault}")
		}
		if !($faults.is_empty()) {
			Shale.fail!("find_deep_calls self_test: ${$faults.len().to_str()} plants wrong")
		}
		marks = "each marked line gives its depths left to right, the outermost only"
		others = "no other line a finding, and no two findings print alike"
		Shale.print!("find_deep_calls (Roc) self_test: PASS (${marks}, ${others})")
	}
}

## A line's mark: the depths it wants, as written (`3, 4`), and the
## outermost and deepest calls its first finding must name, if it says.
Mark : [Marked({ depths : Str, span : [Says(Str), Silent] }), Unmarked]

read_mark! : Str => Mark
read_mark! = |line| {
	depths = "([0-9]+(?:, [0-9]+)*)"
	span = "(?: from ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+) to ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+))?"
	match Shale.re_find!(line, "# depth ${depths}${span}$") {
		Found(found) =>
			match found.groups {
				[wanted, outermost, deepest] if outermost != "" =>
					Marked({ depths: wanted, span: Says("${outermost} to ${deepest}") })
				[wanted, ..] => Marked({ depths: wanted, span: Silent })
				[] => crash "find_deep_calls: a mark matched with no groups"
			}
		NoMatch => Unmarked
	}
}

## The findings on one line of a plant, left to right.
findings_at_line : List(NestFinding), { path : Str, line : U64 } -> List(NestFinding)
findings_at_line = |findings, { path, line }|
	findings
		.keep_if(|finding| finding.path == path and finding.nest.line == line)
		.sort_by(|finding| finding.nest.column)

## A plant's line to judge: where it is, its mark and its findings.
JudgedLine : {
	place : Str,
	path : Str,
	mark : Mark,
	line_findings : List(NestFinding),
}

## What is wrong with one line: its findings against its mark.
line_faults : JudgedLine -> List(Str)
line_faults = |{ place, path, mark, line_findings }| {
	got = Str.join_with(line_findings.map(|finding| finding.nest.depth.to_str()), ", ")
	match mark {
		Marked({ depths, span }) => {
			quiet_fault =
				if path.drop_prefix(SelfTest.plants).starts_with("quiet_") {
					["${place}: a quiet plant holds a `# depth` mark"]
				} else {
					[]
				}
			span_fault =
				match span {
					Says(says) =>
						match line_findings.first() {
							Ok(first) if NestFinding.head(first).contains(says) => []
							_ => ["${place}: the finding does not say `${says}`"]
						}
					Silent => []
				}
			depth_fault =
				if line_findings.is_empty() {
					["${place}: no finding, want depth ${depths}"]
				} else if got != depths {
					["${place}: depth ${got}, want ${depths}"]
				} else {
					[]
				}
			quiet_fault.concat(span_fault).concat(depth_fault)
		}
		Unmarked =>
			if line_findings.is_empty() {
				[]
			} else {
				["${place}: a finding (depth ${got}) on a line not marked for one"]
			}
	}
}

## A fault for each line that two findings print alike.
duplicate_line_faults : List(NestFinding) -> List(Str)
duplicate_line_faults = |findings| {
	finding_lines = findings.map(NestFinding.finding_line)
	is_printed_twice = |line| finding_lines.count_if(|other| other == line) > 1
	once_each = |seen, line| {
		if seen.contains(line) {
			seen
		} else {
			seen.append(line)
		}
	}
	finding_lines
		.keep_if(is_printed_twice)
		.fold([], once_each)
		.map(|line| "two findings print the same line, ${line}")
}

-- This recipe finds calls nested three or more deep, like `f(g(h(x)))`, in
-- every .roc file of a tree. Such a call has to be read from the inside
-- out. The Roc style guide (roc-apps docs/roc-style.md) asks for code that
-- reads left to right instead: a method chain, a pipe, or a named middle
-- step. The recipe reads each file's syntax tree from Roc's own parser
-- (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale).
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/find_deep_calls.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc min=4
--   shale cookbook:roc/find_deep_calls.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob   the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default;
--   min    the least depth to report, 3 by default;
--   house  with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style
--          (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code;
--   loose  with `loose=1`, a record, list or tuple argument does not reset
--          the depth.
--
-- A call's depth is one more than the deepest call among its arguments.
-- Some things pass their parts' depth through without adding a level:
-- whatever reads left to right (a method's receiver in `a.f().g()`, the
-- left side of `x |> f` and `x->f()`), a tag or nominal wrapper
-- (`Ok(...)`, `ChatPath.(...)`), `?`, parentheses, operators, field or
-- tuple access, and a string's interpolation. So `f(g(h(x) + 1))`,
-- `f(!g(h(x)))`, `f(g(h(x).a))` and `f("${g(h(x))}")` are each three deep. A lambda argument starts again at zero, since its body
-- is read on its own, and so does a record, list or tuple argument, whose
-- parts have names or places, unless `loose=1`.
--
-- Each finding is the outermost call of one nest:
--   path:line:column: nested: depth N, <outermost> to <deepest>: <source line>
-- The column tells apart two nests on one line. The outermost and deepest
-- calls are named (`List.concat to Str.to_utf8`, or `.concat` for a method)
-- so that a nest spread over several lines says more than its first line.
-- The output is the count by depth, the findings, and the count again
-- (cookbook/findings.shale). Files that don't parse are listed after
-- the findings, and then the run fails.
--
-- `self_test=1` checks the plants in `cookbook/roc/plants/find_deep_calls/` at
-- `min=3`. A plant line ending `# depth N` must give one finding of depth
-- N, and one ending `# depth N, M` a finding for each, left to right; an
-- added `from A to B` means the finding must say `A to B`. No unmarked line
-- may give a finding, no two findings may print the same line, and a
-- `quiet_*.roc` plant may hold no mark.
-- budget: steps=100000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/find_deep_calls/"
const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const LOOSE = arg("loose", "") == "1"
const MIN = SELF_TEST and 3 or arg("min", 3)
use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./house.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")

-- The node kinds that pass their parts' depth through. `unary` is `!x` or
-- `-x`, `receiver` holds the value whose method is called, and an `e-string`
-- holds its interpolations' code.
const PASS_THROUGH = {["e-arrow-call"] = true, ["e-question-suffix"] = true, ["e-nominal-apply"] = true, mapper = true, ["e-binop"] = true, unary = true, ["e-field-access"] = true, ["e-tuple-access"] = true, receiver = true, ["e-string"] = true}
const LOOSE_PASS_THROUGH = {["e-record"] = true, ["e-list"] = true, ["e-tuple"] = true, field = true}

function passes_depth_through(kind, loose)
  return has_key(PASS_THROUGH, kind) or (loose and has_key(LOOSE_PASS_THROUGH, kind))
end

function is_call(node)
  return node.kind == "e-apply" or node.kind == "e-method-call"
end

-- Whether a call nested under a node of this kind still belongs to the
-- same nest as the call above it.
function continues_nest(node, loose)
  local kind = node.kind
  return is_call(node) or kind == "args" or kind == "receiver" or kind == "e-tuple" or passes_depth_through(kind, loose)
end

-- The call depth of node `i`, cached in `memo`, where -1 means not yet
-- computed.
function call_depth(nodes, memo, i, loose)
  if memo[i] >= 0 then return memo[i] end
  local node = nodes[i]
  local kind = node.kind
  local depth = 0
  if kind == "e-apply" then
    -- The first kid is the function called, the rest its arguments.
    local deepest_argument = 0
    for argument in drop(node.kids, 1) do
      deepest_argument = max(deepest_argument, call_depth(nodes, memo, argument, loose))
    end
    -- A tag's payload, as in `Ok(...)`, is no call.
    if nodes[node.kids[1]].kind == "e-tag" then depth = deepest_argument else depth = 1 + deepest_argument end
  elseif kind == "e-method-call" then
    local receiver_depth = 0
    local deepest_argument = 0
    for kid in node.kids do
      if nodes[kid].kind == "receiver" then receiver_depth = call_depth(nodes, memo, nodes[kid].kids[1], loose) end
      if nodes[kid].kind == "args" then
        for argument in nodes[kid].kids do
          deepest_argument = max(deepest_argument, call_depth(nodes, memo, argument, loose))
        end
      end
    end
    depth = max(1 + deepest_argument, receiver_depth)
  elseif passes_depth_through(kind, loose) or (kind == "e-tuple" and #node.kids == 1) then
    -- A one-item tuple is a pair of parentheses.
    for kid in node.kids do
      depth = max(depth, call_depth(nodes, memo, kid, loose))
    end
  end
  memo[i] = depth
  return depth
end

-- Whether the call at `i` is the outermost of its nest: the first call
-- above it, through nodes that continue the nest, is not as deep.
function is_outermost(nodes, memo, i, loose)
  local p = nodes[i].parent
  while p > 0 do
    if is_call(nodes[p]) then return call_depth(nodes, memo, p, loose) < call_depth(nodes, memo, i, loose) end
    if not continues_nest(nodes[p], loose) then return true end
    p = nodes[p].parent
  end
  return true
end

-- A call's name: an apply's function (`List.concat`), or a method call's
-- method (`.concat`).
function call_name(nodes, i)
  local node = nodes[i]
  if node.kind == "e-method-call" then return get(node, "method", "?") end
  local head = nodes[node.kids[1]]
  return get(head, "raw", get(head, "name", head.kind))
end

-- Whether the call at `j` is inside the nest of the call at `top`: every
-- node between them continues the nest.
function is_in_nest(nodes, top, j, loose)
  local p = nodes[j].parent
  while p > 0 and p ~= top do
    if not continues_nest(nodes[p], loose) then return false end
    p = nodes[p].parent
  end
  return p == top
end

-- The deepest call of the nest under the call at `top`: the first call of
-- depth 1 inside it, in source order.
function deepest_call(nodes, memo, top, loose)
  local j = top + 1
  while j <= #nodes and nodes[j].depth > nodes[top].depth do
    if is_call(nodes[j]) and call_depth(nodes, memo, j, loose) == 1 and is_in_nest(nodes, top, j, loose) then return j end
    j = j + 1
  end
  return top
end

const paths = glob(GLOB)
local finding_count = 0
local count_by_depth = {}
local finding_lines = {}
-- For the self-test: each line's findings, `path:line` to a list of
-- `{col, depth, text}`, and how many times each finding line printed.
const findings_at_line = {}
const times_printed = {}
local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths)
for f in parsed.files do
  local nodes = f.nodes
  local memo = {}
  for n in nodes do push(memo, -1) end
  local source_lines = {}
  for i = 1, #nodes do
    if is_call(nodes[i]) and call_depth(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) >= MIN and is_outermost(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE) then
      if #source_lines == 0 then source_lines = split(read(f.path), "\n") end
      local line = nodes[i].line
      local depth = call_depth(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE)
      local span = call_name(nodes, i) .. " to " .. call_name(nodes, deepest_call(nodes, memo, i, LOOSE))
      local head = f.path .. ":" .. line .. ":" .. nodes[i].col .. ": nested: depth " .. depth .. ", " .. span
      local finding = head .. ": " .. trim(source_lines[line])
      if not house_leaves_out("find_deep_calls", "nested") then
        push(finding_lines, finding)
        incr(times_printed, finding)
        count_by_depth[tostring(depth)] = get(count_by_depth, tostring(depth), 0) + 1
        push_at(findings_at_line, f.path .. ":" .. line, {col = nodes[i].col, depth = depth, text = head})
        finding_count = finding_count + 1
      end
    end
  end
end
local counts = {}
for depth in sort(keys(count_by_depth)) do push(counts, "depth " .. depth .. " " .. count_by_depth[depth]) end
print_findings("find_deep_calls (Roc): " .. #paths .. " files; nested " .. finding_count .. " (min " .. MIN .. ", " .. (LOOSE and "loose" or "strict") .. ")" .. (#counts > 0 and ("; " .. join(counts, ", ")) or "") .. house_note("find_deep_calls"), finding_lines)
fail_if_refused("find_deep_calls", parsed.refused)
if SELF_TEST then
  local wrong = {}
  local marks = 0
  for p in paths do
    local n = 0
    for l in lines(read(p)) do
      n = n + 1
      local mark = re_find(l, "# depth ([0-9]+(?:, [0-9]+)*)(?: from ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+) to ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+))?$")
      local key = p .. ":" .. n
      local got = {}
      local texts = {}
      if has_key(findings_at_line, key) then
        for g in sort(findings_at_line[key], "col") do
          push(got, tostring(g.depth))
          push(texts, g.text)
        end
      end
      if mark ~= nil then
        marks = marks + 1
        if starts_with(sub(p, #PLANTS + 1), "quiet_") then push(wrong, key .. ": a quiet plant holds a `# depth` mark") end
        local want = mark.groups[1]
        local outermost_name = get(mark.groups, 2, "")
        if outermost_name ~= nil and outermost_name ~= "" then
          local says = outermost_name .. " to " .. mark.groups[3]
          if #texts == 0 or not contains(texts[1], says) then push(wrong, key .. ": the finding does not say `" .. says .. "`") end
        end
        if #got == 0 then push(wrong, key .. ": no finding, want depth " .. want)
        elseif join(got, ", ") ~= want then push(wrong, key .. ": depth " .. join(got, ", ") .. ", want " .. want) end
      elseif #got > 0 then
        push(wrong, key .. ": a finding (depth " .. join(got, ", ") .. ") on a line not marked for one")
      end
    end
  end
  for l in keys(times_printed) do
    if times_printed[l] > 1 then push(wrong, "two findings print the same line, " .. l) end
  end
  if marks == 0 then push(wrong, "no plant holds a `# depth` mark") end
  for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end
  if #wrong > 0 then fail("find_deep_calls self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end
  print("find_deep_calls (Roc) self_test: PASS (each marked line gives its depths left to right, the outermost only, no other line a finding, and no two findings print alike)")
end
