## The recipe, as its refusals name it.
who : Str
who = "hunt_names"

## The run stopped, saying why; the text is never used.
stop! : Str => Str
stop! = |why| {
	Shale.fail!(why)
	""
}

read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => stop!("${who}: no ${path}")
	}

## The pin every recipe's self-test runs, from cookbook/roc/pinned.shale's
## `SELF_TEST_PIN`, its one home.
self_test_pin! : {} => Str
self_test_pin! = |{}| {
	pinned = read_text!("cookbook:roc/pinned.shale")
	match Shale.re_find!(pinned, "\nconst SELF_TEST_PIN = \"([^\"]+)\"") {
		Found(matched) => matched.groups.first() ?? ""
		NoMatch => stop!("${who}: cookbook/roc/pinned.shale names no SELF_TEST_PIN")
	}
}

## The modules roc-types reports for the app `root`, built with the Roc at
## `roc`, or a stop: roc-types missing, of another format, built for another
## Roc, or refusing the app.
modules_of! : Str, Str => RocTypes.Modules
modules_of! = |root, roc| {
	exe = checker_for!(roc)
	if !(Shale.exists!(exe)) {
		Shale.fail!("`roc_types`: no ${exe}: ${RocTypes.install_hint}")
	}
	ran = Shale.run!({
		argv: [Shale.real!(exe), Shale.real!(root)],
		keep: Whole(64000000),
		timeout_ms: 300000,
		want: "",
	})
	output_lines = Text.lines(ran.out)
	pin = match RocTypes.pin_of(output_lines, root) {
		Ok(found) => found
		Err(why) => stop!(why)
	}
	own = "tools:roc-${pin}/roc"
	if !(Shale.exists!(own)) or Shale.real!(own) != roc {
		another = "its types would be another compiler's. Install the roc-types of the tree's pin (https://github.com/showell/roc-types), or move the tree to ${pin}"
		Shale.fail!("`roc_types`: roc-types reads Roc ${pin}, and ${root}'s tree is built with ${roc}: ${another}")
	}
	if ran.code != 0 {
		ended = if ran.code < 0 {
			"did not exit"
		} else {
			"exited ${ran.code.to_str()}"
		}
		Shale.fail!("`roc_types`: roc-types ${root} ${ended}, what it said:\n${RocTypes.said_on_failure(output_lines)}")
	}
	match RocTypes.modules_of(output_lines) {
		Ok(modules) => modules
		Err(why) => {
			Shale.fail!(why)
			{ paths: [], records: Dict.empty(), warnings: [] }
		}
	}
}

## The checker for the compiler at `roc`: the one installed for its pin,
## `tools:roc-types-<pin>/bin/roc-types`, as compilers sit side by side, or
## else the default.
checker_for! : Str => Str
checker_for! = |roc| {
	default = "tools:roc-types/bin/roc-types"
	match Shale.re_find!(roc, "/roc-([^/]+)/roc$") {
		Found(matched) => {
			own = "tools:roc-types-${matched.groups.first() ?? ""}/bin/roc-types"
			if Shale.exists!(own) {
				own
			} else {
				default
			}
		}
		NoMatch => default
	}
}

cookbook/roc/hunt_names/Words.roc, 222 lines

## The word lists hunt_names judges names by, read from their one home each:
## cookbook/words/ (verbs, participles, the vague and container words,
## prepositions, namespaces, Roc's own words and the numbers, list names,
## world verbs, cited sources), a project's `terms=` file, the house style's
## checks from cookbook/roc/house.shale and the methods Roc calls by name
## from cookbook/roc/headers.shale. Each refusal is worded as
## cookbook/roc/declared.shale's readers word it.
import pf.Shale
import lib.Text

Words := [].{

	## A project's terms: each term's element type (`""` for none) and its
	## words, by the term.
	Terms : {
		lists : Dict(Str, Str),
		words : Dict(Str, List(Str)),
	}

	## Every table the checks read.
	Lists : {
		verbs : Set(Str),
		participles : Set(Str),
		ed_verbs : Set(Str),
		vague : Set(Str),
		containers : Set(Str),
		prepositions : Set(Str),
		world_verbs : Set(Str),
		namespaces : Dict(Str, Set(Str)),
		taken : Dict(Str, Str),
		list_names : Dict(Str, Str),
		terms : Words.Terms,
		fixed_names : Set(Str),
	}

	## The tables, read in the Shale original's order, and the verbs held to
	## reading as no participle. `terms_file` is `""` for none.
	read! : Str => Words.Lists
	read! = |terms_file| {
		verbs = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/verbs.txt")
		participles = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/participles.txt")
		ed_verbs = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/ed_verbs.txt")
		vague = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/vague.txt")
		containers = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/containers.txt")
		prepositions = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/prepositions.txt")
		namespaces = namespace_instructions!("namespaces.txt")
		taken = taken_word_kinds!("taken.txt")
		list_names = list_name_kinds!("list_names.txt")
		world_verbs = Words.word_set!("cookbook:words/world_verbs.txt")
		terms = project_terms!(terms_file)
		for word in word_list_lines!("cookbook:words/verbs.txt") {
			if Words.reads_as_participle(word, participles, ed_verbs) {
				Shale.fail!("hunt_names: `${word}` is in cookbook/words/verbs.txt and reads as a participle, which would make its effects states")
			}
		}
		fixed_names = language_fixed_names!({})
		{ verbs, participles, ed_verbs, vague, containers, prepositions, world_verbs, namespaces, taken, list_names, terms, fixed_names }
	}

	## A list of one word a line, as a set. A word listed twice, or a line of
	## two words, stops the run.
	word_set! : Str => Set(Str)
	word_set! = |path| {
		if !(Shale.exists!(path)) {
			Shale.fail!("no word list ${path}")
		}
		var $set = Set.empty()
		for word in word_list_lines!(path) {
			if word.contains(" ") or $set.contains(word) {
				Shale.fail!("${path}: `${word}` is no single new word")
			}
			if word != "" {
				$set = $set.insert(word)
			}
		}
		$set
	}

	## Whether a word reads as a past participle: an irregular one of
	## participles.txt, or a word past three letters ending in `ed` that
	## ed_verbs.txt doesn't list.
	reads_as_participle : Str, Set(Str), Set(Str) -> Bool
	reads_as_participle = |word, participles, ed_verbs|
		if participles.contains(word) {
			Bool.True
		} else {
			word.count_utf8_bytes() > 3 and word.ends_with("ed") and !(ed_verbs.contains(word))
		}

	## The checks cookbook/roc/house.shale names as our house style for
	## hunt_names, its one home.
	house_style! : {} => List(Str)
	house_style! = |{}| {
		text = read_text!("cookbook:roc/house.shale")
		match Shale.re_find!(text, "\n  hunt_names = \\{([^}]*)\\}") {
			Found(matched) => Shale.re_find_all!(matched.groups.first() ?? "", "\"([^\"]+)\"").map(|quoted| quoted.groups.first() ?? "")
			NoMatch => {
				Shale.fail!("hunt_names: cookbook/roc/house.shale's HOUSE_CHECKS names no hunt_names")
				[]
			}
		}
	}
}

## A file's text, or a stop naming it.
read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("no word list ${path}")
			""
		}
	}

## The lines of a word list, any note after `--` cut off, trimmed.
word_list_lines! : Str => List(Str)
word_list_lines! = |path| Text.lines(read_text!(path)).map(|line| Text.trim(Text.before_first(line, "--")))

## namespaces.txt: a prefix a line, then the namespace's own instructions
## (`port in out`), as the set of each prefix's instructions.
namespace_instructions! : Str => Dict(Str, Set(Str))
namespace_instructions! = |file| {
	var $by_prefix = Dict.empty()
	for line in word_list_lines!("cookbook:words/${file}") {
		match Text.words(line) {
			[prefix, .. as instructions] => {
				if $by_prefix.contains(prefix) {
					Shale.fail!("hunt_names: cookbook/words/${file}: `${prefix}` twice")
				}
				$by_prefix = $by_prefix.insert(prefix, Set.from_list(instructions))
			}
			[] => {}
		}
	}
	$by_prefix
}

## taken.txt: a word a line, then its kind, `roc` or `cardinal`.
taken_word_kinds! : Str => Dict(Str, Str)
taken_word_kinds! = |file| {
	var $kinds = Dict.empty()
	for line in word_list_lines!("cookbook:words/${file}") {
		said = Text.words(line)
		if !(said.is_empty()) {
			match said {
				[word, kind] if (kind == "roc" or kind == "cardinal") and !($kinds.contains(word)) => {
					$kinds = $kinds.insert(word, kind)
				}
				_ => Shale.fail!("hunt_names: cookbook/words/${file}: `${Str.join_with(said, " ")}` is no new word with its kind, `roc` or `cardinal`")
			}
		}
	}
	$kinds
}

## list_names.txt: a word a line, then its kind, `many`, `one`, `after`,
## `accumulator` or `adjective`.
list_name_kinds! : Str => Dict(Str, Str)
list_name_kinds! = |file| {
	known_kinds = ["many", "one", "after", "accumulator", "adjective"]
	var $kinds = Dict.empty()
	for line in word_list_lines!("cookbook:words/${file}") {
		said = Text.words(line)
		if !(said.is_empty()) {
			match said {
				[word, kind] if known_kinds.contains(kind) and !($kinds.contains(word)) => {
					$kinds = $kinds.insert(word, kind)
				}
				_ => Shale.fail!("hunt_names: cookbook/words/${file}: `${Str.join_with(said, " ")}` is no new word with its kind, `many`, `one`, `after`, `accumulator` or `adjective`")
			}
		}
	}
	$kinds
}

## A project's own terms, none for `""`: a term a line, its words joined by
## `_`, then after a `:` the element type of the list it names.
project_terms! : Str => Words.Terms
project_terms! = |path| {
	var $terms = { lists: Dict.empty(), words: Dict.empty() }
	if path == "" {
		return $terms
	}
	if !(Shale.exists!(path)) {
		Shale.fail!("hunt_names: terms=${path}: no such file")
	}
	for line in word_list_lines!(path) {
		if line != "" {
			parts = line.split_on(":")
			term = Text.trim(parts.first() ?? "")
			element = Text.trim(parts.get(1) ?? "")
			is_bad_element = element != "" and !(Shale.re_match!(element, "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$"))
			is_bad_term = !(Shale.re_match!(term, "^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$"))
			if parts.len() > 2 or is_bad_term or is_bad_element or $terms.lists.contains(term) {
				Shale.fail!("hunt_names: ${path}: `${line}` is no new term, `word` or `word: Type`")
			}
			$terms = {
				lists: $terms.lists.insert(term, element),
				words: $terms.words.insert(term, term.split_on("_")),
			}
		}
	}
	$terms
}

## The methods Roc calls by name, from their one home,
## cookbook/roc/headers.shale's LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES.
language_fixed_names! : {} => Set(Str)
language_fixed_names! = |{}| {
	text = read_text!("cookbook:roc/headers.shale")
	match Shale.re_find!(text, "\nconst LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES = \\{([^\n]*)\\}\n") {
		Found(matched) => {
			entries = Shale.re_find_all!(matched.groups.first() ?? "", "([a-z_!]+)\"?\\]? = true")
			Set.from_list(entries.map(|entry| entry.groups.first() ?? ""))
		}
		NoMatch => {
			Shale.fail!("hunt_names: cookbook/roc/headers.shale names no LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES")
			Set.empty()
		}
	}
}

cookbook/roc/hunt_names/TypeText.roc, 307 lines

## What hunt_names reads of a type, in the tree or written as text
## (cookbook/roc/declared.shale's readers, and types.shale's
## `roc_type_parts`): a tag union's tags, an argument's shape, the types an
## annotation mentions, a function type's parts, a `Try`'s success and a
## list's element, a tag's first word and words joined as a type's name; and
## where a node sits: its source text, the sibling before it, and whether a
## definition calls itself.
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree

TypeText := [].{

	## A tag union's tag names (`Unpinned` for `Unpinned(Str)` too), and
	## whether any tag carries a payload.
	Union : { names : List(Str), has_payload : Bool }

	## An argument's type as `command_tense` and `mixed_tense` need it: a tag
	## union written in place, a named type by its last part, or neither; and
	## whether it was a `List` of that.
	ArgumentShape : {
		shape : [Written(TypeText.Union), Named(Str), Unread],
		is_list : Bool,
	}

	## A function type's parts as text: whether the type is a function, the
	## text before its arrow and the text after it, its whole text when it is
	## no function.
	Parts : { is_function : Bool, arguments : Str, result : Str }

	## The tags of the tag union at `at`.
	union_shape : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> TypeText.Union
	union_shape = |nodes, at| {
		var $names = []
		var $has_payload = Bool.False
		for part in Tree.node_at(nodes, at).kids {
			part_node = Tree.node_at(nodes, part)
			if part_node.kind == "tags" {
				for tag in part_node.kids {
					tag_node = Tree.node_at(nodes, tag)
					name = if tag_node.kind == "ty-apply" {
						$has_payload = Bool.True
						Tree.attribute(Tree.node_at(nodes, Tree.first_kid(tag_node)), "name")
					} else {
						Tree.attribute(tag_node, "name")
					}
					if name != "" {
						$names = $names.append(name)
					}
				}
			}
		}
		{ names: $names, has_payload: $has_payload }
	}

	## The shape of the argument type at `at`; a `List(T)` gives `T`'s.
	argument_shape : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> TypeText.ArgumentShape
	argument_shape = |nodes, at| {
		node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
		unread = { shape: Unread, is_list: Bool.False }
		if node.kind == "ty-tag-union" {
			{ shape: Written(TypeText.union_shape(nodes, at)), is_list: Bool.False }
		} else if node.kind == "ty-apply" {
			match node.kids {
				[head, element] if Tree.attribute(Tree.node_at(nodes, head), "name") == "List" =>
					{ ..TypeText.argument_shape(nodes, element), is_list: Bool.True }
				_ => unread
			}
		} else {
			name = Tree.attribute(node, "name")
			if name == "" {
				unread
			} else {
				{ shape: Named(Tree.last_part(name)), is_list: Bool.False }
			}
		}
	}

	## The names of the types the type at `at` mentions, each by its last
	## part, added to `into`.
	mentioned_type_names : List(Tree.Node), U64, Set(Str) -> Set(Str)
	mentioned_type_names = |nodes, at, into| {
		node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
		name = Tree.attribute(node, "name")
		here = if node.kind.starts_with("ty") and name != "" {
			into.insert(Tree.last_part(name))
		} else {
			into
		}
		node.kids.fold(here, |names, kid| TypeText.mentioned_type_names(nodes, kid, names))
	}

	## The first argument in a function type's argument text, `a, b`.
	first_argument : Str -> Str
	first_argument = |arguments| {
		bytes = arguments.to_utf8()
		$depth : I64
		var $depth = 0
		$at : U64
		var $at = 0
		for byte in bytes {
			$depth = $depth + depth_change(byte)
			if $depth == 0 and byte == ',' {
				return Text.trim(Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.take_first($at)))
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		Text.trim(arguments)
	}

	## `Try(Fraction, [OutOfRange])` gives `Fraction`, and any other type
	## itself, trimmed.
	success_type : Str -> Str
	success_type = |written| {
		text = Text.trim(written)
		if text.starts_with("Try(") and text.ends_with(")") {
			TypeText.first_argument(inside(text, 4))
		} else {
			text
		}
	}

	## The element type's text of a `List(...)` or a `Try` of one.
	list_element : Str -> Try(Str, [NoList])
	list_element = |written| {
		text = TypeText.success_type(written)
		if text.starts_with("List(") and text.ends_with(")") {
			Ok(inside(text, 5))
		} else {
			Err(NoList)
		}
	}

	## The leading run of name bytes of a type's text (`A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`,
	## `_`, `.`), `""` when it starts with none.
	type_head : Str -> Str
	type_head = |text| {
		bytes = text.to_utf8()
		length = bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_type_name_byte(byte))) ?? bytes.len()
		Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.take_first(length))
	}

	## The last word of a type's text, or `""` for one with no name:
	## `Shapes.RoundShape(a)` gives `shape`.
	element_word : Str -> Str
	element_word = |element| {
		head = TypeText.type_head(element)
		Text.name_words(Tree.last_part(head)).last() ?? ""
	}

	## Words joined as one type name: `rounded`, `rectangle` gives
	## `RoundedRectangle`.
	camel_case : List(Str) -> Str
	camel_case = |words| Str.join_with(words.map(capitalized), "")

	## A tag's first word, lowercased: `Unpinned` gives `unpinned`, `AddedTo`
	## gives `added`.
	tag_first_word : Str -> Str
	tag_first_word = |tag| {
		bytes = tag.to_utf8()
		match bytes {
			[first, .. as rest] => {
				length = rest.find_first_index(Text.is_capital) ?? rest.len()
				Text.lower(Str.from_utf8_lossy([first].concat(rest.take_first(length))))
			}
			[] => ""
		}
	}

	## A type's text as its parts: a function when an arrow stands outside
	## every bracket, once any `where` clause is dropped.
	parts_of : Str -> TypeText.Parts
	parts_of = |written| {
		bytes = written.to_utf8()
		body = bytes.take_first(where_start(bytes))
		$depth : I64
		var $depth = 0
		$at : U64
		var $at = 0
		while $at + 1 < body.len() {
			byte = body.get($at) ?? 0
			$depth = $depth + depth_change(byte)
			is_arrow = (byte == '-' or byte == '=') and (body.get($at + 1) ?? 0) == '>'
			if $depth == 0 and is_arrow {
				return {
					is_function: Bool.True,
					arguments: Text.trim(Str.from_utf8_lossy(body.take_first($at))),
					result: Text.trim(Str.from_utf8_lossy(body.drop_first($at + 2))),
				}
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		{ is_function: Bool.False, arguments: "", result: Text.trim(Str.from_utf8_lossy(body)) }
	}

	## The source text of a node, from the file's lines: its end column is
	## one past its last byte.
	span_text : List(Str), Tree.Node -> Str
	span_text = |source_lines, node|
		if node.line == 0 {
			""
		} else if node.line == node.end_line {
			columns(Text.line_at(source_lines, node.line), node.col, node.end_col)
		} else {
			first = columns(Text.line_at(source_lines, node.line), node.col, Text.line_at(source_lines, node.line).count_utf8_bytes() + 1)
			middle = source_lines.sublist({ start: node.line, len: node.end_line - node.line - 1 })
			last = columns(Text.line_at(source_lines, node.end_line), 1, node.end_col)
			Str.join_with([first].concat(middle).append(last), "\n")
		}

	## The place of the sibling just before the node at `at`, or 0.
	previous_sibling : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> U64
	previous_sibling = |nodes, at| {
		parent = Tree.node_at(nodes, at).parent
		if parent == 0 {
			return 0
		}
		$previous : U64
		var $previous = 0
		for kid in Tree.node_at(nodes, parent).kids {
			if kid == at {
				return $previous
			}
			$previous = kid
		}
		0
	}

	## Whether the definition at `at` names `name` in its body, as an
	## identifier (`name`, `Tree.name`) or a method call. A node's
	## descendants follow it, each deeper than it.
	calls_itself : List(Tree.Node), U64, Str -> Bool
	calls_itself = |nodes, at, name| {
		depth = Tree.node_at(nodes, at).depth
		var $place = at + 1
		while $place <= nodes.len() and Tree.node_at(nodes, $place).depth > depth {
			node = Tree.node_at(nodes, $place)
			if node.kind == "e-ident" {
				raw = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
				if raw == name or raw.ends_with(".${name}") {
					return Bool.True
				}
			}
			if node.kind == "e-method-call" and Tree.attribute(node, "method") == name {
				return Bool.True
			}
			$place = $place + 1
		}
		Bool.False
	}
}

## How a byte moves the bracket depth.
depth_change : U8 -> I64
depth_change = |byte|
	if byte == '(' or byte == '[' or byte == '{' {
		1
	} else if byte == ')' or byte == ']' or byte == '}' {
		-1
	} else {
		0
	}

## The bytes before ` where ` outside every bracket, or all of them.
where_start : List(U8) -> U64
where_start = |bytes| {
	clause = " where ".to_utf8()
	$depth : I64
	var $depth = 0
	$at : U64
	var $at = 0
	for byte in bytes {
		$depth = $depth + depth_change(byte)
		if $depth == 0 and bytes.sublist({ start: $at, len: clause.len() }) == clause {
			return $at
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	bytes.len()
}

## A text between its first `opening` bytes and its last byte.
inside : Str, U64 -> Str
inside = |text, opening| {
	length = text.count_utf8_bytes()
	Text.bytes_of(text, { start: opening, count: length - opening - 1 })
}

## Shale's `sub(line, from, to - 1)`: the bytes from column `from` to before
## column `to`, both counted from 1, `""` when none lie between.
columns : Str, U64, U64 -> Str
columns = |line, from, to|
	if to <= from or from == 0 {
		""
	} else {
		Text.bytes_of(line, { start: from - 1, count: to - from })
	}

is_type_name_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_type_name_byte = |byte| Text.is_capital(byte) or Text.is_small_letter(byte) or Text.is_digit(byte) or byte == '_' or byte == '.'

## A word with its first byte made a capital, as Shale's `upper` does.
capitalized : Str -> Str
capitalized = |word|
	match word.to_utf8() {
		[first, .. as rest] if Text.is_small_letter(first) => Str.from_utf8_lossy([first - 32].concat(rest))
		_ => word
	}

cookbook/roc/hunt_names/Makers.roc, 122 lines

## What hunt_names' `phrase_name` passes as a maker
## (cookbook/roc/declared.shale's `reads_as_maker`): a constructor that gives its own module's type, a
## conversion (`to_*`, `into_*`, and a `from_*` that takes or gives its
## module's type, or sits in a module with no type of its own), and a
## changed copy (`with_*`, `without_*` giving its first argument's type).
import lib.Text
import lib.Tree
import Facts
import Reading
import TypeText

Makers := [].{

	## What a definition's type says: whether it is a function, its first
	## argument's type, what it gives, whether its type is known at all, and
	## the note a finding adds when the type is the checker's.
	Signature : {
		is_function : Bool,
		first : Str,
		result : Str,
		is_known : Bool,
		source_note : Str,
	}

	## Whether a function named `words`, whose first word is a preposition,
	## reads as a constructor, a conversion or a changed copy.
	reads_as_maker : Reading.Definition, List(Str), Makers.Signature, Facts.Gathered, Set(Str) -> Bool
	reads_as_maker = |definition, words, signature, facts, prepositions| {
		word = words.first() ?? ""
		if ["into", "to"].contains(word) {
			Bool.True
		} else if ["with", "without"].contains(word) and signature.result == signature.first {
			Bool.True
		} else if word == "from" {
			is_from_conversion(definition, words, signature, facts, prepositions)
		} else {
			constructor_words.contains(word) and is_own_type(definition, TypeText.success_type(signature.result), facts)
		}
	}
}

## The first words a constructor may start with: the ones constructors use in
## safari, roc-chat and roc-markdown (`Clock.at_step`, `Dm.between`,
## `SignedIn.by_session`, `MdText.for_input`, `Name.of_strict`,
## `Directory.with_founder`).
constructor_words : List(Str)
constructor_words = ["at", "between", "by", "for", "of", "with"]

## Whether `written` names the module the definition is in, a type declared
## in its file, or the type it is a member of. Type arguments don't count.
is_own_type : Reading.Definition, Str, Facts.Gathered -> Bool
is_own_type = |definition, written, facts| {
	head = TypeText.type_head(written)
	if head == "" {
		return Bool.False
	}
	parts = head.split_on(".")
	first_part = parts.first() ?? ""
	last_part = parts.last() ?? ""
	if parts.len() == 1 and facts.type_names.contains("${definition.path}|${first_part}") {
		Bool.True
	} else {
		first_part == Tree.module_name(definition.path) or first_part == definition.owner or last_part == definition.owner
	}
}

## Whether `written` names its module's own type anywhere in it: each run
## that starts with a capital at a word's start.
mentions_own_type : Reading.Definition, Str, Facts.Gathered -> Bool
mentions_own_type = |definition, written, facts|
	capital_runs(written).any(|run| is_own_type(definition, run, facts))

## Each run of name bytes (`A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_`, `.`) that starts with a
## capital no word byte stands before, left to right.
capital_runs : Str -> List(Str)
capital_runs = |text| {
	bytes = text.to_utf8()
	var $runs = []
	$at : U64
	var $at = 0
	while $at < bytes.len() {
		byte = bytes.get($at) ?? 0
		before = if $at == 0 {
			' '
		} else {
			bytes.get($at - 1) ?? ' '
		}
		if Text.is_capital(byte) and !(is_word_byte(before)) {
			run = TypeText.type_head(Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.drop_first($at)))
			$runs = $runs.append(run)
			$at = $at + run.count_utf8_bytes()
		} else {
			$at = $at + 1
		}
	}
	$runs
}

is_word_byte : U8 -> Bool
is_word_byte = |byte| Text.is_capital(byte) or Text.is_small_letter(byte) or Text.is_digit(byte) or byte == '_'

## Whether the file at `path` declares one type, `[].{ ... }`, which holds
## the module's functions and has no values of its own.
has_no_type_of_its_own : Str, Facts.Gathered -> Bool
has_no_type_of_its_own = |path, facts|
	match facts.type_kinds.get(path) ?? [] {
		[is_holder] => is_holder
		_ => Bool.False
	}

## Whether a function named `words`, whose first word is `from`, reads as a
## conversion.
is_from_conversion : Reading.Definition, List(Str), Makers.Signature, Facts.Gathered, Set(Str) -> Bool
is_from_conversion = |definition, words, signature, facts, prepositions| {
	gives = TypeText.success_type(signature.result)
	if mentions_own_type(definition, signature.first, facts) or mentions_own_type(definition, gives, facts) {
		Bool.True
	} else {
		second = words.get(1) ?? ""
		signature.is_known and has_no_type_of_its_own(definition.path, facts) and words.len() > 1 and !(prepositions.contains(second))
	}
}

cookbook/roc/hunt_names.shale, 718 lines, at a69380e1

The libraries it loads: cookbook/findings.shale (21 lines), cookbook/roc/parsed.shale (34 lines), cookbook/roc/pinned.shale (20 lines), cookbook/roc/types.shale (301 lines), cookbook/roc/declared.shale (1,075 lines), cookbook/roc/headers.shale (96 lines), cookbook/roc/house.shale (46 lines), cookbook/roc/doc_names.shale (195 lines), cookbook/roc/naming_plants.shale (65 lines), cookbook/roc/naming_passes.shale (146 lines).

-- This recipe looks for awkward names in every .roc file of a tree: an
-- effect named like a state, a question that returns no `Bool`, a name made
-- only of vague words, and the other checks below. A finding is a question
-- for the reader, not a verdict. The recipe reads the top-level definitions
-- and the members of module types (`Html := [].{ ... }`), and locals only for
-- `short_name`, from the syntax tree of Roc's own parser (cookbook/roc/parsed.shale), so
-- an annotation broken across lines and a `where` clause read as Roc reads
-- them. Files that don't parse are listed after the findings, and then the
-- run fails.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/hunt_names.shale glob=chat/**/*.roc
--   shale cookbook:roc/hunt_names.shale self_test=1
--
-- The arguments:
--   glob       the files to check, `**/*.roc` by default;
--   words      with `words=1`, print the census of effects' first words
--              (below) instead of the findings;
--   house      with `house=0`, leave out what is only our house style
--              (cookbook/roc/house.shale), for another project's code;
--   types      with `types=1`, also ask Roc's type checker (below);
--   root       the app the type checker starts from, or several
--              (`root=a.roc,b.roc`);
--   terms      a project's file of its own terms, which `singular_list`
--              reads (below): a term a line, its words joined by `_`, and
--              after a `:` the element type of the list it names. Delivery's
--              `route: Stop` says a `List(Stop)` is a route, and `two_opt`
--              alone is one word, an act's name, as a verb is;
--   self_test  with `self_test=1`, check the plants (below).
--
-- An effect is a function whose name ends in `!`. The checks:
--
--   state_effect  An effect whose first word is a past participle
--                 (`held_raw!`, `done!`) is named like a state; a verb would
--                 say what it does. The participle is fine when it starts
--                 the name of a type in the effect's annotation
--                 (`rounded_rectangle! : Frame, RoundedRectangle => {}`),
--                 because there it describes the thing the effect draws.
--   question      A function named as a question (`is_*`, `has_*`, `can_*`,
--                 `should_*`) that returns something other than a `Bool`,
--                 or an effect so named that returns no `Bool`
--                 (`is_open! : Str => Str`); and a function that returns a
--                 `Bool` but is named like a state (`marked : Str -> Bool`).
--                 A name with `_is_` or `_has_` inside (`unsigned_is_even`)
--                 is a question too. An effect that returns a `Bool`
--                 (`is_playing! : Sound => Bool`) is fine, because asking
--                 the host about live state has to be an effect. Only
--                 functions are checked: a value (`has_got : List(Bool)`)
--                 and an inferred type (`is_eq : _`) are not. With
--                 `types=1` a definition's type comes from the checker, so
--                 an unannotated `is_ready = |n| n + 1` is checked, and a
--                 result that is an alias of `Bool` (`Answer : Bool`)
--                 counts as a `Bool`.
--   vague         A name made only of vague words (cookbook/words/vague.txt):
--                 `handle_data`, `process!`, `do_it`. The entry points
--                 `handle`, `run` and `main` are fine.
--   name_type     A value named `*_count` whose type is not an integer, or
--                 `*_path` whose type is neither `Str` nor one naming `Path`.
--   noun_effect   An effect whose first word is not a known verb
--                 (cookbook/words/verbs.txt), such as a plain noun (`links!`,
--                 `page!`), reads as a value rather than an act. When the
--                 first word is a namespace prefix such as `block_` or
--                 `port_` (cookbook/words/namespaces.txt), the word after it
--                 is checked instead, here and by `state_effect`, and the
--                 namespace's own instructions listed in that file count as
--                 verbs (`port_out_32!`). An effect whose first argument is
--                 a surface, a `Frame` or a `Canvas`, is named for what it
--                 draws there (`circle! : Frame, Circle => {}`, called as
--                 `frame.circle!(...)`), so it is not checked. An effect with
--                 no annotation shows no surface, so it is checked.
--   negative      A `Bool` value named `no_*` or `not_*`, or an annotated
--                 name starting `is_not_`: its negation reads twice.
--   preposition_split  One stem given different trailing prepositions in
--                 one file (`blocks_of`, `blocks_in`, `blocks_from`). One
--                 relation should keep one preposition, or the names should
--                 say how they differ. It is reported once, at the first
--                 name. These prepositions are left out before counting:
--                 - one of a pair of opposites (`insert_before` beside
--                   `insert_after`; also `from` and `to`, `with` and
--                   `without`, `over` and `under`);
--                 - a `_from` name that takes more arguments than its
--                   siblings, a recursive worker resuming at an index
--                   (`blocks_from` beside `blocks_in`);
--                 - a module's suffix convention: a preposition on three
--                   or more stems in the same file, whose annotations
--                   share their first argument's type and their result
--                   (roc-markdown's `*_onto` writers each take a `List(U8)`
--                   and return it), so `run_onto` beside `run_at` is no
--                   split. Only the pair's own file counts, so a pair's
--                   verdict never moves when another file gains or loses
--                   a name;
--                 - a word the file declares as a keyword of the language
--                   it interprets, in a comment line such as
--                   `# keywords: for, on` (BASIC's `do_for`, `do_on`).
--   command_tense  An effect that takes a tag union whose tags all start
--                 with a past participle and carry no payload
--                 (`pin! : ..., [Pinned, Unpinned]`) names an instruction
--                 like an event. A command is a verb (`[Pin, Unpin]`). A
--                 union with a payload (`[Known(accounts), Unasked]`)
--                 carries state rather than an order. The union may be
--                 written in place or be a type declared in any file
--                 checked, and a `List(T)` argument is checked as `T`.
--   mixed_tense   An effect that takes a tag union (read as for
--                 `command_tense`, payloads included) with a tag starting
--                 with a verb beside one starting with a past participle
--                 (`apply! : [Pin, Unpinned]`): one of them is in the wrong
--                 mood. Only what an effect is handed is checked. A union an
--                 effect returns, a record field and a pure function's
--                 argument hold the domain's words for states (`Redirect`
--                 beside `Found`).
--   container     A type's name (`Entry`, `NodeInfo`) or a record field's
--                 (`items : List(Str)`) made only of container words
--                 (cookbook/words/containers.txt) and vague words. It says
--                 where a value sits, not what it holds. When the container
--                 word is the domain's own, the doc comment above the
--                 declaration says whose it is: `## A folder's entry` keeps
--                 `Entry`, and `## A listing's entries` keeps a field
--                 `entries`. A type's words are split at its capitals, a
--                 field's at its underscores. A field of one plain value (a
--                 number, a `Str`, a `Bool`: `entry : F64`) holds nothing a
--                 container could, so it passes. Fields in a local's
--                 annotation are not read.
--   short_name    A name of one letter (`w : F64`, `{ k : U64 }`, `p = w *
--                 h`): a top-level or member name, a record field, and every
--                 binding inside a definition, a local, a function's or a
--                 lambda's parameter, a match arm's binding, a destructured
--                 record's field and a `var` (past its `$`). A field or a
--                 binding may be a coordinate (`x`, `y`, `z`, and `w` beside
--                 `x` and `y`), a colour's channel (`r`, `g`, `b`, and `a`
--                 beside them) or a triangle's corner (`a`, `b` and `c`, all
--                 three, a binding's from one record). A loop's variable may
--                 be one letter too: a `for`'s binding, a `var` a `while`
--                 tests, and the parameters of a one-line lambda that is the
--                 direct argument of a list method (`xs.map(|x| x * 2)`,
--                 `List.walk(xs, 0, |n, x| n + x)`; declared.shale's
--                 LOOP_METHODS). A lambda over two lines, or handed to
--                 anything else, names its parameters.
--   worker_name   A name whose last word says only that it is a helper:
--                 `_acc`, `_loop`, `_inner`, `_helper` or `_rec`
--                 (`count_acc`). Name a recursive worker for the parameter
--                 it adds, so that a call reads as a sentence:
--                 `count_from(xs, at)` for a start point,
--                 `html_onto(out, node)` for an output being built,
--                 `walk_with(tree, seen)` for other carried state. The entry
--                 function takes the plain name, `count`. `_step`, `_walk`
--                 and `_go` are ordinary words too, so they are reported
--                 only on a definition that calls itself.
--   stacked_preposition  A name whose last two words are both prepositions
--                 (cookbook/words/prepositions.txt), like `rest_from_onto`:
--                 a worker's suffix added to an entry name that already ends
--                 in one. Let each read once: the entry says what it returns
--                 (`tail_after`), the worker what it adds (`rest_onto`). A
--                 name made only of prepositions (`at_of`) is not reported,
--                 since its first word serves as a noun.
--   taken_word    A name that is a whole word from cookbook/words/taken.txt:
--                 a function named by one of Roc's own words (`record`,
--                 `tag`, `alias`, `module`), which reads as Roc's rather
--                 than the domain's, or a value named by a number from
--                 `one` to `twelve` (`three : List(Fields)`), which says
--                 how many rather than what it holds. A function that
--                 returns the very thing, its result's last part being the
--                 word capitalized (`record : ApiKey.Key -> ApiKey.Record`),
--                 is fine.
--   bare_participle  A pure function whose whole name is one past participle
--                 (`added`, `joined`, `named`, `chosen`), which reads too
--                 easily as a `Bool`. Name it by a noun for what it gives
--                 (`user_by_name`) or a verb for what it does (`add_user`).
--                 A name of two parts or more (`escaped_text`, `is_added`)
--                 and a value are not reported. An effect named this way is
--                 left to `state_effect`, and a function that gives a `Bool`
--                 to `question`.
--   phrase_name   A pure function, not a constant, whose first word is a
--                 preposition (cookbook/words/prepositions.txt) and which gives
--                 something other than a `Bool`: `in_view`, `on_next_segment`,
--                 `over_gap`. Bare like that it reads as a yes or no and hides
--                 what it gives, and a reader of a definition has often lost
--                 the module's context. Name the thing (`trees_in_view`,
--                 `rider_on_next_segment`), even if that repeats the module.
--                 The type decides what reads as a constructor or conversion,
--                 and these pass:
--                 - a constructor: a first word in CONSTRUCTOR_WORDS
--                   (cookbook/roc/declared.shale) and a result, or a `Try`
--                   of one, that is its own module's type, a type declared
--                   in that module, or the type it is a member of (`Clock.at_step : U32 -> Clock`,
--                   `Color.of_hex : U32 -> Color.Rgb`). The word matters as
--                   well as the type: `Scene.in_view : View -> Scene` gives
--                   its own type and still reads as a question;
--                 - a conversion: `to_*` and `into_*`, which name what they
--                   give;
--                 - a `from_*` that takes or gives its own module's type, as
--                   above, even inside a record, a union or a list
--                   (`Along.from_start : Along -> Distance`,
--                   `Key.from_path : Str -> Try({ key : Key }, [NoKey])`). A
--                   `Try` gives its success only: an error that carries the
--                   type is no conversion to it;
--                 - a `from_<noun>` in a module that has no type of its own,
--                   one whose file declares only `Hex :: [].{ ... }`
--                   (`Hex.from_hex : Str -> Try(List(U8), [NotHex])`). Such a
--                   module has no type to take or give. A module with a type
--                   is held to the rule above, so
--                   `DateTime.from_clock : I64 -> Try(Str, [OutOfRange])`,
--                   which neither takes nor gives a `DateTime`, is reported.
--                   The next word has to be no preposition, so `from_behind`
--                   stays a phrase, and the type has to be known;
--                 - a changed copy: `with_*` or `without_*` that gives its
--                   first argument's type (`with_lean : Bike, Angle -> Bike`).
--                 A definition with no annotation shows none of this, so it
--                 is reported unless `types=1` supplies its type. A list that
--                 is no function, a value, a field or a parameter, named from
--                 a preposition, that `singular_list` would report
--                 (`by_slot : List(List(Stop))`) is reported here instead: it
--                 wants its noun (`routes_by_slot`), not a plural.
--   singular_list  A name that holds or gives a `List(...)`, or a `Try` of
--                 one, but reads as one thing: `triangle : List(Shape)`. The
--                 name ends in a plural of what the list holds (`triangles`,
--                 `herd_cows`) or is explicit (`triangle_list`). A collective
--                 noun is no plural: `herd`, `crowd` and `route` are reported.
--                 Read are top-level and member definitions, record fields,
--                 and the plain parameters of a top-level or member lambda.
--                 The word that counts is the one before a preposition or an
--                 `after` word of cookbook/words/list_names.txt, else the
--                 last (`trees_in_view`, `corners_ahead`). These pass:
--                 - a `List(U8)`, whose bytes are plumbing: the name says what
--                   they mean (`boundary`). A `List(F64)` is checked, since a
--                   flat run of coordinates can't be told from many readings;
--                 - a word list_names.txt calls `many`, one that can't be
--                   counted, and a word read as a participle (`clipped`);
--                 - a function whose whole name is a verb (`draw`) or a term
--                   (`two_opt`), and a changed copy: a function that gives
--                   its first argument's type, whatever its first word
--                   (`trim_hull`, `coalesce`, `stable_by_load_desc`);
--                 - a word the project's terms (`terms=`) say names a list
--                   of its element (`route` of `Stop`s);
--                 - one letter, and a value named by a number, which are
--                   `short_name`'s and `taken_word`'s to judge;
--                 - an accumulator's short idiom, as a whole name (`out`);
--                 - a name `phrase_name` reports, to be named again anyway.
--                 The word list, a participle and a verb don't pass a word
--                 that is the element's own (`route : List(Route)`), and a
--                 changed copy of more than one word does, as its object is
--                 one element (`set_run : List(Run), Run -> List(Run)`). A word
--                 verbs.txt holds that list_names.txt calls `one` is no verb
--                 here (`route`). An `s` makes no plural after `s` (`class`),
--                 after letters that are no word (`pts`), or in a `one` word
--                 (`axis`). A word list_names.txt calls `adjective`
--                 (`stable`, `cheapest`) is no noun, so the finding says the
--                 name has none and offers no plural of it. A term's words
--                 read as one (`two_opt_pass`'s word is `pass`). An alias of
--                 a list isn't seen, and with `types=1` an unannotated
--                 definition or parameter is read by its inferred type.
--   world_verb    A pure function whose first word is a verb of
--                 cookbook/words/world_verbs.txt, one that claims to act on
--                 something outside (`draw`, `paint_shape`). Nothing is drawn
--                 by a function that only makes a value, so name it for that
--                 value (`tree_shapes`). A verb that says what happens to its
--                 argument is fine (`plus`, `clamp`, `trim_hull`). An effect,
--                 which does act, and a value are not reported. A `##` doc
--                 directly above the definition (or its annotation) answers
--                 it, saying why the verb stands: a renderer named for what
--                 its output is drawn as, as `single`'s doc answers it in
--                 check_boundaries.
--   where_name    A method in a `where` clause named by one word
--                 (`[a.height : a -> U64]`). A clause matches by name alone,
--                 so the name is the whole contract: two words say what it is
--                 for (`scenery_height`). The methods Roc calls by name
--                 (`is_eq`, `plus`, `map`) are fine. A local's clause is read.
--   stale_doc_name  A backticked name in a comment line (`#` or `##` first)
--                 that names nothing in the file or the modules it imports:
--                 a rename leaves its comments behind (rename.shale counts
--                 and leaves them). A bare name is judged when it has two
--                 words or more (`cheapest_insert`), since a one-word one
--                 (`for`, `fold`) is often the language's or the prose's; a
--                 `Module.name` (`Route.two_opt`, a call's parentheses
--                 allowed) is judged against `Module.roc` beside the file,
--                 else a module of that name among the files read (a
--                 package's, `import game.SunPath`), and left when there is
--                 none, as for `List.map` (cookbook/roc/doc_names.shale).
--                 An import is read the same way, and one whose names can't
--                 be read leaves the file's bare names unjudged, as does a
--                 possessive before one (`roc-ray's`), or a language or
--                 library of cookbook/words/cited_sources.txt before it in
--                 its sentence ("Rust's `is_ascii_digit`", "Zig `isDigit`,
--                 Rust `is_ascii_digit`"): it is another's. A
--                 platform's `provides` symbols (`roc_plan`) are its names,
--                 and its bare `roc_` names (`roc_crashed`) the host's.
--
-- Each name is judged once: from its annotation when it has one, else from
-- its definition. An effect that takes an effectful function (`map2!`,
-- `on_err!`: an argument's type holds a `=>`, or a lambda argument's name
-- ends in `!`) has its `!` from that callback, so it is judged as the name
-- without the `!`. Names chosen elsewhere are skipped: the methods Roc calls
-- by name (cookbook/roc/headers.shale), and the top-level names a platform
-- dictates, which are what an app's header provides (`app [loaded, step]`)
-- and what a platform's header requires and provides.
--
-- The output is the counts, one line per finding,
-- `path:line: <check>: <why>`, and the counts again
-- (cookbook/findings.shale).
--
-- The word lists are in cookbook/words/, shared with the Zig name hunt.
-- participles.txt lists the irregular past participles; any other word
-- ending in `ed` counts as one unless ed_verbs.txt lists it. With `words=1`
-- the recipe prints a census instead of the findings: each first word the
-- effects start with, how many start with it, and its verdict: `verb`,
-- `participle`, `vague`, `asks` (`is`, `has`) or `refused` (what
-- `noun_effect` reports). A verb missing from verbs.txt shows up there as
-- `refused`.
--
-- With `types=1` the recipe asks Roc's type checker for each definition's
-- type (cookbook/roc/types.shale). It needs `root=` and the tree's
-- `roc-version` file. A root the checker refuses, or a roc-types built for
-- another Roc version, stops the run. A file that no root imports is
-- checked without types, listed after the findings, and fails the run.
--
--   cd <repo> && shale <shale>/cookbook/roc/hunt_names.shale glob=app/*.roc root=app/main.roc types=1
--
-- `self_test=1` runs the recipe over `cookbook/roc/plants/hunt_names/`. Each
-- plant is named for the check it holds (`question.roc`,
-- `question_where.roc`) and must make that check report, and no other. A
-- `quiet_*.roc` plant must make no check report. Every check needs a plant,
-- and a plant named for no check fails the test. A plant another imports is
-- a CamelCase module, read as snake case (`QuietDocShelf.roc` is
-- `quiet_doc_shelf.roc`); the plants' terms are `terms.txt` there; each plant
-- opens by naming its check, so the check names count as names for
-- `stale_doc_name`; and cookbook/roc/naming_plants.shale holds these
-- rules, with what a finding must say, or not. The census must also give
-- the right verdict for one known word of the plants per verdict. The
-- plants in `typed/` are checked with the types, from their app
-- `typed/QuietApp.roc`, and their CamelCase module names read as snake case
-- (`QuestionInferred` as `question_inferred`); the rest are checked
-- without. The self-test fails without roc-types.
--
-- The recipe reads each file's source as well as its tree, to tell `->`
-- from `=>`, which the tree writes alike. On a large tree that needs more
-- than the default arena.
--
-- What it reads of each definition is cookbook/roc/declared.shale's
-- `file_definitions`, and the checks judged over the whole tree once every
-- file is read are cookbook/roc/naming_passes.shale's.
-- budget: steps=800000000 arena_bytes=3000000000 output_bytes=4000000

const SELF_TEST = arg("self_test", "") == "1"
use("cookbook:findings.shale")
use("./parsed.shale")
use("./pinned.shale")
use("./types.shale")
use("./declared.shale")
use("./headers.shale")
use("./house.shale")
use("./doc_names.shale")
use("./naming_plants.shale")
use("./naming_passes.shale")
const PLANTS = "cookbook:roc/plants/hunt_names/"
const GLOB = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "*.roc") or arg("glob", "**/*.roc")
const TYPES_ARG = arg("types", "0")
if TYPES_ARG ~= "0" and TYPES_ARG ~= "1" then fail("hunt_names: types=" .. TYPES_ARG .. ": 0 (the default) or 1") end
-- The self-test checks its typed plants with the types, and the rest
-- without.
const USE_TYPES = SELF_TEST or TYPES_ARG == "1"
const ROOT = SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "typed/QuietApp.roc") or arg("root", "")
-- The type checker's answers, filled in once the files are known; empty
-- unless USE_TYPES.
const CHECKER_TYPES = {real = {}, pats = {}, exprs = {}, unreached = {}}
const CENSUS_ONLY = arg("words", "") == "1"
const CHECKS = {"state_effect", "question", "vague", "name_type", "negative", "noun_effect", "command_tense", "mixed_tense", "container", "preposition_split", "short_name", "worker_name", "stacked_preposition", "taken_word", "bare_participle", "phrase_name", "singular_list", "world_verb", "where_name", "stale_doc_name"}
-- `worker_name` reports a helper suffix always, and a suffix that is also an
-- ordinary word (a fold's `step`, `List.walk`, `can_go`) only on a
-- definition that calls itself.
const HELPER_SUFFIXES = {acc = true, loop = true, inner = true, helper = true, rec = true}
const RECURSION_SUFFIXES = {step = true, walk = true, go = true}

const VERBS = word_set("cookbook:words/verbs.txt")
const PARTICIPLES = word_set("cookbook:words/participles.txt")
const ED_VERBS = word_set("cookbook:words/ed_verbs.txt")
const VAGUE = word_set("cookbook:words/vague.txt")
const CONTAINERS = word_set("cookbook:words/containers.txt")
const PREPOSITIONS = word_set("cookbook:words/prepositions.txt")

const NAMESPACES = namespace_instructions("namespaces.txt")

const TAKEN_WORDS = taken_word_kinds("taken.txt")

const LIST_NAMES = list_name_kinds("list_names.txt")
const WORLD_VERBS = word_set("cookbook:words/world_verbs.txt")
const PLAIN_ELEMENTS = set_of({"U16", "U32", "U64", "I16", "I32", "I64", "F32", "F64", "Dec", "Str", "Bool"})
const TERMS = project_terms(SELF_TEST and (PLANTS .. "terms.txt") or arg("terms", ""))
-- The tables `singular_list` reads (cookbook/roc/declared.shale's
-- `list_name_finding`).
const LIST_WORDS = {list_names = LIST_NAMES, taken = TAKEN_WORDS, verbs = VERBS, prepositions = PREPOSITIONS, plain = PLAIN_ELEMENTS, participles = PARTICIPLES, ed_verbs = ED_VERBS, terms = TERMS}
const SURFACES = {Frame = true, Canvas = true}
-- The keywords each file declares (`# keywords: for, on`), by path.
const DECLARED_KEYWORDS = {}
const ENTRY_POINT_NAMES = {handle = true, run = true, main = true}
const INTEGER_TYPES = {U8 = true, U16 = true, U32 = true, U64 = true, U128 = true, I8 = true, I16 = true, I32 = true, I64 = true, I128 = true}

-- The tag union each type declaration names, by the type's name: `Edit` of
-- `Edit : [Opened, Closed]` maps to its `union_shape`.
const TAG_UNION_TYPES = {}
-- The aliases of `Bool` declared in the files read, by each name the type
-- checker may write for them (`Answer`, `Owner.Answer`).
const BOOL_ALIASES = {}
-- Each type a file declares, by path, as whether it is `[].{ ... }`: an empty
-- union with members.
const TYPES_DECLARED_IN_FILE = {}
-- Each type name a file declares, at the top or inside a module's own type
-- (`MdText := [].{ Budget : ... }`), as a set of `path|Name`.
const TYPE_NAMES_IN_FILE = {}

-- Every type name and record field name that `container` checks, each
-- `{path, line, name, words, is_field, doc}`, where `doc` is the comment
-- lines above its declaration, lowercased.
const TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES = {}
-- The tables declared.shale's `file_definitions` fills.
const FILE_FACTS = {keywords = DECLARED_KEYWORDS, unions = TAG_UNION_TYPES, bool_aliases = BOOL_ALIASES, type_kinds = TYPES_DECLARED_IN_FILE, type_names = TYPE_NAMES_IN_FILE, names = TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES}

const count_by_check = {}
for c in CHECKS do count_by_check[c] = 0 end
-- The set of `path|check` pairs where the check reported, for the self-test.
const fired_in_file = {}
-- Each first word an effect starts with, mapped to `{word, count, verdict}`.
const first_word_census = {}
const finding_lines = {}

function report(path, line, check, why)
  if house_leaves_out("hunt_names", check) then return nil end
  if not CENSUS_ONLY then push(finding_lines, path .. ":" .. line .. ": " .. check .. ": " .. why) end
  count_by_check[check] = count_by_check[check] + 1
  fired_in_file[path .. "|" .. check] = true
  return nil
end

function is_participle(word)
  return reads_as_participle(word, PARTICIPLES, ED_VERBS)
end

for word in keys(VERBS) do
  if is_participle(word) then fail("hunt_names: `" .. word .. "` is in cookbook/words/verbs.txt and reads as a participle, which would make its effects states") end
end

-- What an effect's first word says: `participle`, `verb`, `vague`, `asks`
-- (`is`, `has`) or `refused`.
function first_word_verdict(word)
  if is_participle(word) then return "participle" end
  if has_key(VERBS, word) then return "verb" end
  if has_key(VAGUE, word) then return "vague" end
  if word == "is" or word == "has" then return "asks" end
  return "refused"
end

-- ── the syntax tree ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

-- The checker's type of each plain-name pattern in the parsed file `f`, by
-- its node's index as text: none unless USE_TYPES and the checker reached
-- the file.
function pattern_types_in(f)
  local typed = {}
  if not (USE_TYPES and has_key(CHECKER_TYPES.real, f.path)) then return typed end
  for i = 1, #f.nodes do
    if f.nodes[i].kind == "p-ident" then
      local checker_type = roc_type_at(CHECKER_TYPES, "pat", f.path, f.nodes[i])
      if checker_type ~= nil then typed[tostring(i)] = checker_type end
    end
  end
  return typed
end

-- Every top-level and module-member annotation and definition in the
-- parsed files, as declared.shale's `file_definitions` reads them, filling
-- FILE_FACTS along the way.
function read_definitions(parsed_files)
  local definitions = {}
  for f in parsed_files do
    local src = split(read(f.path), "\n")
    local known = {dictated = header_names(f.nodes).dictated, pattern_types = pattern_types_in(f), recursion_suffixes = RECURSION_SUFFIXES}
    for def in file_definitions(f, src, known, FILE_FACTS) do push(definitions, def) end
  end
  return definitions
end

-- ── the checks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function all_tags_past(tags)
  for t in tags do
    if not is_participle(tag_first_word(t)) then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- What a definition's type says, for `question`, `taken_word` and
-- `phrase_name`: `{is_function, first, result, known, source_note}`. The type
-- is the checker's when it gave one, else the annotation's. `known` is false
-- for a definition with no annotation and no checker's type.
function definition_signature(def)
  local signature = {is_function = def.annotation and def.fn, first = get(def, "first", ""), result = get(def, "result", ""), known = def.annotation, source_note = ""}
  if has_key(def, "typed") then
    local checker = roc_type_parts(def.typed)
    signature = {is_function = checker.fn, first = first_argument(checker.args), result = checker.result, known = true, source_note = " (the checker's type)"}
    if has_key(BOOL_ALIASES, checker.result) then signature.result = "Bool" end
  end
  return signature
end

-- Reports a name whose type says many and whose head word says one:
-- `singular_list` in the header. `subject` is `{path, line, name, kind,
-- is_function, first, gives}`, `kind` being what the report calls it.
function judge_list_name(subject)
  local found = list_name_finding(subject, LIST_WORDS)
  if found ~= nil then report(subject.path, subject.line, found.check, found.why) end
  return nil
end

-- Reports what each check finds in one definition record, except
-- `container` and `preposition_split`, which are judged over all the files
-- afterwards.
function judge_definition(def)
  local path = def.path
  local line = def.line
  local full_name = def.name
  if has_key(LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES, full_name) then return nil end
  local has_bang = ends_with(full_name, "!")
  local name = has_bang and sub(full_name, 1, #full_name - 1) or full_name
  local is_effect = has_bang and not def.callback
  local ws = split(name, "_")
  local last_word = ws[#ws]
  local is_annotation = def.annotation
  -- A definition paired with an annotation was judged at the annotation.
  local judged_here = not def.paired
  local asks_inside = contains(name, "_is_") or contains(name, "_has_")
  local has_namespace = is_effect and #ws > 1 and has_key(NAMESPACES, ws[1])
  local act_word = has_namespace and ws[2] or ws[1]
  local act_verdict = first_word_verdict(act_word)
  if has_namespace and act_verdict == "refused" and has_key(NAMESPACES[ws[1]], act_word) then act_verdict = "verb" end
  local act_place = has_namespace and ("the word after its namespace `" .. ws[1] .. "_`") or "its first word"
  local named_as_state = is_participle(act_word) and not asks_inside
  if is_effect and judged_here then
    if not has_key(first_word_census, act_word) then first_word_census[act_word] = {word = act_word, count = 0, verdict = act_verdict} end
    first_word_census[act_word].count = first_word_census[act_word].count + 1
  end
  local arguments = get(def, "args") or {}
  local draws_on_surface = #arguments > 0 and has_key(SURFACES, get(arguments[1], "ref", ""))
  if is_effect and judged_here and act_verdict == "refused" and not draws_on_surface then
    if has_key(PREPOSITIONS, act_word) then report(path, line, "noun_effect", "`" .. full_name .. "` has an effect but " .. act_place .. " is a preposition, `" .. act_word .. "`: an effect is named for its act")
    else report(path, line, "noun_effect", "`" .. full_name .. "` has an effect but " .. act_place .. ", `" .. act_word .. "`, is no verb: it reads as a value, not an act") end
  end
  if judged_here and #ws > 1 and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, last_word) then note_trailing_preposition(def, ws) end
  local names_drawn_type = #ws > 1 and has_key(get(def, "types") or {}, camel_case(ws))
  if is_effect and judged_here and named_as_state and not names_drawn_type then report(path, line, "state_effect", "`" .. full_name .. "` has an effect but is named as a state, `" .. act_word .. "`: a verb says what it does") end
  local named_as_question = #ws > 1 and (ws[1] == "is" or ws[1] == "has" or ws[1] == "can" or ws[1] == "should")
  local signature = definition_signature(def)
  local returns_bool = signature.is_function and signature.result == "Bool"
  if named_as_question and judged_here and is_effect and not returns_bool then report(path, line, "question", "`" .. full_name .. "` asks a question but has an effect" .. (signature.is_function and (" and gives `" .. signature.result .. "`" .. signature.source_note) or "")) end
  if returns_bool and named_as_state and judged_here then report(path, line, "question", "`" .. full_name .. "` gives a `Bool`" .. signature.source_note .. " but is named as a state, `" .. ws[1] .. "`: ask it (`is_*`, `has_*`)") end
  if named_as_question and judged_here and signature.known and signature.is_function and not is_effect and signature.result ~= "Bool" and signature.result ~= "_" then report(path, line, "question", "`" .. full_name .. "` asks a question but gives `" .. signature.result .. "`" .. signature.source_note) end
  if judged_here then
    local all_vague = true
    for w in ws do
      if not has_key(VAGUE, w) then all_vague = false end
    end
    if #ws == 1 and has_key(ENTRY_POINT_NAMES, ws[1]) then all_vague = false end
    if all_vague then report(path, line, "vague", "`" .. full_name .. "` is only vague words: what does it handle, and how?") end
    if #name == 1 then report(path, line, "short_name", "`" .. full_name .. "` is one letter, read far from where it is defined: name what it holds") end
    local has_leading_noun = false
    for w in take(ws, max(#ws - 2, 0)) do
      if not has_key(PREPOSITIONS, w) then has_leading_noun = true end
    end
    if has_leading_noun and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, last_word) and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, ws[#ws - 1]) then report(path, line, "stacked_preposition", "`" .. full_name .. "` stacks two prepositions, `_" .. ws[#ws - 1] .. "_" .. last_word .. "`: let each read once, the entry named for what it gives (`rest`, `tail_after`) and the worker for what it adds (`rest_onto`)") end
    -- A function is known by its type, else by a lambda definition; a value
    -- by a type that is no function, else by a definition that is no
    -- lambda. An inferred annotation (`two : _`) with no checker's type is
    -- neither.
    local has_type = signature.known and not (is_annotation and get(def, "whole", "") == "_" and not has_key(def, "typed"))
    local is_lambda = get(def, "lambda", false)
    local is_function = signature.is_function or (not signature.known and is_lambda)
    local is_value = (has_type and not signature.is_function) or (not signature.known and not is_lambda)
    local taken_kind = get(TAKEN_WORDS, name, "")
    if taken_kind == "roc" and is_function then
      local result_parts = split(signature.result, ".")
      local returns_the_word = signature.is_function and result_parts[#result_parts] == camel_case({name})
      if not returns_the_word then report(path, line, "taken_word", "`" .. full_name .. "` is Roc's own word, `" .. name .. "`, for a function that gives no `" .. camel_case({name}) .. "`: name it for the domain's thing (`element`, `append`), and keep Roc's words for Roc") end
    end
    if taken_kind == "cardinal" and is_value then report(path, line, "taken_word", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a number's name for a value: it says how many, not what it holds") end
    -- An effect so named is `state_effect`'s, and a function so named that
    -- gives a `Bool` is `question`'s, so this check takes the rest.
    if not has_bang and #ws == 1 and is_participle(name) and is_function and not returns_bool then report(path, line, "bare_participle", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a function named by a bare past participle, which reads as a `Bool`: name it by a noun for what it gives (`user_by_name`) or a verb for what it does (`add_user`)") end
    -- An effect is `noun_effect`'s, and a result of `_` says nothing.
    if not has_bang and has_key(PREPOSITIONS, ws[1]) and is_function and not returns_bool and signature.result ~= "_" and not reads_as_maker(def, ws, signature, FILE_FACTS, PREPOSITIONS) then
      local gives = signature.known and ("gives `" .. signature.result .. "`" .. signature.source_note) or "has no annotation to show it makes its own type"
      report(path, line, "phrase_name", "`" .. full_name .. "` starts with a preposition, `" .. ws[1] .. "`, and " .. gives .. ": bare, it reads as a yes or no and hides what it gives; name the thing (`trees_in_view`, not `in_view`)")
    elseif signature.known then
      judge_list_name({path = path, line = line, name = full_name, kind = signature.is_function and "function" or "value", is_function = signature.is_function, first = signature.first, gives = signature.result})
    end
    if not has_bang and is_function and has_key(WORLD_VERBS, ws[1]) and not get(def, "has_doc", false) then report(path, line, "world_verb", "`" .. full_name .. "` is pure, and `" .. ws[1] .. "` claims to act on something outside: name it for the value it gives (`tree_shapes`, not `draw_tree`)") end
    local argument_types = get(def, "argument_types", {})
    local parameters = get(def, "parameters", {})
    for k = 1, #parameters do
      local parameter = parameters[k]
      local parameter_type = k <= #argument_types and argument_types[k] or get(parameter, "typed", "")
      if parameter.name ~= "" then judge_list_name({path = path, line = parameter.line, name = parameter.name, kind = "parameter", is_function = false, first = "", gives = parameter_type}) end
    end
  end
  -- `worker_name` is judged at the definition, which knows whether it calls
  -- itself, and at an annotation only when no definition follows it, as
  -- with a hosted effect.
  local annotation_alone = is_annotation and not get(def, "has_def", false)
  local helper_suffix = has_key(HELPER_SUFFIXES, last_word) and (annotation_alone or not is_annotation)
  local recursion_suffix = has_key(RECURSION_SUFFIXES, last_word) and get(def, "recurses", false)
  if #ws > 1 and (helper_suffix or recursion_suffix) then report(path, line, "worker_name", "`" .. full_name .. "` is named only as a helper, `_" .. last_word .. "`: name the worker for the parameter it adds (`_from` a start point, `_onto` an output built, `_with` other carried state) and give the entry function the plain name") end
  if is_annotation and not def.fn and def.whole ~= "_" then
    local annotated_type = def.whole
    if last_word == "count" and not has_key(INTEGER_TYPES, annotated_type) then report(path, line, "name_type", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a count of type `" .. annotated_type .. "`") end
    if last_word == "path" and annotated_type ~= "Str" and not contains(annotated_type, "Path") then report(path, line, "name_type", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a path of type `" .. annotated_type .. "`") end
    if annotated_type == "Bool" and (ws[1] == "no" or ws[1] == "not") and #ws > 1 then report(path, line, "negative", "`" .. full_name .. "` is a negative flag: `" .. full_name .. " = Bool.false` reads twice") end
  end
  if is_annotation and is_effect and def.fn then
    for argument in arguments do
      local union = get(argument, "union")
      local ref = get(argument, "ref")
      if union == nil and ref ~= nil then union = get(TAG_UNION_TYPES, ref) end
      if union ~= nil then
        local shown = (get(argument, "list") and "a list of " or "") .. "`[" .. join(union.names, ", ") .. "]`"
        if not union.payload and #union.names >= 2 and all_tags_past(union.names) then report(path, line, "command_tense", "`" .. full_name .. "` takes " .. shown .. ", an instruction named like an event: name its tags as commands (`Pinned` is `Pin`)") end
        local command_tags = {}
        local event_tags = {}
        for t in union.names do
          local w = tag_first_word(t)
          if is_participle(w) then push(event_tags, t) elseif has_key(VERBS, w) then push(command_tags, t) end
        end
        if #command_tags > 0 and #event_tags > 0 then report(path, line, "mixed_tense", "`" .. full_name .. "` takes " .. shown .. ": commands (" .. join(command_tags, ", ") .. ") beside events (" .. join(event_tags, ", ") .. "): name what it is told to do in one mood") end
      end
    end
  end
  if is_annotation and #ws > 2 and ws[1] == "is" and ws[2] == "not" then report(path, line, "negative", "`" .. full_name .. "` asks a negative: `!" .. full_name .. "(...)` reads twice") end
  return nil
end

local paths = glob(GLOB)
if SELF_TEST then
  for q in glob(PLANTS .. "typed/*.roc") do push(paths, q) end
end
local file_count = #paths
-- The self-test's untyped plants are imported by no root.
const UNTYPED_PLANTS = SELF_TEST and set_of(glob(PLANTS .. "*.roc")) or {}
if USE_TYPES then
  local got = roc_types_for_files("hunt_names", ROOT, roc_bin("hunt_names", SELF_TEST), paths, UNTYPED_PLANTS)
  CHECKER_TYPES.real = got.real
  CHECKER_TYPES.pats = got.pats
  CHECKER_TYPES.exprs = got.exprs
  CHECKER_TYPES.unreached = got.unreached
end
local parsed = parse_roc_files(paths)
-- This loop does not `yield`, because a yield may keep only 1 MiB, and a
-- large tree's definitions pass that. The arena in the header holds them.
for def in read_definitions(parsed.files) do
  judge_definition(def)
end

for file in parsed.files do
  for found in where_name_findings(file, LANGUAGE_FIXED_NAMES) do report(file.path, found.line, "where_name", found.why) end
  for found in short_binding_findings(file) do report(file.path, found.line, "short_name", found.why) end
end

-- `stale_doc_name` in the header. Each plant opens by naming its check, so
-- in the self-test the check names, and this recipe's, count as names.
function plant_doc_names()
  local known = set_of(CHECKS)
  known.hunt_names = true
  return known
end
const DOC_NAMES_SEEN = {known = SELF_TEST and plant_doc_names() or {}, by_module = {}, by_path = {}, sources = word_set("cookbook:words/cited_sources.txt")}
-- Each file read is known by its path too, so `module_names` parses only
-- a module beside one that the run didn't read.
for file in parsed.files do
  local module = module_name(file.path)
  local names = get(DOC_NAMES_SEEN.by_module, module) or {}
  local own = names_in_tree(file.nodes)
  for n in keys(own) do names[n] = true end
  DOC_NAMES_SEEN.by_module[module] = names
  DOC_NAMES_SEEN.by_path[file.path] = {found = true, names = own}
end
for file in parsed.files do
  for found in stale_doc_findings(file.path, split(read(file.path), "\n"), file.nodes, DOC_NAMES_SEEN) do report(file.path, found.line, "stale_doc_name", found.why) end
end

for named in TYPE_AND_FIELD_NAMES do
  for found in container_findings(named, VAGUE, CONTAINERS) do report(named.path, named.line, found.check, found.why) end
  if named.is_field then judge_list_name({path = named.path, line = named.line, name = named.name, kind = "field", is_function = named.is_function, first = named.first, gives = named.gives}) end
end

for found in preposition_split_findings(DECLARED_KEYWORDS) do report(found.path, found.line, "preposition_split", found.why) end

if CENSUS_ONLY then
  local census = census_lines(first_word_census)
  print_findings("hunt_names (Roc) census: " .. file_count .. " files; " .. census.summary, census.lines)
else
  local check_counts = {}
  for c in CHECKS do push(check_counts, c .. " " .. count_by_check[c]) end
  print_findings("hunt_names (Roc): " .. file_count .. " files; " .. join(check_counts, ", ") .. house_note("hunt_names"), finding_lines)
end
fail_if_refused("hunt_names", parsed.refused, CHECKER_TYPES.unreached)

-- A plant's name relative to PLANTS. A typed plant is a CamelCase module
-- (`typed/QuestionInferred.roc`), as is a plant another imports
-- (`QuietDocShelf.roc`), and its name is given in snake case
-- (`question_inferred.roc`).
function plant_name(path)
  local name = sub(path, #PLANTS + 1)
  if starts_with(name, "typed/") then name = sub(name, 7) end
  if re_find(name, "^[A-Z]") ~= nil then return snake_case_plant_name(name) end
  return name
end

if SELF_TEST then
  local names = {}
  for path in paths do names[path] = plant_name(path) end
  local wrong = plants_wrong({plants = PLANTS, checks = CHECKS, paths = paths, names = names, fired = fired_in_file, census = first_word_census, findings = finding_lines})
  for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end
  if #wrong > 0 then fail("hunt_names self_test: " .. #wrong .. " plants wrong") end
  print("hunt_names (Roc) self_test: PASS (each check fires on its plants alone, the quiet_ plants on none, and the census gives each verdict its known word)")
end
