find_dead_code

The functions and generators in Shale's C that no program reaches, and those only the tests reach: every item a node, its masked words its edges, walked from each program's main and the tests.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.list!, Shale.print!, Shale.read!.
Roc: 461 lines in 3 files. Shale original: 277 lines, plus 503 lines in the library it loads, which other recipes share.

Roc

It also imports Item, Paths, Split, Words from the C splitter.

cookbook/c/find_dead_code/find_dead_code.roc, 165 lines

## find_dead_code, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md): the
## functions and generators in Shale's C that no program reaches, from the
## splitter the C recipes share (cookbook/c/items/, a package). Its
## launcher, cookbook/c/find_dead_code.shale, is how it is run, and its
## header says the arguments and the rules. check_goldens.shale, beside
## this, holds its output on the plants to its goldens, line for line.
##
##   shale cookbook:c/find_dead_code.shale dir=c/host
##   shale cookbook:c/find_dead_code.shale self_test=1
##
## The effects: `Shale.arg!` for the arguments, `Shale.glob!` for the files,
## `Shale.read!` for each one's text, and `Shale.print!` and `Shale.fail!`
## for the verdict. Graph, beside this, finds what no program reaches;
## SelfTest holds it to the plants.
## budget: steps=200000000 arena_bytes=2000000000 roc_cpu_ms=600000
app [main!] {
	items: "../items/main.roc",
	pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc",
}

import pf.Shale
import items.Item
import items.Paths
import items.Split
import items.Words
import Graph
import SelfTest

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	if integer_or_stop!("self_test", Shale.arg!("self_test", "0")) == 1 {
		SelfTest.run!(find!)
	} else {
		folder = Shale.arg!("dir", "c")
		found = find!(folder)
		for each in found.findings {
			Shale.print!(Graph.finding_line(each))
		}
		for line in summary(folder, found) {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
	}
}

## A value given as `name=`, which must be an integer, as Shale's `arg` reads
## one whose default is.
integer_or_stop! : Str, Str => I64
integer_or_stop! = |name, given|
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(value) => value
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("find_dead_code: ${name}=${given} is not an integer")
			0
		}
	}

## What was found under a folder: the findings, and how many items were
## nodes.
Found : { findings : List(Graph.Finding), nodes : U64 }

## The findings over the folder.
find! : Str => Found
find! = |folder| {
	nodes = read_nodes!(folder)
	{ findings: Graph.findings(nodes), nodes: nodes.len() }
}

## The summary: the counts by rule, then by folder and rule.
summary : Str, Found -> List(Str)
summary = |folder, found| {
	rules = found.findings.fold(Dict.empty(), |counts, each| counted(counts, each.rule))
	folders = found.findings.fold(Dict.empty(), |counts, each| counted(counts, "${folder_of(each.path)} ${each.rule}"))
	parts = sorted_counts(rules).map(|(rule, count)| "${count.to_str()} ${rule}")
	counts = "${found.findings.len().to_str()} findings: ${Str.join_with(parts, ", ")}"
	head = "find_dead_code: ${found.nodes.to_str()} items under ${folder}; ${counts}"
	sorted_counts(folders).map(|(key, count)| "  ${key}: ${count.to_str()}").prepend(head)
}

## The counts with one more of `key`.
counted : Dict(Str, U64), Str -> Dict(Str, U64)
counted = |counts, key| counts.insert(key, (counts.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)

## The counts, by key in the order of their bytes.
sorted_counts : Dict(Str, U64) -> List((Str, U64))
sorted_counts = |counts| counts.to_list().sort_with(|(x, _), (y, _)| Words.byte_order(x, y))

## The folder a path is in, as Shale's `dirname` gives it: up to its last
## `/`, or "" when it has none.
folder_of : Str -> Str
folder_of = |path| {
	bytes = path.to_utf8()
	match bytes.find_last_index(|byte| byte == '/') {
		Ok(slash) => Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.take_first(slash))
		Err(_) => ""
	}
}

## The kinds of item that are nodes: each names others, or is named. A type
## is one, since a generator's type may be named only in a struct's field.
node_kinds : List(Item.Kind)
node_kinds = [Function, Test, TestList, Data, Macro, Generator, Struct, Union, Enum, Typedef]

## The kinds whose words are the whole item's text, not a body's uses.
whole_kinds : List(Item.Kind)
whole_kinds = [Data, Macro, Generator, Struct, Union, Enum, Typedef]

## The tree's nodes, one for each item of a node's kind, in file order.
read_nodes! : Str => List(Graph.Node)
read_nodes! = |folder| {
	var $nodes = []
	for path in c_files_under!(folder) {
		text = read_text!(path)
		lines = Split.lines(text)
		test = Paths.is_test_path(folder, path)
		for item in split_or_stop!(path, text) {
			if node_kinds.contains(item.kind) {
				words =
					if whole_kinds.contains(item.kind) {
						Words.uses(Split.masked_text(lines, { first: item.first, last: item.last }))
					} else {
						item.uses
					}
				node = { path, line: item.first, kind: item.kind, name: item.name, test, words, macro: item.macro, makes: item.makes }
				$nodes = $nodes.append(node)
			}
		}
	}
	$nodes
}

## The file's text. A file the glob named and the read finds gone stops the
## run.
read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("find_dead_code: ${path} went missing during the walk")
			""
		}
	}

## The file's items, each body's uses read, or the run stopped with the line
## the dialect does not account for.
split_or_stop! : Str, Str => List(Item)
split_or_stop! = |path, text|
	match Split.items({ path, text, uses: Bool.True }) {
		Ok(items) => items
		Err(why) => {
			Shale.fail!(why)
			[]
		}
	}

## The C files under the folder, sorted, any folder named `out` (c/out, the
## build's output) left out. A folder that is not there stops the run, in
## the words of the Shale original's walk: a check that can't run fails.
c_files_under! : Str => List(Str)
c_files_under! = |folder| {
	if Shale.list!(folder) == Missing {
		Shale.fail!("`walk(\"${folder}\")`: not found (FileNotFound)")
	}
	paths = Shale.glob!("${folder}/**/*.c").concat(Shale.glob!("${folder}/**/*.h"))
	paths.keep_if(|path| !(Paths.is_in_out_folder(folder, path))).sort_with(Words.byte_order)
}

cookbook/c/find_dead_code/Graph.roc, 251 lines

## The tree's names as a graph, and what no program reaches. Every
## function, test, test list, data item, macro, generator and type is a
## node; its edges are the nodes its words name. A word resolves to its own
## file's node of that name when the file has one, else to every node of
## that name in the tree, never to the node itself. A generator answers to
## its type's name and to each function its macro makes (`Ints`,
## `Ints_make`, `Ints_push`). The roots are the programs: production's each
## `main` outside the tests, the tests' each test, test list and `main` of
## theirs.
import items.Item
import items.Words

Graph := [].{

	## A node: where its item is, its kind and name, whether its file is the
	## tests', the words it names, and a generator's macro or a macro's own
	## functions (`make`, `push`).
	Node : {
		path : Str,
		line : U64,
		kind : Item.Kind,
		name : Str,
		test : Bool,
		words : List(Str),
		macro : Str,
		makes : List(Str),
	}

	## A finding: where it is, its rule (`dead` or `test_only`) and its text.
	Finding : { path : Str, line : U64, rule : Str, text : Str }

	## The findings over the nodes, sorted by place: each function (not a
	## `main`) and generator no program reaches, `dead`, and each outside
	## the tests' files that only the tests reach, `test_only`.
	findings : List(Graph.Node) -> List(Graph.Finding)
	findings = |nodes| {
		edges = edges_of(nodes, index_of(nodes))
		roots = roots_of(nodes)
		in_production = reached(edges, roots.production)
		in_tests = reached(edges, roots.tests)
		users = users_of(edges)
		var $found = []
		$at : U64
		var $at = 0
		for node in nodes {
			is_judged = (node.kind == Function and node.name != "main") or node.kind == Generator
			rule =
				if !(is_judged) or is_marked(in_production, $at) {
					""
				} else if is_marked(in_tests, $at) {
					if node.test {
						""
					} else {
						"test_only"
					}
				} else {
					"dead"
				}
			if rule != "" {
				generated =
					if node.kind == Generator {
						" (a ${node.macro} generator)"
					} else {
						""
					}
				named_by =
					match users.get($at) {
						Ok(who) if rule == "dead" => " (named only by unreached code: ${user_names(nodes, who)})"
						_ => ""
					}
				$found = $found.append({ path: node.path, line: node.line, rule, text: "${node.name}${generated}${named_by}" })
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		$found.sort_with(place_order)
	}

	## A finding's line: `path:line: rule: text`.
	finding_line : Graph.Finding -> Str
	finding_line = |found| "${found.path}:${found.line.to_str()}: ${found.rule}: ${found.text}"
}

## The names to their nodes, each node's place counted from 0: `by_name`
## every node of a name, `by_file` a file's own node of it (the last, when
## the file has two).
Index : { by_name : Dict(Str, List(U64)), by_file : Dict((Str, Str), U64) }

## The names each node answers to, indexed: its own, and a generator's
## functions. A test list answers to none: its name is its macro's
## (`TEST_MAIN`), and a list is a root.
index_of : List(Graph.Node) -> Index
index_of = |nodes| {
	makes = nodes.fold(
		Dict.empty(),
		|so_far, node|
			if node.kind == Macro {
				so_far.insert(node.name, node.makes)
			} else {
				so_far
			},
	)
	var $by_name = Dict.empty()
	var $by_file = Dict.empty()
	$at : U64
	var $at = 0
	for node in nodes {
		if node.name != "" and node.kind != TestList {
			made =
				if node.kind == Generator {
					(makes.get(node.macro) ?? []).map(|suffix| "${node.name}_${suffix}")
				} else {
					[]
				}
			for name in made.prepend(node.name) {
				$by_name = $by_name.insert(name, ($by_name.get(name) ?? []).append($at))
				$by_file = $by_file.insert((node.path, name), $at)
			}
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	{ by_name: $by_name, by_file: $by_file }
}

## Each node's edges, the nodes its words resolve to, in its words' order.
edges_of : List(Graph.Node), Index -> List(List(U64))
edges_of = |nodes, index|
	nodes.map_with_index(|node, at| node.words.fold([], |out, word| out.concat(resolved(index, { node, at, word }))))

## The nodes a word of the node at `at` resolves to: its file's own of that
## name, else every one of it, never the node itself.
resolved : Index, { node : Graph.Node, at : U64, word : Str } -> List(U64)
resolved = |index, { node, at, word }| {
	named =
		match index.by_file.get((node.path, word)) {
			Ok(own) => [own]
			Err(_) => index.by_name.get(word) ?? []
		}
	named.keep_if(|target| target != at)
}

## The roots: production's, each `main` outside the tests; the tests', each
## test, test list and `main` of theirs.
roots_of : List(Graph.Node) -> { production : List(U64), tests : List(U64) }
roots_of = |nodes| {
	var $production = []
	var $tests = []
	$at : U64
	var $at = 0
	for node in nodes {
		if node.kind == Function and node.name == "main" {
			if node.test {
				$tests = $tests.append($at)
			} else {
				$production = $production.append($at)
			}
		} else if node.kind == Test or node.kind == TestList {
			$tests = $tests.append($at)
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	{ production: $production, tests: $tests }
}

## Which nodes the roots reach, a mark a node by its place.
reached : List(List(U64)), List(U64) -> List(Bool)
reached = |edges, roots| {
	var $marks = List.repeat(Bool.False, edges.len())
	var $work = []
	for root in roots {
		if !(is_marked($marks, root)) {
			$marks = marked($marks, root)
			$work = $work.append(root)
		}
	}
	$next : U64
	var $next = 0
	while $next < $work.len() {
		at = $work.get($next) ?? 0
		$next = $next + 1
		for target in edges.get(at) ?? [] {
			if !(is_marked($marks, target)) {
				$marks = marked($marks, target)
				$work = $work.append(target)
			}
		}
	}
	$marks
}

is_marked : List(Bool), U64 -> Bool
is_marked = |marks, at| marks.get(at) ?? Bool.False

marked : List(Bool), U64 -> List(Bool)
marked = |marks, at|
	match marks.set(at, Bool.True) {
		Ok(now) => now
		Err(_) => crash "find_dead_code: an edge past the last node"
	}

## Who names each node: a node's place to the places of the nodes whose
## edges reach it, once for each edge.
users_of : List(List(U64)) -> Dict(U64, List(U64))
users_of = |edges| {
	var $users = Dict.empty()
	$at : U64
	var $at = 0
	for out in edges {
		for target in out {
			$users = $users.insert(target, ($users.get(target) ?? []).append($at))
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	$users
}

## The names of the nodes at the places, sorted, each once, joined by `, `.
user_names : List(Graph.Node), List(U64) -> Str
user_names = |nodes, places| {
	names = places
		.map(|place| (nodes.get(place) ?? no_node).name)
		.sort_with(Words.byte_order)
	once = names.fold(
		[],
		|kept, name|
			if kept.last() == Ok(name) {
				kept
			} else {
				kept.append(name)
			},
	)
	Str.join_with(once, ", ")
}

## The node a place past the last would be, which no edge reaches.
no_node : Graph.Node
no_node = { path: "", line: 0, kind: Function, name: "", test: Bool.False, words: [], macro: "", makes: [] }

## Findings by path, in the order of their bytes, then by line.
place_order : Graph.Finding, Graph.Finding -> [Before, Same, After]
place_order = |x, y|
	match Words.byte_order(x.path, y.path) {
		Same =>
			if x.line < y.line {
				Before
			} else if x.line > y.line {
				After
			} else {
				Same
			}
		other => other
	}

cookbook/c/find_dead_code/SelfTest.roc, 45 lines

## find_dead_code's self-test: the recipe run over
## cookbook/c/plants/find_dead_code/ and held to the plants' own list of
## findings, exactly: each way to be used (a call, a pointer in a table, a
## macro, a generator's function or its type) and each near miss (a comment,
## a string, a member, a prototype, recursion, a macro nobody uses, a
## same-named helper in another test file).
import pf.Shale
import Graph

SelfTest := [].{

	## The check, a stop when it fails, then the PASS line. `find!` is the
	## recipe's own, the findings over a folder.
	run! : (Str => { findings : List(Graph.Finding), nodes : U64 }) => {}
	run! = |find!| {
		got = joined(find!(plants).findings.map(Graph.finding_line))
		want = [
			"lib.c:6: dead: Chars (a VEC_DEFINE generator)",
			"lib.c:18: dead: lib_proto_only",
			"lib.c:43: dead: lib_in_unused_macro (named only by unreached code: LIB_UNUSED_CALL)",
			"lib.c:50: dead: lib_recursive",
			"lib.c:56: dead: lib_by_dead (named only by unreached code: lib_recursive)",
			"lib.c:61: dead: lib_in_comment",
			"lib.c:66: dead: lib_member",
			"lib.c:71: test_only: lib_tested",
			"lib.h:11: dead: lib_header_dead",
			"lib.h:14: test_only: lib_header_tested",
			"test.h:14: dead: test_unused_kit",
			"tests/test_lib.c:10: dead: test_lib_stray",
			"tests/test_lib.c:16: dead: pick",
		]
		wanted = joined(want.map(|line| "${plants}/${line}"))
		if got != wanted {
			Shale.fail!("find_dead_code self-test: the plants' findings are\n${got}\nthey should be\n${wanted}")
		}
		Shale.print!("PASS find_dead_code self-test: ${want.len().to_str()} findings over the plants, exactly, and each near miss left alone")
	}
}

## Where the plants are.
plants : Str
plants = "cookbook/c/plants/find_dead_code"

joined : List(Str) -> Str
joined = |lines| Str.join_with(lines, "\n")

Shale original

cookbook/c/find_dead_code.shale, 277 lines, at 616dab12

The libraries it loads: cookbook/c/items.shale (503 lines).

-- Finds Shale's C that no program reaches, from cookbook/c/items.shale's
-- splitter. GCC's unused-function warning passes by every `static inline`
-- function (each header's and those of .c files a unit may not call), and a
-- function some other dead function calls is no warning at all, so this reads
-- the whole tree's names instead:
--
--   dead       a function, or a generator (`VEC_DEFINE(Name, T)`), that no
--              program reaches: no item names it, or only items that are
--              themselves unreached do (`named only by unreached code: ...`);
--   test_only  a function outside the tests that only tests reach.
--
-- One line a finding, `path:line: dead: name` or `path:line: test_only:
-- name`, then the counts by rule and by folder.
--
--   shale cookbook:c/find_dead_code.shale            over c/
--   shale cookbook:c/find_dead_code.shale dir=c/host
--   shale cookbook:c/find_dead_code.shale self_test=1
--
-- How it reads a use. Every function, test, test list, data item, macro and
-- generator is a node; its edges are the identifiers its masked text names
-- (items.shale's `uses` for a body, the whole item's words for data, a
-- macro and a generator), so a comment, a string and a member after `.` or
-- `->` are never a use, a prototype is none, and a name taken without a
-- call (a function pointer in a table) is one. A name resolves to its own
-- file's item of that name when the file has one (two test files may each
-- have a `pick`), else to every item of that name in the tree. A generator
-- answers to its type's name and to each function its macro `makes`
-- (`VEC_DEFINE(Ints, int)` to `Ints`, `Ints_make`, `Ints_push`), so a use of
-- `Ints_push` reaches it. A macro is reached by being named, and reaches the
-- names in its body.
--
-- The programs are the roots: each `int main(` outside a `tests` folder
-- (c/shale.c, c/shale_gate.c) is production's; each test, test list and
-- `main` under one is the tests'. A function of the tests' own files (under
-- a `tests` folder, or a file named `test*`, as c/foundation/test.h, the
-- runner) that the tests reach is a test's helper, never a finding.
--
-- What it can't see: a name made by `##` outside a generator (only
-- test.h's `TEST` and `TEST_PART` do that, and tests are roots), and a
-- use that a preprocessor branch compiles out: every branch counts.
--
-- `self_test=1` runs it over cookbook/c/plants/find_dead_code/ and holds the
-- findings to the plants' own list, exactly: each way to be used (a call, a
-- pointer in a table, a macro, a generator's function or its type) and each
-- near miss (a comment, a string, a member, a prototype, recursion, a macro
-- nobody uses, a same-named helper in another test file).
--
-- budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=1000000000 kept_bytes=268435456

use("./items.shale")

const PLANTS = "cookbook/c/plants/find_dead_code"

-- The C files under `dir`, sorted, c/out (the build's output) left out.
function c_files_under(dir)
  local files = {}
  for e in walk_all(dir, {kind = "file", skip = "out"}) do
    if ends_with(e.path, ".c") or ends_with(e.path, ".h") then push(files, e.path) end
  end
  sort(files)
  return files
end

-- Whether `p`, below `dir`, is the tests': in a `tests` folder, or a file
-- whose name starts with `test` (c/foundation/test.h, the tests' runner).
function is_test_path(dir, p)
  local rel = sub(p, #dir + 2)
  return starts_with(rel, "tests/") or contains(rel, "/tests/") or starts_with(basename(p), "test")
end

-- The kinds that are nodes: each names others, or is named. A type is one,
-- since a generator's type may be named only in a struct's field.
const NODE_KINDS = {"function", "test", "test_list", "data", "macro", "generator", "struct", "union", "enum", "typedef"}

-- The kinds whose words are the whole item's text, not a body's `uses`.
const WHOLE_KINDS = {"data", "macro", "generator", "struct", "union", "enum", "typedef"}

-- The tree's nodes, one for each item that names others or is named:
-- `{path, line, kind, name, test, words, macro}`, `test` whether its file is
-- under a `tests` folder.
function read_nodes(dir)
  local nodes = {}
  for p in c_files_under(dir) do
    local all = lines(read(p))
    local test = is_test_path(dir, p)
    for it in c_items(p, {uses = true}) do
      local k = it.kind
      if has_item(NODE_KINDS, k) then
        local words = it.uses
        if has_item(WHOLE_KINDS, k) then words = c_words_used(c_masked_text(all, it.first, it.last)) end
        push(nodes, {path = p, line = it.first, kind = k, name = it.name, test = test, words = words, macro = it.macro, makes = it.makes})
      end
    end
    yield()
  end
  return nodes
end

-- The names each node answers to: its own, and a generator's functions. A
-- test list answers to none: its name is its macro's (`TEST_MAIN`), and a
-- list is a root.
-- Gives `{by_name, by_file}`: a name to its nodes' indexes, and
-- `path|name` to the file's own node.
function index_nodes(nodes)
  local makes = {}
  for n in nodes do
    if n.kind == "macro" then makes[n.name] = n.makes end
  end
  local by_name = {}
  local by_file = {}
  local i = 0
  for n in nodes do
    i = i + 1
    if n.name ~= "" and n.kind ~= "test_list" then
      local names = {n.name}
      if n.kind == "generator" then
        for m in get(makes, n.macro, {}) do push(names, n.name .. "_" .. m) end
      end
      for nm in names do
        push_at(by_name, nm, i)
        by_file[n.path .. "|" .. nm] = i
      end
    end
  end
  return {by_name = by_name, by_file = by_file}
end

-- Each node's edges, the nodes its words resolve to (never itself).
function resolve_edges(nodes, index)
  local edges = {}
  local i = 0
  for n in nodes do
    i = i + 1
    local out = {}
    for w in n.words do
      local own = n.path .. "|" .. w
      if has_key(index.by_file, own) then
        if index.by_file[own] ~= i then push(out, index.by_file[own]) end
      else
        for t in get(index.by_name, w, {}) do
          if t ~= i then push(out, t) end
        end
      end
    end
    push(edges, out)
  end
  return edges
end

-- The nodes reached from `roots`, as a map of index strings.
function reach(edges, roots)
  local seen = {}
  local work = {}
  for r in roots do
    if not has_key(seen, "" .. r) then
      seen["" .. r] = true
      push(work, r)
    end
  end
  local next = 1
  while next <= #work do
    local at = work[next]
    next = next + 1
    for t in edges[at] do
      if not has_key(seen, "" .. t) then
        seen["" .. t] = true
        push(work, t)
      end
    end
  end
  return seen
end

-- The findings over `dir`, sorted by place: `{path, line, rule, name, text}`.
function find_dead(dir)
  local nodes = read_nodes(dir)
  local index = index_nodes(nodes)
  local edges = resolve_edges(nodes, index)
  local prod_roots = {}
  local test_roots = {}
  local i = 0
  for n in nodes do
    i = i + 1
    if n.kind == "function" and n.name == "main" then
      if n.test then push(test_roots, i) else push(prod_roots, i) end
    elseif n.kind == "test" or n.kind == "test_list" then
      push(test_roots, i)
    end
  end
  local prod = reach(edges, prod_roots)
  local tested = reach(edges, test_roots)
  -- Who names each node, for a dead one's line.
  local users = {}
  i = 0
  for out in edges do
    i = i + 1
    for t in out do push_at(users, "" .. t, i) end
  end
  local found = {}
  i = 0
  for n in nodes do
    i = i + 1
    local key = "" .. i
    if (n.kind == "function" and n.name ~= "main") or n.kind == "generator" then
      local rule = ""
      if has_key(prod, key) then
        rule = ""
      elseif has_key(tested, key) then
        if not n.test then rule = "test_only" end
      else
        rule = "dead"
      end
      if rule ~= "" then
        local text = n.name
        if n.kind == "generator" then text = text .. " (a " .. n.macro .. " generator)" end
        if rule == "dead" and has_key(users, key) then
          local who = {}
          for u in users[key] do push(who, nodes[u].name) end
          text = text .. " (named only by unreached code: " .. join(unique(sort(who)), ", ") .. ")"
        end
        push(found, {path = n.path, line = n.line, rule = rule, name = n.name, text = text})
      end
    end
  end
  sort(found, {"path", "line"})
  return {found = found, nodes = #nodes}
end

-- The findings' lines.
function finding_lines(found)
  local out = {}
  for f in found do push(out, f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ": " .. f.rule .. ": " .. f.text) end
  return out
end

function self_test()
  local got = finding_lines(find_dead(PLANTS).found)
  local P = PLANTS .. "/"
  local want = {
    P .. "lib.c:6: dead: Chars (a VEC_DEFINE generator)",
    P .. "lib.c:18: dead: lib_proto_only",
    P .. "lib.c:43: dead: lib_in_unused_macro (named only by unreached code: LIB_UNUSED_CALL)",
    P .. "lib.c:50: dead: lib_recursive",
    P .. "lib.c:56: dead: lib_by_dead (named only by unreached code: lib_recursive)",
    P .. "lib.c:61: dead: lib_in_comment",
    P .. "lib.c:66: dead: lib_member",
    P .. "lib.c:71: test_only: lib_tested",
    P .. "lib.h:11: dead: lib_header_dead",
    P .. "lib.h:14: test_only: lib_header_tested",
    P .. "test.h:14: dead: test_unused_kit",
    P .. "tests/test_lib.c:10: dead: test_lib_stray",
    P .. "tests/test_lib.c:16: dead: pick",
  }
  local g = join(got, "\n")
  local w = join(want, "\n")
  if g ~= w then fail("find_dead_code self-test: the plants' findings are\n" .. g .. "\nthey should be\n" .. w) end
  print("PASS find_dead_code self-test: " .. #want .. " findings over the plants, exactly, and each near miss left alone")
  return nil
end

if arg("self_test", 0) == 1 then
  self_test()
else
  local dir = arg("dir", "c")
  local r = find_dead(dir)
  for l in finding_lines(r.found) do print(l) end
  local rules = {}
  local folders = {}
  for f in r.found do
    incr(rules, f.rule)
    incr(folders, dirname(f.path) .. " " .. f.rule)
  end
  local parts = {}
  for k in sort(keys(rules)) do push(parts, rules[k] .. " " .. k) end
  print("find_dead_code: " .. r.nodes .. " items under " .. dir .. "; " .. #r.found .. " findings: " .. join(parts, ", "))
  for k in sort(keys(folders)) do print("  " .. k .. ": " .. folders[k]) end
end

Names in Shale's C that say too little or the wrong thing, from the splitter's items: each case rule, Zig's bound words, vague words alone, and an abbreviation the tree also spells out, its two regular expressions done by hand in their matcher's order.

Its effects: Shale.arg!, Shale.fail!, Shale.glob!, Shale.list!, Shale.print!, Shale.read!.

Roc

It also imports Item, Mask, Paths, Split, Words from the C splitter.

cookbook/c/hunt_names/hunt_names.roc, 257 lines

## hunt_names, in Roc on Shale's platform (roc_platform/README.md): Shale's C
## hunted for names that break c/docs/style.md's "Names" or say too little,
## from the splitter the C recipes share (cookbook/c/items/, a package). A
## finding is a question for a reader, never a verdict. Its launcher,
## cookbook/c/hunt_names.shale, is how it is run, and its header says the
## arguments and the checks. check_goldens.shale, beside this, holds its
## output on the plants to its goldens, line for line.
##
##   shale cookbook:c/hunt_names.shale dir=c/host
##   shale cookbook:c/hunt_names.shale self_test=1
##
## The effects: `Shale.arg!` for the arguments, `Shale.read!` for the word
## tables (cookbook/words/) and each file's text, `Shale.list!` and
## `Shale.glob!` for the files, and `Shale.print!` and `Shale.fail!` for the
## verdict. Checks, beside this, checks a file; Abbreviation, the tree's
## names; SelfTest holds it to the plants.
## budget: steps=200000000 arena_bytes=1000000000 roc_cpu_ms=600000
app [main!] {
	items: "../items/main.roc",
	pf: platform "../../../roc_platform/platform/main.roc",
}

import pf.Shale
import items.Item
import items.Mask
import items.Paths
import items.Split
import items.Words
import Abbreviation
import Checks
import SelfTest

main! : {} => {}
main! = |{}| {
	if integer_or_stop!("self_test", Shale.arg!("self_test", "0")) == 1 {
		SelfTest.run!(hunt!)
	} else {
		folder = Shale.arg!("dir", "c")
		hunted = hunt!(folder)
		for finding in hunted.found {
			Shale.print!(Checks.finding_line(finding))
		}
		Shale.print!(summary(folder, hunted))
		for line in by_folder(hunted.found) {
			Shale.print!(line)
		}
	}
}

## A value given as `name=`, which must be an integer, as Shale's `arg` reads
## one whose default is.
integer_or_stop! : Str, Str => I64
integer_or_stop! = |name, given|
	match I64.from_str(given) {
		Ok(value) => value
		Err(_) => {
			Shale.fail!("hunt_names: ${name}=${given} is not an integer")
			0
		}
	}

## The findings over the folder, sorted by place, and how many files it
## read.
hunt! : Str => { found : List(Checks.Finding), files : U64 }
hunt! = |folder| {
	tables = tables!({})
	files = c_files_under!(folder)
	var $found = []
	var $named = []
	for path in files {
		text = read_text!(path)
		checked = Checks.of_file(path, Split.lines(text), split_or_stop!(path, text), tables)
		$found = $found.concat(checked.found)
		$named = $named.concat(checked.named)
	}
	all = $found.concat(Abbreviation.findings($named, tables.abbreviations))
	{ found: all.sort_with(place_order), files: files.len() }
}

## Findings in the order of their path, line, check and why.
place_order : Checks.Finding, Checks.Finding -> [Before, Same, After]
place_order = |a, b| {
	by_path = Words.byte_order(a.path, b.path)
	if by_path != Same {
		by_path
	} else if a.line < b.line {
		Before
	} else if a.line > b.line {
		After
	} else {
		by_check = Words.byte_order(a.check, b.check)
		if by_check != Same {
			by_check
		} else {
			Words.byte_order(a.why, b.why)
		}
	}
}

## The line of counts: the files, the findings and each check's.
summary : Str, { found : List(Checks.Finding), files : U64 } -> Str
summary = |folder, hunted| {
	parts = Checks.check_names.map(|check| "${check} ${hunted.found.count_if(|finding| finding.check == check).to_str()}")
	"hunt_names: ${hunted.files.to_str()} files under ${folder}; ${hunted.found.len().to_str()} findings: ${Str.join_with(parts, ", ")}"
}

## The findings counted by each file's folder and check, a line each, in the
## order of `<folder> <check>`.
by_folder : List(Checks.Finding) -> List(Str)
by_folder = |found| {
	no_counts : Dict(Str, U64)
	no_counts = Dict.empty()
	counts = found.fold(
		no_counts,
		|so_far, finding| {
			key = "${folder_of(finding.path)} ${finding.check}"
			so_far.insert(key, (so_far.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)
		},
	)
	counts
		.to_list()
		.sort_with(|(a, _), (b, _)| Words.byte_order(a, b))
		.map(|(key, count)| "  ${key}: ${count.to_str()}")
}

## The path's folder, as Shale's `dirname` gives it: up to its last `/`.
folder_of : Str -> Str
folder_of = |path| {
	bytes = path.to_utf8()
	match bytes.find_last_index(|byte| byte == '/') {
		Ok(slash) => Mask.text(bytes.take_first(slash))
		Err(_) => ""
	}
}

## The word tables of cookbook/words/: vague.txt's, containers.txt's with
## `data` and `info`, and c_abbreviations.txt's.
tables! : {} => Checks.Tables
tables! = |{}| {
	containers = word_table!("containers.txt").insert("data").insert("info")
	{ vague: word_table!("vague.txt"), containers, abbreviations: abbreviation_table!({}) }
}

## A table's text. A table that is not there stops the run.
table_text! : Str => Str
table_text! = |file|
	match Shale.read!("cookbook:words/${file}") {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("hunt_names: cookbook/words/${file} is not there")
			""
		}
	}

## A line's text before its note, the `--` that starts one, trimmed.
before_note : List(U8) -> List(U8)
before_note = |line| {
	kept = match Mask.pair_from(line, ('-', '-'), 0) {
		Ok(note) => line.take_first(note)
		Err(_) => line
	}
	Mask.trimmed(kept)
}

## A word table of cookbook/words/, a word a line. A word twice, or a line of
## two, is a mistake in the table: it stops the run.
word_table! : Str => Set(Str)
word_table! = |file| {
	var $words = Set.empty()
	for line in Split.lines(table_text!(file)) {
		word = Mask.text(before_note(line))
		if word.contains(" ") or $words.contains(word) {
			Shale.fail!("hunt_names: cookbook/words/${file}: `${word}` is no single new word")
		}
		if word != "" {
			$words = $words.insert(word)
		}
	}
	$words
}

## cookbook/words/c_abbreviations.txt: an abbreviation to its word, a pair a
## line. An abbreviation twice, or a line of one word or three, stops the
## run.
abbreviation_table! : {} => Dict(Str, Str)
abbreviation_table! = |{}| {
	file = "cookbook/words/c_abbreviations.txt"
	var $table = Dict.empty()
	for line in Split.lines(table_text!("c_abbreviations.txt")) {
		words = words_in(before_note(line))
		match (words.get(0), words.get(1)) {
			(Ok(short), Ok(full)) if words.len() == 2 => {
				if $table.get(short) != Err(KeyNotFound) {
					Shale.fail!("hunt_names: ${file}: `${short}` twice")
				}
				$table = $table.insert(short, full)
			}
			_ =>
				if !(words.is_empty()) {
					Shale.fail!("hunt_names: ${file}: `${Mask.text(line)}` is no pair of an abbreviation and its word")
				}
		}
	}
	$table
}

## The words of a line, as Shale's `words` cuts them: at each run of `\s`.
words_in : List(U8) -> List(Str)
words_in = |line| {
	var $words = []
	var $at = Mask.spaces_end(line, 0)
	while $at < line.len() {
		end = match line.drop_first($at).find_first_index(Mask.is_space) {
			Ok(offset) => $at + offset
			Err(_) => line.len()
		}
		$words = $words.append(Mask.text(line.sublist({ start: $at, len: end - $at })))
		$at = Mask.spaces_end(line, end)
	}
	$words
}

## The file's text. A file the walk named and the read finds gone stops the
## run.
read_text! : Str => Str
read_text! = |path|
	match Shale.read!(path) {
		Found(text) => text
		Missing => {
			Shale.fail!("hunt_names: ${path} went missing during the walk")
			""
		}
	}

## The file's items, or the run stopped with the line the dialect does not
## account for.
split_or_stop! : Str, Str => List(Item)
split_or_stop! = |path, text|
	match Split.items({ path, text, uses: Bool.False }) {
		Ok(items) => items
		Err(why) => {
			Shale.fail!(why)
			[]
		}
	}

## The C files under the folder, sorted, any folder named `out` (c/out, the
## build's output) left out. A folder that is not there stops the run, in
## the words of the Shale original's walk: a check that can't run fails.
c_files_under! : Str => List(Str)
c_files_under! = |folder| {
	if Shale.list!(folder) == Missing {
		Shale.fail!("`walk(\"${folder}\")`: not found (FileNotFound)")
	}
	paths = Shale.glob!("${folder}/**/*.c").concat(Shale.glob!("${folder}/**/*.h"))
	paths.keep_if(|path| !(Paths.is_in_out_folder(folder, path))).sort_with(Words.byte_order)
}

cookbook/c/hunt_names/Abbreviation.roc, 68 lines

## hunt_names' `abbreviation` check, over the whole tree's top-level names: a
## name with a word of cookbook/words/c_abbreviations.txt whose spelled-out
## word another top-level name of the tree uses is one thing with two
## spellings (`bi_split` beside `builtin_scan`). One finding a file and
## abbreviation, at its first name's line, naming its names, as
## cookbook/c/hunt_names.shale, the Shale original, words it.
import Checks

Abbreviation := [].{

	## The tree's findings, from its names in the order the files and their
	## items gave them, and the table of each abbreviation's word.
	findings : List(Checks.Named), Dict(Str, Str) -> List(Checks.Finding)
	findings = |named, table| {
		spelled = named.fold(Set.empty(), |words, each| each.words.fold(words, |all, word| all.insert(word)))
		var $short = Dict.empty()
		for each in named {
			for word in distinct(each.words) {
				match table.get(word) {
					Ok(full) if spelled.contains(full) => {
						key = "${each.path}|${word}"
						entry = $short.get(key) ?? { path: each.path, line: each.line, word, full, names: [] }
						$short = $short.insert(key, { ..entry, names: entry.names.append(each.name) })
					}
					_ => {}
				}
			}
		}
		$short.to_list().map(|(_, entry)| finding(entry))
	}
}

## One file's abbreviation: where it is first, the word and its spelled-out
## word, and the names that hold it.
Short : { path : Str, line : U64, word : Str, full : Str, names : List(Str) }

## The finding of a file's abbreviation: its first four names, and how many
## more.
finding : Short -> Checks.Finding
finding = |entry| {
	names = distinct(entry.names)
	listed = "`${Str.join_with(names.take_first(4), "`, `")}`"
	shown = if names.len() > 4 {
		"${listed} and ${(names.len() - 4).to_str()} more"
	} else {
		listed
	}
	count = if names.len() == 1 {
		"1 name"
	} else {
		"${names.len().to_str()} names"
	}
	why = "`${entry.word}` for `${entry.full}`, which other names spell out, in ${count} here: ${shown}"
	{ path: entry.path, line: entry.line, check: "abbreviation", why }
}

## Each text once, in the order first seen, as Shale's `unique` gives them.
distinct : List(Str) -> List(Str)
distinct = |texts|
	texts.fold(
		[],
		|seen, text|
			if seen.contains(text) {
				seen
			} else {
				seen.append(text)
			},
	)

cookbook/c/hunt_names/Checks.roc, 243 lines

## hunt_names' checks of one file, every one but `abbreviation`, which needs
## the whole tree's names: a type's, a function's and a constant's case, a
## bound's words and their order, a vague function or type, `do`, and a
## vague local or parameter. The file comes split by the C recipes'
## splitter (cookbook/c/items/); each check is cookbook/c/hunt_names.shale's,
## the Shale original's, and its words are the original's.
import items.Item
import items.Mask
import items.Split
import Declared
import Names

Checks := [].{

	## A finding: its file and line, its check and why it is one.
	Finding : { path : Str, line : U64, check : Str, why : Str }

	## A top-level name the file declares, at its item's first line, with its
	## words, for `abbreviation`.
	Named : { path : Str, line : U64, name : Str, words : List(Str) }

	## The word tables the checks read: cookbook/words/vague.txt's,
	## containers.txt's (and `data`, `info`), and c_abbreviations.txt's, an
	## abbreviation to its word.
	Tables : { vague : Set(Str), containers : Set(Str), abbreviations : Dict(Str, Str) }

	## The checks, in the order the counts give them.
	check_names : List(Str)
	check_names = ["type_case", "function_case", "constant_case", "zig_bound", "bound_order", "vague", "do_word", "vague_local", "container_type", "abbreviation"]

	## A finding's line: `path:line: check: why`.
	finding_line : Checks.Finding -> Str
	finding_line = |finding| "${finding.path}:${finding.line.to_str()}: ${finding.check}: ${finding.why}"

	## The file's findings by every check but `abbreviation`, and its
	## top-level names, in the order of its items.
	of_file : Str, List(List(U8)), List(Item), Checks.Tables -> { found : List(Checks.Finding), named : List(Checks.Named) }
	of_file = |path, lines, items, tables| {
		var $found = []
		var $names = []
		for item in items {
			opening = lines.get(item.first - 1) ?? []
			type = type_checks(item, opening, tables)
			constants = constant_checks(item)
			function = function_checks(lines, item, tables)
			$found = $found.concat(type.found).concat(constants.found).concat(function.found)
			named_here = type.names.concat(constants.names).concat(other_names(item)).concat(function.names)
			$names = $names.concat(named_here.map(|name| { name, line: item.first }))
		}
		finding = |each| { path, line: each.line, check: each.check, why: each.why }
		named = |each| { path, line: each.line, name: each.name, words: Names.words_of(each.name) }
		{ found: $found.map(finding), named: $names.map(named) }
	}
}

## A finding before its file is known: its line, its check and why.
Found : { line : U64, check : Str, why : Str }

## What a check makes of an item: its findings, and the names it declares.
Checked : { found : List(Found), names : List(Str) }

## The names a local or a parameter says nothing with.
vague_locals : List(Str)
vague_locals = ["data", "info", "tmp", "temp", "stuff", "thing", "things", "misc", "util", "helper", "obj", "handle"]

## A function's lone word that is an entry point's, never vague alone.
entry_words : List(Str)
entry_words = ["run", "handle"]

## A unit a bound's name may end with, after its `MAX` or `MIN`.
units : List(Str)
units = ["MS", "NS", "US", "S", "BYTES"]

## Whether there are words and every one of them is in the table.
is_only : List(Str), Set(Str) -> Bool
is_only = |words, table| !(words.is_empty()) and words.all(|word| table.contains(word))

## A type's checks: a struct, union, typedef or enum, but no anonymous enum
## (its first constant its name, and no `typedef` opening it), which is
## constants, not a type.
type_checks : Item, List(U8), Checks.Tables -> Checked
type_checks = |item, opening, tables| {
	is_type = item.kind == Struct or item.kind == Union or item.kind == Typedef or item.kind == Enum
	is_anonymous = item.kind == Enum and item.enumerators.first() == Ok(item.name) and !(opening.starts_with("typedef".to_utf8()))
	if is_type and !(is_anonymous) {
		name = item.name
		case = if Names.is_pascal_case(name) {
			[]
		} else {
			[{ line: item.first, check: "type_case", why: "the type `${name}` is not PascalCase" }]
		}
		container = if is_only(Names.words_of(name), tables.containers) {
			[{ line: item.first, check: "container_type", why: "the type `${name}` is only container words: name it for what it holds" }]
		} else {
			[]
		}
		{ found: case.concat(container), names: [name] }
	} else {
		{ found: [], names: [] }
	}
}

## A constant's checks: each of an enum's constants, and a macro named in
## UPPER_SNAKE: its case, Zig's bound words, and a bound not last.
constant_checks : Item -> Checked
constant_checks = |item| {
	macro = if item.kind == Macro and Names.is_upper_snake(item.name) {
		[item.name]
	} else {
		[]
	}
	constants = item.enumerators.concat(macro)
	cased =
		item.enumerators
			.keep_if(|constant| !(Names.is_upper_snake(constant)))
			.map(|constant| { line: item.first, check: "constant_case", why: "the constant `${constant}` is not UPPER_SNAKE" })
	bounds = constants.fold([], |found, constant| found.concat(bound_checks(item.first, constant)))
	{ found: cased.concat(bounds), names: constants }
}

## A constant's bound checks: `MOST` or `LEAST` among its words, and its
## first `MAX` or `MIN` before its last word, unless a unit alone follows it.
bound_checks : U64, Str -> List(Found)
bound_checks = |line, constant| {
	words = constant.split_on("_")
	zig = if words.contains("MOST") or words.contains("LEAST") {
		[{ line, check: "zig_bound", why: "`${constant}` is a bound in Zig's words: C's are `_MAX` and `_MIN`" }]
	} else {
		[]
	}
	count = words.len()
	last_word = words.last() ?? ""
	is_misplaced = |(at, word)|
		(word == "MAX" or word == "MIN") and at + 1 < count and !(at + 2 == count and units.contains(last_word))
	order =
		match words.map_with_index(|word, at| (at, word)).find_first(is_misplaced) {
			Ok((at, word)) => {
				moved = words.drop_at(at).append(word)
				why = "`${constant}` has `${word}` before its last word: a bound ends with it, as `${Str.join_with(moved, "_")}` would"
				[{ line, check: "bound_order", why }]
			}
			Err(_) => []
		}
	zig.concat(order)
}

## The names of a macro not in UPPER_SNAKE and of named data, which no
## check reads but `abbreviation`.
other_names : Item -> List(Str)
other_names = |item|
	if item.kind == Macro and !(Names.is_upper_snake(item.name)) {
		[item.name]
	} else if item.kind == Data and item.name != "" {
		[item.name]
	} else {
		[]
	}

## A function's checks: its case (`main` aside), vague words alone, `do`,
## and its vague parameters and locals.
function_checks : List(List(U8)), Item, Checks.Tables -> Checked
function_checks = |lines, item, tables| {
	if item.kind != Function {
		return { found: [], names: [] }
	}
	name = item.name
	at = item.first
	case = if name == "main" or Names.is_snake_case(name) {
		[]
	} else {
		[{ line: at, check: "function_case", why: "the function `${name}` is not snake_case" }]
	}
	words = Names.words_of(name)
	is_entry = words.len() == 1 and words.all(|word| entry_words.contains(word))
	vague = if is_only(words, tables.vague) and !(is_entry) {
		[{ line: at, check: "vague", why: "`${name}` is only vague words: what does it act on, and how?" }]
	} else {
		[]
	}
	do_word = if name.split_on("_").contains("do") {
		[{ line: at, check: "do_word", why: "`${name}` has `do` in it, which says only that it acts: name the act" }]
	} else {
		[]
	}
	parameters =
		Declared.parameters(head_of(lines, item))
			.keep_if(|parameter| vague_locals.contains(parameter))
			.map(|parameter| { line: at, check: "vague_local", why: "`${name}`'s parameter `${parameter}` says nothing of what it holds" })
	{ found: case.concat(vague).concat(do_word).concat(parameters).concat(vague_body_locals(lines, item)), names: [name] }
}

## A function's head, masked, each run of `\s` one space; a head that shares
## its line with the body ends before the body's `{`.
head_of : List(List(U8)), Item -> List(U8)
head_of = |lines, item| {
	head = spaces_made_one(Split.masked_text(lines, { first: item.sig_first, last: item.sig_last }))
	if item.body_first == item.sig_last {
		match Mask.byte_from(head, '{', 0) {
			Ok(brace) => head.take_first(brace)
			Err(_) => head
		}
	} else {
		head
	}
}

## The vague locals a function's body declares, a finding at each one's
## line: a body below its head, each line masked.
vague_body_locals : List(List(U8)), Item -> List(Found)
vague_body_locals = |lines, item| {
	if item.body_first == 0 or item.body_first == item.sig_last {
		return []
	}
	var $found = []
	var $at = item.body_first
	while $at <= item.body_last {
		match Declared.local(Mask.masked(lines.get($at - 1) ?? [])) {
			Ok(local) if vague_locals.contains(local) => {
				why = "`${item.name}`'s local `${local}` says nothing of what it holds"
				$found = $found.append({ line: $at, check: "vague_local", why })
			}
			_ => {}
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	$found
}

## The text with each run of `\s` made one space.
spaces_made_one : List(U8) -> List(U8)
spaces_made_one = |text|
	text.fold(
		[],
		|out, byte|
			if !(Mask.is_space(byte)) {
				out.append(byte)
			} else if out.last() == Ok(' ') {
				# A space is `\s`, so one that ends `out` is a run's already.
				out
			} else {
				out.append(' ')
			},
	)

cookbook/c/hunt_names/SelfTest.roc, 71 lines

## hunt_names' self-test: the hunt run over cookbook/c/plants/hunt_names/,
## each plant named for the check it holds (`do_word.c`), each near miss in
## `quiet_<check>.c`, and the findings held to the plants' list exactly:
## every check fires on its own plant and on no other, and a quiet plant on
## none.
import pf.Shale
import Checks

SelfTest := [].{

	## Every check, a FAIL line for each that fails and then a stop, else the
	## PASS line. `hunt!` is the recipe's own, a folder's findings, sorted.
	run! : (Str => { found : List(Checks.Finding), files : U64 }) => {}
	run! = |hunt!| {
		found = hunt!(plants).found
		fired = found.map(|finding| (finding.path, finding.check))
		silent =
			Checks.check_names
				.keep_if(|check| !(fired.contains((plant_of(check), check))))
				.map(|check| "`${check}` does not fire on its plant ${plant_of(check)}")
		elsewhere =
			found
				.keep_if(|finding| finding.path != plant_of(finding.check))
				.map(|finding| "`${finding.check}` fires on ${finding.path}:${finding.line.to_str()}, not its plant")
		got = Str.join_with(found.map(Checks.finding_line), "\n")
		want = Str.join_with(wanted, "\n")
		listed = if got == want {
			[]
		} else {
			["the plants' findings are\n${got}\nthey should be\n${want}"]
		}
		wrong = silent.concat(elsewhere).concat(listed)
		for why in wrong {
			Shale.print!("FAIL ${why}")
		}
		if !(wrong.is_empty()) {
			Shale.fail!("hunt_names self-test: ${wrong.len().to_str()} wrong")
		}
		checks = "${Checks.check_names.len().to_str()} checks, each firing on its own plant alone"
		Shale.print!("PASS hunt_names self-test: ${checks}, ${wanted.len().to_str()} findings exactly, the quiet plants on none")
	}
}

## Where the plants are.
plants : Str
plants = "cookbook/c/plants/hunt_names"

## The plant a check fires on.
plant_of : Str -> Str
plant_of = |check| "${plants}/${check}.c"

## The plants' findings, every one, in order.
wanted : List(Str)
wanted = {
	p = "${plants}/"
	[
		"${p}abbreviation.c:4: abbreviation: `bi` for `builtin`, which other names spell out, in 1 name here: `bi_length`",
		"${p}bound_order.c:4: bound_order: `BOUND_MAX_NAME` has `MAX` before its last word: a bound ends with it, as `BOUND_NAME_MAX` would",
		"${p}constant_case.c:4: constant_case: the constant `constant_wrong` is not UPPER_SNAKE",
		"${p}container_type.c:4: container_type: the type `Entry` is only container words: name it for what it holds",
		"${p}container_type.c:8: container_type: the type `NodeInfo` is only container words: name it for what it holds",
		"${p}do_word.c:4: do_word: `store_do_write` has `do` in it, which says only that it acts: name the act",
		"${p}function_case.c:4: function_case: the function `readThing` is not snake_case",
		"${p}type_case.c:4: type_case: the type `bad_type` is not PascalCase",
		"${p}vague.c:4: vague: `handle_data` is only vague words: what does it act on, and how?",
		"${p}vague_local.c:4: vague_local: `vague_local_sum`'s parameter `data` says nothing of what it holds",
		"${p}vague_local.c:5: vague_local: `vague_local_sum`'s local `tmp` says nothing of what it holds",
		"${p}zig_bound.c:4: zig_bound: `ZIG_BOUND_MOST` is a bound in Zig's words: C's are `_MAX` and `_MIN`",
		"${p}zig_bound.c:8: zig_bound: `ZIG_BOUND_LEAST` is a bound in Zig's words: C's are `_MAX` and `_MIN`",
	]
}

cookbook/c/hunt_names/Declared.roc, 195 lines

## The names a function declares, as hunt_names reads them from its masked
## lines: its parameters, from its head, and a body line's local. Each is a
## regular expression of cookbook/c/hunt_names.shale, the Shale original,
## done by hand, its alternatives tried in the order the expression's own
## matcher tries them, so the first match is the original's.
import items.Mask

Declared := [].{

	## The names a function's head declares as its parameters: each part's last
	## word, between the head's first `(` and its last `)`, `void` none. A
	## part's name is `(\w+)\s*(\[[^\]]*\])?\s*$`: a word, then at most one
	## `[...]`, at the part's end, so a function pointer's part has none.
	parameters : List(U8) -> List(Str)
	parameters = |head| {
		open = head.find_first_index(|byte| byte == '(')
		close = head.find_last_index(|byte| byte == ')')
		match (open, close) {
			(Ok(start), Ok(end)) if end > start => {
				inside = head.sublist({ start: start + 1, len: end - start - 1 })
				inside
					.split_on(',')
					.keep_oks(parameter_name)
					.keep_if(|name| name != "void")
			}
			_ => []
		}
	}

	## A body line's declared local, from its masked code: `Type name =`,
	## `Type *name;`, `const Type name[`, as the original's
	## `^\s*(?:const\s+|static\s+|struct\s+|unsigned\s+)*([A-Za-z_]\w*)(?:\s*\*+\s*|\s+)(?:const\s+)?\*?([a-z_]\w*)\s*(?:=|;|\[)`
	## matches it. A first word that is no type (`return x;`) declares
	## nothing.
	local : List(U8) -> Try(Str, [NoLocal])
	local = |code| {
		starts = keyword_starts(code, [Mask.spaces_end(code, 0)])
		# The `*` takes the most keywords first, then gives them back one by one.
		var $left = starts.len()
		while $left > 0 {
			$left = $left - 1
			match declared_from(code, starts.get($left) ?? 0) {
				Ok({ type_word, name }) => {
					if not_types.contains(type_word) {
						return Err(NoLocal)
					}
					return Ok(name)
				}
				Err(_) => {}
			}
		}
		Err(NoLocal)
	}
}

## A declaration's first word that is no type: `return x;` declares nothing.
not_types : List(Str)
not_types = ["return", "else", "case", "goto", "do", "sizeof", "typedef", "break", "continue"]

## The words a declaration may start with before its type, each with the
## spaces after it.
type_keywords : List(Str)
type_keywords = ["const", "static", "struct", "unsigned"]

## The bytes from `start` to `end` as text.
text_of : List(U8), U64, U64 -> Str
text_of = |bytes, start, end| Mask.text(bytes.sublist({ start, len: end - start }))

## A part of the parameters' name: the first run of `\w` whose rest is
## `\s*(\[[^\]]*\])?\s*$`. Every start inside one run leaves the same rest,
## so the leftmost match is a whole run.
parameter_name : List(U8) -> Try(Str, [NoName])
parameter_name = |part| {
	$at : U64
	var $at = 0
	while $at < part.len() {
		end = Mask.word_end(part, $at)
		if end == $at {
			$at = $at + 1
		} else if ends_part(part, end) {
			return Ok(text_of(part, $at, end))
		} else {
			$at = end
		}
	}
	Err(NoName)
}

## Whether what follows `at` is `\s*(\[[^\]]*\])?\s*$`: spaces, at most one
## `[...]`, spaces, and the part's end.
ends_part : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
ends_part = |part, at| {
	after = Mask.spaces_end(part, at)
	if after == part.len() {
		Bool.True
	} else if part.get(after) == Ok('[') {
		match Mask.byte_from(part, ']', after + 1) {
			Ok(close) => Mask.spaces_end(part, close + 1) == part.len()
			Err(_) => Bool.False
		}
	} else {
		Bool.False
	}
}

## Where the type word may start: `starts`, the first after the leading
## spaces, then after each keyword of `type_keywords` and its spaces, as
## many as follow one another.
keyword_starts : List(U8), List(U64) -> List(U64)
keyword_starts = |code, starts| {
	at = starts.last() ?? 0
	match type_keywords.find_first(|keyword| Mask.holds_at(code, at, keyword) and Mask.is_space_at(code, at + keyword.count_utf8_bytes())) {
		Ok(keyword) => keyword_starts(code, starts.append(Mask.spaces_end(code, at + keyword.count_utf8_bytes())))
		Err(_) => starts
	}
}

## The type word at `start` and the name after it: `([A-Za-z_]\w*)`, then
## `\s*\*+\s*` (tried first) or `\s+`, then the name.
declared_from : List(U8), U64 -> Try({ type_word : Str, name : Str }, [NoLocal])
declared_from = |code, start| {
	if !(Mask.is_name_start(code.get(start) ?? 0)) {
		return Err(NoLocal)
	}
	type_end = Mask.word_end(code, start)
	before_stars = Mask.spaces_end(code, type_end)
	with_stars =
		if code.get(before_stars) == Ok('*') {
			[Mask.spaces_end(code, stars_end(code, before_stars))]
		} else {
			[]
		}
	with_spaces =
		if Mask.is_space_at(code, type_end) {
			[Mask.spaces_end(code, type_end)]
		} else {
			[]
		}
	match with_stars.concat(with_spaces).keep_oks(|at| name_after(code, at)).first() {
		Ok(name) => Ok({ type_word: text_of(code, start, type_end), name })
		Err(_) => Err(NoLocal)
	}
}

## The first place at `at` or after it that is no `*`.
stars_end : List(U8), U64 -> U64
stars_end = |code, at| {
	var $end = at
	while code.get($end) == Ok('*') {
		$end = $end + 1
	}
	$end
}

## The name after a declaration's type and its stars:
## `(?:const\s+)?\*?([a-z_]\w*)\s*(?:=|;|\[)`, each optional part taken
## first, then left.
name_after : List(U8), U64 -> Try(Str, [NoLocal])
name_after = |code, at| {
	keyword_end = at + 5
	after_const =
		if Mask.holds_at(code, at, "const") and Mask.is_space_at(code, keyword_end) {
			[Mask.spaces_end(code, keyword_end)]
		} else {
			[]
		}
	starts = after_const.concat([at]).fold(
		[],
		|tried, place|
			if code.get(place) == Ok('*') {
				tried.concat([place + 1, place])
			} else {
				tried.append(place)
			},
	)
	match starts.keep_oks(|start| name_at(code, start)).first() {
		Ok(name) => Ok(name)
		Err(_) => Err(NoLocal)
	}
}

## The name at `start`, `[a-z_]\w*`, when `\s*` then `=`, `;` or `[`
## follows it.
name_at : List(U8), U64 -> Try(Str, [NoLocal])
name_at = |code, start| {
	first = code.get(start) ?? 0
	if !((first >= 'a' and first <= 'z') or first == '_') {
		return Err(NoLocal)
	}
	end = Mask.word_end(code, start)
	match code.get(Mask.spaces_end(code, end)) {
		Ok(byte) if byte == '=' or byte == ';' or byte == '[' => Ok(text_of(code, start, end))
		_ => Err(NoLocal)
	}
}

cookbook/c/hunt_names/Names.roc, 72 lines

## The words and the cases of a C name, as hunt_names reads them: the
## regular expressions of cookbook/c/hunt_names.shale, the Shale original,
## done by hand over the name's bytes. A name of Shale's C is ASCII, and a
## byte past it is in no class here.
Names := [].{

	## A C name's words, lower case: `NodeInfo`, `node_info` and `NODE_INFO`
	## all `[node, info]`. A `_` goes between a lower-case letter or a digit
	## and the capital after it (`([a-z0-9])([A-Z])`), then the name is cut at
	## each `_`, an empty word left out.
	words_of : Str -> List(Str)
	words_of = |name| {
		bytes = name.to_utf8()
		var $spelled = []
		$at : U64
		var $at = 0
		while $at < bytes.len() {
			byte = bytes.get($at) ?? 0
			$spelled = $spelled.append(lowered(byte))
			next = bytes.get($at + 1) ?? 0
			if (is_lower(byte) or is_digit(byte)) and is_upper(next) {
				$spelled = $spelled.append('_')
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		$spelled.split_on('_').keep_if(|word| !(word.is_empty())).map(|word| Str.from_utf8_lossy(word))
	}

	## Whether the name is `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`: a type's PascalCase.
	is_pascal_case : Str -> Bool
	is_pascal_case = |name|
		is_shaped(name, is_upper, |byte| is_upper(byte) or is_lower(byte) or is_digit(byte))

	## Whether the name is `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`: a function's snake_case.
	is_snake_case : Str -> Bool
	is_snake_case = |name|
		is_shaped(name, is_lower, |byte| is_lower(byte) or is_digit(byte) or byte == '_')

	## Whether the name is `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`: a constant's UPPER_SNAKE.
	is_upper_snake : Str -> Bool
	is_upper_snake = |name|
		is_shaped(name, is_upper, |byte| is_upper(byte) or is_digit(byte) or byte == '_')
}

## Whether the name's first byte is `first`'s and every byte after it is
## `rest`'s, an empty name being neither.
is_shaped : Str, (U8 -> Bool), (U8 -> Bool) -> Bool
is_shaped = |name, first, rest| {
	bytes = name.to_utf8()
	match bytes.first() {
		Ok(byte) => first(byte) and bytes.drop_first(1).all(rest)
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}
}

is_upper : U8 -> Bool
is_upper = |byte| byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z'

is_lower : U8 -> Bool
is_lower = |byte| byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z'

is_digit : U8 -> Bool
is_digit = |byte| byte >= '0' and byte <= '9'

## The byte lower case, as Shale's `lower` makes it: ASCII alone.
lowered : U8 -> U8
lowered = |byte|
	if is_upper(byte) {
		byte + 32
	} else {
		byte
	}

Shale original

The libraries it loads: cookbook/c/items.shale (503 lines).

-- Hunts Shale's C for names that break c/docs/style.md's "Names" or say
-- too little, from cookbook/c/items.shale's splitter. A finding is a
-- question for a reader, never a verdict. The first version is small, each
-- check narrow enough that its findings are worth reading:
--
--   type_case       a type (a struct, union, typedef or tagged enum) not
--                   `PascalCase`; an anonymous enum is constants, no type
--   function_case   a function not `snake_case`
--   constant_case   an enum's constant not `UPPER_SNAKE`
--   zig_bound       a constant or macro with Zig's bound words, `MOST` or
--                   `LEAST`: C's are `_MAX` and `_MIN`
--   bound_order     a constant or macro whose `MAX` or `MIN` is not its last
--                   word (`STORE_MAX_NAME`, not `STORE_NAME_MAX`), a unit
--                   after it (`_MS`, `_BYTES`) left alone
--   vague           a function named of nothing but cookbook/words/vague.txt's
--                   words (`handle_data`); a lone `run` or `handle` is an
--                   entry point's, and a piece's noun before a vague word
--                   (`json_value`, `vm_run`) is no finding
--   do_word         a function with the word `do` in its name, which says
--                   only that it acts
--   vague_local     a local or parameter named only `data`, `info`, `tmp`,
--                   `temp`, `stuff`, `thing`, `things`, `misc`, `util`,
--                   `helper`, `obj` or `handle`
--   container_type  a type named of nothing but container words
--                   (cookbook/words/containers.txt, and `data`, `info`):
--                   `Entry`, `NodeInfo`; a type is named for what it holds
--   abbreviation    a top-level name with a word of
--                   cookbook/words/c_abbreviations.txt whose spelled-out
--                   word another top-level name of the tree uses: one thing,
--                   two spellings (`bi_split` beside `builtin_scan`); one
--                   finding a file and abbreviation, naming its names
--
-- One line a finding, `path:line: check: why`, then the counts by check and
-- by folder.
--
--   shale cookbook:c/hunt_names.shale             over c/
--   shale cookbook:c/hunt_names.shale dir=c/host
--   shale cookbook:c/hunt_names.shale self_test=1
--
-- `self_test=1` runs it over cookbook/c/plants/hunt_names/, each plant named
-- for the check it holds (`do_word.c`), each near miss in `quiet_<check>.c`,
-- and holds the findings to the plants' list exactly: every check fires on
-- its own plant and on no other, and a quiet plant on none.
--
-- budget: steps=400000000 arena_bytes=1000000000 kept_bytes=268435456

use("./items.shale")

const PLANTS = "cookbook/c/plants/hunt_names"
const CHECKS = {"type_case", "function_case", "constant_case", "zig_bound", "bound_order", "vague", "do_word", "vague_local", "container_type", "abbreviation"}
const VAGUE_LOCALS = {"data", "info", "tmp", "temp", "stuff", "thing", "things", "misc", "util", "helper", "obj", "handle"}
const ENTRY = {"run", "handle"}
-- A unit a bound's name may end with, after its `MAX` or `MIN`.
const UNITS = {"MS", "NS", "US", "S", "BYTES"}
-- A declaration's first word that is no type: `return x;` declares nothing.
const NOT_TYPES = {"return", "else", "case", "goto", "do", "sizeof", "typedef", "break", "continue"}

-- A word table of cookbook/words/, a word a line, `--` starting a note. A
-- word twice, or a line of two, is a mistake in the table: it fails.
function word_table(file)
  local t = {}
  for l in lines(read("cookbook:words/" .. file)) do
    local w = trim(split(l, "--")[1])
    if contains(w, " ") or has_key(t, w) then fail("hunt_names: cookbook/words/" .. file .. ": `" .. w .. "` is no single new word") end
    if w ~= "" then t[w] = true end
  end
  return t
end

-- cookbook/words/c_abbreviations.txt: an abbreviation to its word.
function abbreviation_table()
  local t = {}
  for l in lines(read("cookbook:words/c_abbreviations.txt")) do
    local ws = words(trim(split(l, "--")[1]))
    if #ws == 2 then
      if has_key(t, ws[1]) then fail("hunt_names: cookbook/words/c_abbreviations.txt: `" .. ws[1] .. "` twice") end
      t[ws[1]] = ws[2]
    elseif #ws ~= 0 then
      fail("hunt_names: cookbook/words/c_abbreviations.txt: `" .. l .. "` is no pair of an abbreviation and its word")
    end
  end
  return t
end

-- The C files under `dir`, sorted, c/out (the build's output) left out.
function c_files_under(dir)
  local files = {}
  for e in walk_all(dir, {kind = "file", skip = "out"}) do
    if ends_with(e.path, ".c") or ends_with(e.path, ".h") then push(files, e.path) end
  end
  sort(files)
  return files
end

-- A C name's words, lower case: `NodeInfo`, `node_info` and `NODE_INFO` all
-- `{node, info}`.
function words_of(name)
  local s = re_replace(name, "([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", "\\1_\\2")
  local got = {}
  for w in split(lower(s), "_") do
    if w ~= "" then push(got, w) end
  end
  return got
end

-- Every word of every table in `t`.
function all_in(ws, t)
  if #ws == 0 then return false end
  for w in ws do
    if not has_key(t, w) then return false end
  end
  return true
end

-- The names a function's head declares as its parameters: each part's last
-- word, between the head's first `(` and its last `)`.
function param_names(head)
  local open = find(head, "(")
  local close = nil
  local k = #head
  while k > 0 and close == nil do
    if sub(head, k, k) == ")" then close = k end
    k = k - 1
  end
  if open == nil or close == nil or close <= open then return {} end
  local names = {}
  for part in split(sub(head, open + 1, close - 1), ",") do
    local m = re_find(part, [=[(\w+)\s*(\[[^\]]*\])?\s*$]=])
    if m ~= nil and m.groups[1] ~= "void" then push(names, m.groups[1]) end
  end
  return names
end

-- A body line's declared local, or nil: `Type name =`, `Type *name;`,
-- `const Type name[`.
const DECL = [=[^\s*(?:const\s+|static\s+|struct\s+|unsigned\s+)*([A-Za-z_]\w*)(?:\s*\*+\s*|\s+)(?:const\s+)?\*?([a-z_]\w*)\s*(?:=|;|\[)]=]

function local_of(code)
  local m = re_find(code, DECL)
  if m == nil or has_item(NOT_TYPES, m.groups[1]) then return nil end
  return m.groups[2]
end

-- What the hunt reads of one file: its findings by every check but
-- `abbreviation`, and its top-level names `{name, line, words}` for that
-- check, which needs the whole tree's.
function hunt_file(p, tables)
  local all = lines(read(p))
  local found = {}
  local named = {}
  for it in c_items(p) do
    local k = it.kind
    local anonymous = k == "enum" and #it.enumerators > 0 and it.enumerators[1] == it.name and not starts_with(all[it.first], "typedef")
    if (k == "struct" or k == "union" or k == "typedef" or k == "enum") and not anonymous then
      if not re_match(it.name, "^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$") then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "type_case", why = "the type `" .. it.name .. "` is not PascalCase"}) end
      if all_in(words_of(it.name), tables.containers) then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "container_type", why = "the type `" .. it.name .. "` is only container words: name it for what it holds"}) end
      push(named, {name = it.name, line = it.first})
    end
    local constants = {}
    for en in it.enumerators do push(constants, en) end
    if k == "macro" and re_match(it.name, "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$") then push(constants, it.name) end
    for en in it.enumerators do
      if not re_match(en, "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$") then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "constant_case", why = "the constant `" .. en .. "` is not UPPER_SNAKE"}) end
    end
    for c in constants do
      local ws = split(c, "_")
      if has_item(ws, "MOST") or has_item(ws, "LEAST") then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "zig_bound", why = "`" .. c .. "` is a bound in Zig's words: C's are `_MAX` and `_MIN`"}) end
      local j = 1
      while j < #ws do
        if (ws[j] == "MAX" or ws[j] == "MIN") and not (j == #ws - 1 and has_item(UNITS, ws[#ws])) then
          local moved = {}
          local x = 1
          while x <= #ws do
            if x ~= j then push(moved, ws[x]) end
            x = x + 1
          end
          push(moved, ws[j])
          push(found, {line = it.first, check = "bound_order", why = "`" .. c .. "` has `" .. ws[j] .. "` before its last word: a bound ends with it, as `" .. join(moved, "_") .. "` would"})
          j = #ws
        end
        j = j + 1
      end
      push(named, {name = c, line = it.first})
    end
    if k == "macro" and not re_match(it.name, "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$") then push(named, {name = it.name, line = it.first}) end
    if k == "data" and it.name ~= "" then push(named, {name = it.name, line = it.first}) end
    if k == "function" then
      local n = it.name
      push(named, {name = n, line = it.first})
      if n ~= "main" and not re_match(n, "^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$") then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "function_case", why = "the function `" .. n .. "` is not snake_case"}) end
      local ws = words_of(n)
      if all_in(ws, tables.vague) and not (#ws == 1 and has_item(ENTRY, ws[1])) then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "vague", why = "`" .. n .. "` is only vague words: what does it act on, and how?"}) end
      if has_item(split(n, "_"), "do") then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "do_word", why = "`" .. n .. "` has `do` in it, which says only that it acts: name the act"}) end
      local head = re_replace(c_masked_text(all, it.sig_first, it.sig_last), [=[\s+]=], " ")
      if it.body_first == it.sig_last then head = sub(head, 1, find(head, "{") - 1) end
      for q in param_names(head) do
        if has_item(VAGUE_LOCALS, q) then push(found, {line = it.first, check = "vague_local", why = "`" .. n .. "`'s parameter `" .. q .. "` says nothing of what it holds"}) end
      end
      if it.body_first ~= 0 and it.body_first ~= it.sig_last then
        local b = it.body_first
        while b <= it.body_last do
          local l = local_of(c_mask(all[b]))
          if l ~= nil and has_item(VAGUE_LOCALS, l) then push(found, {line = b, check = "vague_local", why = "`" .. n .. "`'s local `" .. l .. "` says nothing of what it holds"}) end
          b = b + 1
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return {found = found, named = named}
end

-- The findings over `dir`, sorted by place: `{path, line, check, why}`.
function hunt(dir)
  local tables = {vague = word_table("vague.txt"), containers = word_table("containers.txt"), abbreviations = abbreviation_table()}
  tables.containers["data"] = true
  tables.containers["info"] = true
  local found = {}
  local named = {}
  local files = c_files_under(dir)
  for p in files do
    local r = hunt_file(p, tables)
    for f in r.found do push(found, {path = p, line = f.line, check = f.check, why = f.why}) end
    for x in r.named do push(named, {path = p, line = x.line, name = x.name, words = words_of(x.name)}) end
    yield()
  end
  -- The words the tree's top-level names spell, for `abbreviation`.
  local spelled = {}
  for x in named do
    for w in x.words do spelled[w] = true end
  end
  -- One finding a file and abbreviation, at its first name, naming them.
  local short = {}
  local order = {}
  for x in named do
    for w in unique(x.words) do
      if has_key(tables.abbreviations, w) and has_key(spelled, tables.abbreviations[w]) then
        local key = x.path .. "|" .. w
        if not has_key(short, key) then
          short[key] = {path = x.path, line = x.line, word = w, names = {}}
          push(order, key)
        end
        push(short[key].names, x.name)
      end
    end
  end
  for key in order do
    local s = short[key]
    local names = unique(s.names)
    local shown = "`" .. join(take(names, 4), "`, `") .. "`"
    if #names > 4 then shown = shown .. " and " .. (#names - 4) .. " more" end
    local count = #names .. " names"
    if #names == 1 then count = "1 name" end
    push(found, {path = s.path, line = s.line, check = "abbreviation", why = "`" .. s.word .. "` for `" .. tables.abbreviations[s.word] .. "`, which other names spell out, in " .. count .. " here: " .. shown})
  end
  sort(found, {"path", "line", "check", "why"})
  return {found = found, files = #files}
end

-- The findings' lines.
function finding_lines(found)
  local out = {}
  for f in found do push(out, f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ": " .. f.check .. ": " .. f.why) end
  return out
end

function self_test()
  local r = hunt(PLANTS)
  local wrong = {}
  -- Every check fires on its own plant and no other; a quiet plant on none.
  local fired = {}
  for f in r.found do fired[f.path .. "|" .. f.check] = true end
  for c in CHECKS do
    local mine = PLANTS .. "/" .. c .. ".c"
    if not has_key(fired, mine .. "|" .. c) then push(wrong, "`" .. c .. "` does not fire on its plant " .. mine) end
  end
  for f in r.found do
    if f.path ~= PLANTS .. "/" .. f.check .. ".c" then push(wrong, "`" .. f.check .. "` fires on " .. f.path .. ":" .. f.line .. ", not its plant") end
  end
  local P = PLANTS .. "/"
  local want = {
    P .. "abbreviation.c:4: abbreviation: `bi` for `builtin`, which other names spell out, in 1 name here: `bi_length`",
    P .. "bound_order.c:4: bound_order: `BOUND_MAX_NAME` has `MAX` before its last word: a bound ends with it, as `BOUND_NAME_MAX` would",
    P .. "constant_case.c:4: constant_case: the constant `constant_wrong` is not UPPER_SNAKE",
    P .. "container_type.c:4: container_type: the type `Entry` is only container words: name it for what it holds",
    P .. "container_type.c:8: container_type: the type `NodeInfo` is only container words: name it for what it holds",
    P .. "do_word.c:4: do_word: `store_do_write` has `do` in it, which says only that it acts: name the act",
    P .. "function_case.c:4: function_case: the function `readThing` is not snake_case",
    P .. "type_case.c:4: type_case: the type `bad_type` is not PascalCase",
    P .. "vague.c:4: vague: `handle_data` is only vague words: what does it act on, and how?",
    P .. "vague_local.c:4: vague_local: `vague_local_sum`'s parameter `data` says nothing of what it holds",
    P .. "vague_local.c:5: vague_local: `vague_local_sum`'s local `tmp` says nothing of what it holds",
    P .. "zig_bound.c:4: zig_bound: `ZIG_BOUND_MOST` is a bound in Zig's words: C's are `_MAX` and `_MIN`",
    P .. "zig_bound.c:8: zig_bound: `ZIG_BOUND_LEAST` is a bound in Zig's words: C's are `_MAX` and `_MIN`",
  }
  local got = join(finding_lines(r.found), "\n")
  if got ~= join(want, "\n") then push(wrong, "the plants' findings are\n" .. got .. "\nthey should be\n" .. join(want, "\n")) end
  for w in wrong do print("FAIL " .. w) end
  if #wrong > 0 then fail("hunt_names self-test: " .. #wrong .. " wrong") end
  print("PASS hunt_names self-test: " .. #CHECKS .. " checks, each firing on its own plant alone, " .. #want .. " findings exactly, the quiet plants on none")
  return nil
end

if arg("self_test", 0) == 1 then
  self_test()
else
  local dir = arg("dir", "c")
  local r = hunt(dir)
  for l in finding_lines(r.found) do print(l) end
  local by = {}
  local folders = {}
  for f in r.found do
    incr(by, f.check)
    incr(folders, dirname(f.path) .. " " .. f.check)
  end
  local parts = {}
  for c in CHECKS do push(parts, c .. " " .. get(by, c, 0)) end
  print("hunt_names: " .. r.files .. " files under " .. dir .. "; " .. #r.found .. " findings: " .. join(parts, ", "))
  for k in sort(keys(folders)) do print("  " .. k .. ": " .. folders[k]) end
end
