	## list on it. No group on it stacks, since stacking any group around the
	## data, or beside it, makes `roc fmt` open every group around that one.
	is_data_line : Str, U64 -> Bool
	is_data_line = |text, width| {
		bytes = text.to_utf8()
		Bytes.width_of(bytes) > width and Packed.holds_number_list(bytes)
	}

	## Whether a group holds enough to read better stacked.
	is_big : Groups.Group, U64 -> Bool
	is_big = |group, tokens| group.items >= Stacking.stack_items and group.tokens >= tokens

	## Whether a group on its line should stack: big, no trailing comma yet,
	## not a function type's arguments, not a row of literals and not numeric
	## data. The caller asks is_data_line first, once a line.
	should_stack : Stacking.Placed, Stacking.Rule -> Bool
	should_stack = |placed, rule| {
		group = placed.group
		bytes = placed.line.to_utf8()
		if !(Stacking.is_big(group, rule.tokens)) or group.trailing or group.fn_type {
			Bool.False
		} else {
			is_row = Packed.is_literal_row({ bytes, group }, rule.width)
			!(is_row) and !(Packed.is_number_data(bytes, group))
		}
	}

	## The group on a line that the rewrite gives a trailing comma: the
	## outermost, then widest, group that should stack; or else, on a line
	## wider than `width`, the widest group of two or more items whose
	## stacking brings the line within `width`. None on a line of data.
	group_to_stack : Str, Stacking.Rule -> Try(Groups.Group, [NoGroup])
	group_to_stack = |text, rule|
		if Stacking.is_data_line(text, rule.width) {
			Err(NoGroup)
		} else {
			groups = Groups.groups_on_line(text)
			var $best = Err(NoGroup)
			if rule.tokens > 0 {
				for group in groups {
					if Stacking.should_stack({ line: text, group }, rule) {
						$best = match $best {
							Err(_) => Ok(group)
							Ok(best) =>
								if is_outer_or_wider(group, best) {
									Ok(group)
								} else {
									Ok(best)
								}
						}
					}
				}
			}
			if $best != Err(NoGroup) or Bytes.line_width(text) <= rule.width {
				$best
			} else {
				group_to_wrap(text.to_utf8(), { width: rule.width, groups })
			}
		}

	## The line with a comma after the last item of its group, before any
	## spaces that come ahead of the group's closing bracket.
	with_trailing_comma : Stacking.Placed -> Str
	with_trailing_comma = |placed| {
		bytes = placed.line.to_utf8()
		group = placed.group
		var $j = group.close - 1
		while $j > group.open and Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $j) == ' ' {
			$j = $j - 1
		}
		Str.from_utf8_lossy(
			Bytes.span(bytes, 1, $j).append(',').concat(Bytes.rest_from(bytes, $j + 1)),
		)
	}

	## The line a stacked group of the lines would be on one line, spaced as
	## `roc fmt` spaces it, or `Kept` when a line break inside it does more
	## than separate items: a blank line, or a block's statements.
	group_on_one_line : List(Str), Groups.Group -> Try(Str, [Kept])
	group_on_one_line = |source_lines, group| {
		var $joined = text_up_to_group(source_lines, group)
		var $i = group.line + 1
		while $i <= group.close_line {
			piece = Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, $i))
			before = $joined.last() ?? 0
			first = Bytes.byte_at(piece, 1)
			closes = Groups.is_closer(first) or ($i == group.close_line and first == '|')
			if piece.is_empty() {
				return Err(Kept)
			}
			after_bar = before == '|' and $i == group.line + 1
			separates = before == ',' or Groups.closer_of(before) != 0 or after_bar
			if !(separates) {
				return Err(Kept)
			}
			if closes and before == ',' {
				$joined = $joined.drop_last(1)
			}
			if before == '{' or first == '}' or (before == ',' and !(closes)) {
				$joined = $joined.append(' ')
			}
			$joined = $joined.concat(piece)
			$i = $i + 1
		}
		Ok(Str.from_utf8_lossy(with_annotation_rest(source_lines, { group, joined: $joined })))
	}

	## The stacked groups of the lines that should sit on one line, by where
	## they close. A group around one that stays on several lines can't be one
	## line itself: `roc fmt` would give it its comma back. A group whose line
	## doesn't end in its trailing comma is refused, with that line.
	groups_to_unstack : List(Str), Stacking.Rule -> Try(List(Stacking.Unstacked), [NoComma(U64)])
	groups_to_unstack = |source_lines, rule| {
		var $out = []
		var $last_kept = Err(NoGroup)
		for group in Groups.groups_in_lines(Stacking.without_targets_section(source_lines)) {
			if group.line != group.close_line {
				holds_kept = match $last_kept {
					Ok(kept) => is_inside(kept, group)
					Err(_) => Bool.False
				}
				if holds_kept or !(should_unstack(source_lines, { group, rule })) {
					$last_kept = Ok(group)
				} else {
					close_bytes = Bytes.line_of(source_lines, group.close_line)
					comma_line = if Bytes.trimmed(
						Bytes.span(close_bytes, 1, group.close - 1),
					).is_empty() {
						group.close_line - 1
					} else {
						group.close_line
					}
					comma = Bytes.trimmed_end(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, comma_line)).len()
					if Bytes.byte_at(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, comma_line), comma) != ',' {
						return Err(NoComma(comma_line))
					}
					$out = $out.append({ group, comma_line, comma })
				}
			}
		}
		Ok($out)
	}

	## The lines with the trailing comma of each of the groups taken out,
	## which `roc fmt` reads as asking for one line.
	without_trailing_commas : List(Str), List(Stacking.Unstacked) -> List(Str)
	without_trailing_commas = |source_lines, unstacked| {
		var $out = source_lines
		for found in unstacked {
			bytes = Bytes.line_of($out, found.comma_line)
			cut = Str.from_utf8_lossy(Bytes.span(bytes, 1, found.comma - 1))
			$out = $out.set(
				found.comma_line - 1,
				cut,
			) ?? crash "Stacking: a comma past the lines' end"
		}
		$out
	}

	## The lines with a platform header's `targets:` section blanked, for
	## reading groups: `roc fmt` lays that section out by itself, so a
	## rewrite that tried would never end.
	without_targets_section : List(Str) -> List(Str)
	without_targets_section = |source_lines|
		if !(source_lines.any(|text| text.contains("targets:"))) {
			source_lines
		} else {
			found = Groups.groups_in_lines(source_lines).find_first(
				|group| ends_in_targets(
					Bytes.span(
						Bytes.line_of(source_lines, group.line),
						1,
						group.open - 1,
					),
				),
			)
			match found {
				Ok(group) =>
					source_lines.map_with_index(
						|text, index|
							if index + 1 >= group.line and index + 1 <= group.close_line {
								""
							} else {
								text
							},
					)
				Err(_) => source_lines
			}
		}

	## The columns that strings' text takes up on each line of a file, from
	## its tree and its lines, by line number. A run of string text that
	## crosses a line is refused, with its line.
	string_columns_on_lines : List(Tree.Node), List(Str) -> Try(Dict(U64, U64), [CrossesLine(U64)])
	string_columns_on_lines = |nodes, source_lines| {
		var $by_line = Dict.empty()
		for node in nodes {
			if node.kind == "e-string-part" or node.kind == "p-string-text" {
				if node.line != node.end_line {
					return Err(CrossesLine(node.line))
				}
				bytes = Bytes.line_of(source_lines, node.line)
				text = if node.end_col == 0 {
					Bytes.rest_from(bytes, node.col)
				} else {
					Bytes.span(bytes, node.col, node.end_col - 1)
				}
				so_far = $by_line.get(node.line) ?? 0
				$by_line = $by_line.insert(node.line, so_far + Bytes.width_of(text))
			}
		}
		Ok($by_line)
	}
}

## Whether the text before a group ends in `targets:` and spaces, the word
## standing alone (`\btargets: *$`).
ends_in_targets : List(U8) -> Bool
ends_in_targets = |bytes| {
	var $end = bytes.len()
	while $end > 0 and Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end) == ' ' {
		$end = $end - 1
	}
	word = "targets:".to_utf8()
	if $end < word.len() {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		start = $end - word.len() + 1
		Bytes.span(
			bytes,
			start,
			$end,
		) == word and !(Bytes.is_word_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, start - 1)))
	}
}

## Whether stacked group `group` should sit on one line: not big, nothing a
## rewrite can't join, and a joined line within the width.
should_unstack : List(Str), { group : Groups.Group, rule : Stacking.Rule } -> Bool
should_unstack = |source_lines, judged| {
	group = judged.group
	rule = judged.rule
	kept = group.fixed or holds_parentheses_open(group) or Stacking.is_big(group, rule.tokens)
	if !(group.trailing) or kept {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		match Stacking.group_on_one_line(source_lines, group) {
			Ok(joined) => Bytes.line_width(joined) <= rule.width
			Err(_) => Bool.False
		}
	}
}

## Whether a group to stack is a better one than `best`: outer to it, or as
## deep and wider.
is_outer_or_wider : Groups.Group, Groups.Group -> Bool
is_outer_or_wider = |group, best| {
	wider = group.close - group.open > best.close - best.open
	group.depth < best.depth or (group.depth == best.depth and wider)
}

## Whether a group is what keeps the parentheses around it on several lines.
## They would join its line, past what group_on_one_line measures.
holds_parentheses_open : Groups.Group -> Bool
holds_parentheses_open = |group|
	group.parent.closer == ')' and group.parent.line < group.line and !(group.parent.trailing)

## Whether group `inner`, which closes before `outer`, lies inside it.
is_inside : Groups.Group, Groups.Group -> Bool
is_inside = |inner, outer|
	inner.line > outer.line or (inner.line == outer.line and inner.open > outer.open)

## The text before a group once it sits on one line. A stacked group among an
## annotation's arguments moves its line down from the annotation's, and `roc
## fmt` brings it back up with the group on one line.
text_up_to_group : List(Str), Groups.Group -> List(U8)
text_up_to_group = |source_lines, group| {
	up_to = Bytes.span(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, group.line), 1, group.open)
	above = Bytes.line_of(source_lines, group.line - 1)
	if group.line > 1 and is_annotation_line(Bytes.trimmed(above)) {
		above.append(' ').concat(Bytes.trimmed(up_to))
	} else {
		up_to
	}
}

## `joined`, the line a group would be on, with the rest of its annotation
## when the group is among an annotation's arguments: stacking such a group
## puts the arguments after it on lines of their own, and `roc fmt` brings
## them back up with it. The rest runs to the line with the annotation's
## arrow; without one, `joined` is the whole line.
with_annotation_rest : List(Str), { group : Groups.Group, joined : List(U8) } -> List(U8)
with_annotation_rest = |source_lines, at| {
	group = at.group
	opens = annotation_opens(Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, group.line)))
	follows = group.line > 1 and is_annotation_line(
		Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, group.line - 1)),
	)
	if !(opens) and !(follows) {
		return at.joined
	}
	var $rest = at.joined
	var $i = group.close_line + 1
	while $rest.last() == Ok(',') and $i <= source_lines.len() {
		piece = Bytes.trimmed(Bytes.line_of(source_lines, $i))
		if piece.is_empty() {
			return at.joined
		}
		$rest = $rest.append(' ').concat(piece)
		if holds_arrow(piece) {
			return $rest
		}
		$i = $i + 1
	}
	at.joined
}

## Whether the bytes hold `->` or `=>`.
holds_arrow : List(U8) -> Bool
holds_arrow = |bytes| {
	var $at = 1
	while $at < bytes.len() {
		byte = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at)
		if (byte == '-' or byte == '=') and Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $at + 1) == '>' {
			return Bool.True
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	Bool.False
}

## Where an annotation's name and its `!` end on a trimmed line, one past
## them: `^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!?`.
annotated_name_end : List(U8) -> Try(U64, [NoName])
annotated_name_end = |bytes| {
	first = Bytes.byte_at(bytes, 1)
	if (first >= 'a' and first <= 'z') or first == '_' {
		var $end = 2
		while Bytes.is_word_byte(Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end)) {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		if Bytes.byte_at(bytes, $end) == '!' {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		Ok($end)
	} else {
		Err(NoName)
	}
}

## Whether a trimmed line starts a function's annotation whose bare
## arguments go on past it: `^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? : .*,$`.
is_annotation_line : List(U8) -> Bool
is_annotation_line = |bytes|
	match annotated_name_end(bytes) {
		Ok(end) => Bytes.span(
			bytes,
			end,
			end + 2,
		) == [' ', ':', ' '] and bytes.len() >= end + 3 and bytes.last() == Ok(',')
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}

## Whether a trimmed line opens with a function's annotation:
## `^[a-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*!? : `.
annotation_opens : List(U8) -> Bool
annotation_opens = |bytes|
	match annotated_name_end(bytes) {
		Ok(end) => Bytes.span(bytes, end, end + 2) == [' ', ':', ' ']
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}

## The group on a line wider than the width that the rewrite stacks for its
## width alone: the widest group of two or more items, not a function type's
## arguments, whose stacking brings the line within the width.
group_to_wrap : List(U8),
{
	width : U64,
	groups : List(Groups.Group),
} -> Try(Groups.Group, [NoGroup])
group_to_wrap = |bytes, given| {
	var $best = Err(NoGroup)
	for group in given.groups {
		if group.items >= 2 and !(group.trailing) and !(group.fn_type) and stacking_fits(
			{ bytes, group },
			given.width,
		) {
			$best = match $best {
				Ok(best) if group.close - group.open <= best.close - best.open => Ok(best)
				_ => Ok(group)
			}
		}
	}
	$best
}

## Whether stacking a group brings its line within `width`, as far as the
## line itself goes: the text up to its opening bracket is one line, and its
## closing bracket and what follows it, at the line's indent, another.
stacking_fits : { bytes : List(U8), group : Groups.Group }, U64 -> Bool
stacking_fits = |at, width|
	if Bytes.width_of(Bytes.span(at.bytes, 1, at.group.open)) > width {
		Bool.False
	} else {
		is_indent = |byte| byte == ' ' or byte == '\t'
		indent_end = at.bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_indent(byte))) ?? at.bytes.len()
		indent = at.bytes.take_first(indent_end)
		Bytes.width_of(indent.concat(Bytes.rest_from(at.bytes, at.group.close))) <= width
	}

cookbook/roc/lib/Text.roc, 214 lines

## Text cut, trimmed, lowered and ordered as Shale's builtins and preludes do
## it (`lines`, `words`, `trim`, `lower`, `sub`, `split`, `between`,
## `basename`, `dirname`, `path_under`, `sort`), and a name's words as
## cookbook/roc/declared.shale splits them, so a recipe's output is its
## Shale original's, byte for byte.
Text := [].{

	## A text's lines, as Shale's `lines` splits it: a last newline ends a
	## line, and an empty text has none.
	lines : Str -> List(Str)
	lines = |text| {
		parts = text.split_on("\n")
		if text.ends_with("\n") or text == "" {
			parts.drop_last(1)
		} else {
			parts
		}
	}

	## Line `number` of `source_lines`, counted from 1. A line the file lacks
	## stops the run, as Shale's index past a list's end does.
	line_at : List(Str), U64 -> Str
	line_at = |source_lines, number|
		match source_lines.get(number - 1) {
			Ok(line) => line
			Err(_) => crash "Text.line_at: the file has no line ${number.to_str()}"
		}

	## The bytes of `text` from place `start` (counted from 0), `count` of them
	## or as many as there are, as text.
	bytes_of : Str, { start : U64, count : U64 } -> Str
	bytes_of = |text, span| {
		bytes = text.to_utf8().sublist({ start: span.start, len: span.count })
		Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes)
	}

	## The text without the spaces, tabs, carriage returns and newlines at its
	## ends, as Shale's `trim` takes them.
	trim : Str -> Str
	trim = |text| {
		bytes = text.to_utf8()
		is_kept = |byte| !(byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\r' or byte == '\n')
		match bytes.find_first_index(is_kept) {
			Ok(start) => {
				end = bytes.find_last_index(is_kept) ?? start
				Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.sublist({ start, len: end + 1 - start }))
			}
			Err(_) => ""
		}
	}

	## The text with its ASCII capitals made small, as Shale's `lower` does.
	lower : Str -> Str
	lower = |text| Str.from_utf8_lossy(text.to_utf8().map(lower_byte))

	is_capital : U8 -> Bool
	is_capital = |byte| byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z'

	is_small_letter : U8 -> Bool
	is_small_letter = |byte| byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z'

	is_digit : U8 -> Bool
	is_digit = |byte| byte >= '0' and byte <= '9'

	## The text before the first `separator`, or all of it (Shale's
	## `split(s, separator)[1]`).
	before_first : Str, Str -> Str
	before_first = |text, separator|
		match text.split_first(separator) {
			Ok(parts) => parts.before
			Err(_) => text
		}

	## The text after the last `separator`, or all of it.
	after_last : Str, Str -> Str
	after_last = |text, separator|
		match text.split_last(separator) {
			Ok(parts) => parts.after
			Err(_) => text
		}

	## Shale's `between(text, opening, closing)`: after the first `opening`,
	## before the next `closing`.
	between : Str, Str, Str -> Try(Str, [NotFound])
	between = |text, opening, closing| {
		after_opening = text.split_first(opening)?
		inside = after_opening.after.split_first(closing)?
		Ok(inside.before)
	}

	## Shale's `basename`: the path after its last `/`.
	basename : Str -> Str
	basename = |path| Text.after_last(path, "/")

	## Shale's `dirname`: the path before its last `/`, `""` (the root) when
	## it has none.
	dirname : Str -> Str
	dirname = |path|
		match path.split_last("/") {
			Ok(parts) => parts.before
			Err(_) => ""
		}

	## Shale's `path_under`: a name below a folder, spelled as every call takes
	## it: in the root (`""`, `"."`) the name, in a mount's folder (`m:`,
	## `m:.`) `m:name`, else `dir/name`.
	path_under : Str, Str -> Str
	path_under = |folder, name|
		if folder == "" or folder == "." {
			name
		} else if folder.ends_with(":") {
			"${folder}${name}"
		} else if folder.ends_with(":.") {
			"${folder.drop_suffix(".")}${name}"
		} else {
			"${folder}/${name}"
		}

	## A name's words, lowercased: split at its underscores and before each
	## capital that follows a letter or digit, so `TiltStep` and `tilt_step`
	## both give `tilt` and `step` (cookbook/roc/declared.shale's
	## `name_words`).
	name_words : Str -> List(Str)
	name_words = |name| {
		var $words = []
		var $word = []
		for byte in name.to_utf8() {
			if byte == '_' {
				$words = with_word($words, $word)
				$word = []
			} else if Text.is_capital(byte) and !($word.is_empty()) {
				$words = with_word($words, $word)
				$word = [byte]
			} else {
				$word = $word.append(byte)
			}
		}
		with_word($words, $word)
	}

	## A text's words, as Shale's `words` splits it: the runs between spaces,
	## tabs, carriage returns and newlines, none empty.
	words : Str -> List(Str)
	words = |text| {
		var $said = []
		var $word = []
		for byte in text.to_utf8() {
			if byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\r' or byte == '\n' {
				$said = with_raw_word($said, $word)
				$word = []
			} else {
				$word = $word.append(byte)
			}
		}
		with_raw_word($said, $word)
	}

	## The texts put in Shale's `sort` order, bytewise.
	sort_bytewise : List(Str) -> List(Str)
	sort_bytewise = |texts| texts.sort_with(Text.byte_order)

	## Two texts in the order of their bytes, a text before every longer one
	## it starts, as Shale's `sort` puts strings.
	byte_order : Str, Str -> [Before, Same, After]
	byte_order = |first, second| {
		pairs = List.map2(
			first.to_utf8(),
			second.to_utf8(),
			|x, y| (x, y),
		)
		match pairs.find_first(|(x, y)| x != y) {
			Ok((x, y)) =>
				if x < y {
					Before
				} else {
					After
				}
			Err(_) =>
				if first.count_utf8_bytes() < second.count_utf8_bytes() {
					Before
				} else if first.count_utf8_bytes() > second.count_utf8_bytes() {
					After
				} else {
					Same
				}
		}
	}
}

lower_byte : U8 -> U8
lower_byte = |byte|
	if Text.is_capital(byte) {
		byte + 32
	} else {
		byte
	}

## `said` with `bytes` after it as a word, as they are, when there are any.
with_raw_word : List(Str), List(U8) -> List(Str)
with_raw_word = |said, bytes|
	if bytes.is_empty() {
		said
	} else {
		said.append(Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes))
	}

## `words` with `bytes` after them as a lowercased word, when there are any.
with_word : List(Str), List(U8) -> List(Str)
with_word = |words, bytes|
	if bytes.is_empty() {
		words
	} else {
		words.append(Text.lower(Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes)))
	}

cookbook/roc/lib/Tree.roc, 169 lines

## Roc's tree of a file, as `Shale.roc_tree!` gives it, read: a node by its
## place, its attributes and kids, a type written back as Roc writes it or as
## a shape, the module a file holds, and whether the file is an app.
import Text

Tree := [].{

	## A node of Roc's tree, its fields named by the platform: `parent` and
	## `kids` are places in the tree counted from 1, the root's parent 0;
	## `depth` is how far below the root it is, and `line` is 0 for a node
	## with no span.
	Node : {
		kind : Str,
		depth : U64,
		parent : U64,
		kids : List(U64),
		line : U64,
		col : U64,
		end_line : U64,
		end_col : U64,
		attrs : List({ name : Str, value : Str }),
	}

	## The node at a place counted from 1, which the tree's own `parent` and
	## `kids` always name.
	node_at : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Tree.Node
	node_at = |nodes, place|
		if place == 0 {
			crash "Tree.node_at: the tree has no node 0"
		} else {
			match nodes.get(place - 1) {
				Ok(node) => node
				Err(_) => crash "Tree.node_at: the tree has no node ${place.to_str()}"
			}
		}

	## A node's attribute, by its name, when the tree gives it one.
	find_attribute : Tree.Node, Str -> Try(Str, [NoSuchAttribute])
	find_attribute = |node, name|
		match node.attrs.find_first(|attribute_entry| attribute_entry.name == name) {
			Ok(attribute_entry) => Ok(attribute_entry.value)
			Err(_) => Err(NoSuchAttribute)
		}

	## A node's attribute, `""` where the tree gives it none.
	attribute : Tree.Node, Str -> Str
	attribute = |node, name| Tree.find_attribute(node, name) ?? ""

	## The place of a node's kid, the kids counted from 1.
	kid_at : Tree.Node, U64 -> U64
	kid_at = |node, number|
		match node.kids.get(number - 1) {
			Ok(kid) => kid
			Err(_) => crash "Tree.kid_at: a ${node.kind} with no kid ${number.to_str()}"
		}

	## The place of a node's first kid: an apply's function, a receiver's
	## value.
	first_kid : Tree.Node -> U64
	first_kid = |node|
		match node.kids.first() {
			Ok(kid) => kid
			Err(_) => crash "Tree.first_kid: a ${node.kind} with no kids"
		}

	## The place of a node's last kid.
	last_kid : Tree.Node -> U64
	last_kid = |node|
		match node.kids.last() {
			Ok(kid) => kid
			Err(_) => crash "Tree.last_kid: a ${node.kind} with no kids"
		}

	## The kind of a node's kid, the kids counted from 1, `""` when it has no
	## such kid.
	kid_kind : List(Tree.Node), Tree.Node, U64 -> Str
	kid_kind = |nodes, node, number|
		if number == 0 {
			""
		} else {
			match node.kids.get(number - 1) {
				Ok(kid) => Tree.node_at(nodes, kid).kind
				Err(_) => ""
			}
		}

	## A dotted name's last part: `Geom.Pose` gives `Pose`.
	last_part : Str -> Str
	last_part = |name| Text.after_last(name, ".")

	## The type at `at`, as Roc writes it (cookbook/roc/declared.shale's
	## `render_type`): `List(U8)`, `{ id : U8 }`, `[A, B]`, `(U8 -> Bool)`. The
	## tree does not say which arrow a function type has, so both come out as
	## `->`.
	written_type : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Str
	written_type = |nodes, at| type_text(nodes, at, AsWritten)

	## The type at `at` as a shape: written as Roc writes it, each name cut to
	## its last part and a record's fields and a union's tags sorted, so two
	## copies of one type read alike.
	shape : List(Tree.Node), U64 -> Str
	shape = |nodes, at| type_text(nodes, at, AsShape)

	## The module a .roc file holds, by its file name: the name without its
	## last four bytes, as Shale's `module_name` cuts `.roc`.
	module_name : Str -> Str
	module_name = |path| {
		bytes = Text.basename(path).to_utf8()
		if bytes.len() > 4 {
			Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.take_first(bytes.len() - 4))
		} else {
			""
		}
	}

	## Whether the file is an app, with an `app` header.
	is_app : List(Tree.Node) -> Bool
	is_app = |nodes| nodes.any(|node| node.kind == "app")
}

## How a type is written: as the code writes it, or as a shape, its names cut
## to their last parts and its fields and tags sorted.
TypeStyle : [AsWritten, AsShape]

## The type at `at`, written in `style`.
type_text : List(Tree.Node), U64, TypeStyle -> Str
type_text = |nodes, at, style| {
	node = Tree.node_at(nodes, at)
	kind = node.kind
	name = Tree.attribute(node, "name")
	texts_of = |kids| kids.map(|kid| type_text(nodes, kid, style))
	joined = |kids| Str.join_with(texts_of(kids), ", ")
	members_joined = |kids|
		match style {
			AsWritten => joined(kids)
			AsShape => Str.join_with(Text.sort_bytewise(texts_of(kids)), ", ")
		}
	first = |{}| type_text(nodes, Tree.first_kid(node), style)
	if kind == "ty-apply" {
		"${first({})}(${joined(node.kids.drop_first(1))})"
	} else if kind == "ty-fn" {
		result = type_text(nodes, Tree.last_kid(node), style)
		"(${joined(node.kids.drop_last(1))} -> ${result})"
	} else if kind == "ty-record" {
		"{ ${members_joined(node.kids)} }"
	} else if kind == "ty-tuple" {
		"(${joined(node.kids)})"
	} else if kind == "tags" {
		members_joined(node.kids)
	} else if kind == "ty-tag-union" {
		"[${first({})}]"
	} else if kind == "anno-record-field" {
		"${name} : ${first({})}"
	} else if name != "" {
		match style {
			AsWritten => name
			AsShape => Tree.last_part(name)
		}
	} else if kind == "_" {
		"_"
	} else {
		raw = Tree.attribute(node, "raw")
		if raw != "" {
			raw
		} else {
			"(${kind})"
		}
	}
}

cookbook/roc/lib/main.roc, 11 lines

## The modules the cookbook's Roc recipes share, a package each recipe's app
## names by a relative path (`lib: "../lib/main.roc"`, then `import lib.Tree`):
## Roc's tree of a file read (Tree), what a file declares (Declarations),
## what its header dictates (Headers), text cut and ordered as Shale's
## builtins do it (Text) and a line's bytes as they read it (Bytes), a
## check's finding (Finding), roc-types' output read (RocTypes), and a
## file's bracket groups (Groups) judged by the stacking rule (Stacking), the
## packed ones apart (Packed). None reaches an effect: a recipe's own modules
## do that, through `import pf.Shale` (roc_platform/README.md, "A script may
## be several files").
package [Bytes, Declarations, Finding, Groups, Headers, Packed, RocTypes, Stacking, Text, Tree] {}
contents

The C splitter

The package the programs over Shale's C share, imported as items.X: it blanks strings and comments, then splits a file into its top-level items, each with its kind, name, lines, head and body. Each example that imports it names the modules it uses.

cookbook/c/items/Guard.roc, 81 lines

## A header's guard, framed: Split.items gives a header's items to
## Guard.framed, which makes its `#ifndef` and `#define` one item and its
## `#endif` another.
import Item

Guard := [].{

	## A header's items with its guard framed: its `#ifndef SHALE_<NAME>_H` and
	## the `#define` after it made one item, and the `#endif` that ends the file
	## another, each of kind `Guard`, named for the guard. A header without that
	## framing is an error.
	framed : Str, List(Item) -> Try(List(Item), Str)
	framed = |path, items| {
		name = file_name(path)
		stem = Str.from_utf8_lossy(name.to_utf8().drop_last(2))
		guard = "SHALE_${upper(stem)}_H"
		opening = "ifndef ${guard}"
		var $out = []
		var $is_framed = Bool.False
		var $at = 0
		while $at < items.len() {
			item = items.get($at) ?? Item.new(Directive, "", { first: 0, last: 0 })
			if !($is_framed) and item.kind == Directive and item.name == opening {
				match items.get($at + 1) {
					Ok(define) if define.kind == Macro and define.name == guard => {
						guard_item = { ..Item.new(Guard, guard, { first: item.first, last: define.last }), comment_first: item.comment_first, comment_last: item.comment_last }
						$out = $out.append(guard_item)
						$is_framed = Bool.True
						$at = $at + 2
					}
					_ => {
						why = "a guard's `#ifndef` with no `#define ${guard}` after it"
						return Err(unaccounted(path, item.first, why, "#ifndef ${guard}"))
					}
				}
			} else {
				$out = $out.append(item)
				$at = $at + 1
			}
		}
		if !($is_framed) {
			return Err(unaccounted(path, 1, "a header with no `#ifndef ${guard}`", name))
		}
		match $out.last() {
			Ok(tail) if tail.kind == Directive and tail.name == "endif" =>
				Ok($out.drop_last(1).append({ ..tail, kind: Guard, name: guard }))
			Ok(tail) => Err(unaccounted(path, tail.first, "a header whose last item is not its guard's `#endif`", tail.name))
			Err(_) => Err(unaccounted(path, 1, "a header with no `#ifndef ${guard}`", name))
		}
	}
}

## The path's last part, after its last `/`.
file_name : Str -> Str
file_name = |path| {
	bytes = path.to_utf8()
	match bytes.find_last_index(|byte| byte == '/') {
		Ok(slash) => Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes.drop_first(slash + 1))
		Err(_) => path
	}
}

## The text with its ASCII letters made capitals, as Shale's `upper` does.
upper : Str -> Str
upper = |text|
	Str.from_utf8_lossy(
		text.to_utf8().map(
			|byte|
				if byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z' {
					byte - 32
				} else {
					byte
				},
		),
	)

## The error for line `number` of the file at `path`: its place and why
## first, then what the line shows.
unaccounted : Str, U64, Str, Str -> Str
unaccounted = |path, number, why, shown|
	"${path}:${number.to_str()}: ${why}: ${shown}"

cookbook/c/items/Head.roc, 365 lines

## The readers of an item's opening line or head, each over masked bytes
## (Mask.masked), each the regular expression of cookbook/c/items.shale,
## the Shale original, done by hand: the one match a backtracking search
## would find, with its groups.
import Mask

Head := [].{

	## A head read as a function's, its return type and its name, or
	## `NoFunction` when it declares none (a variable, a function pointer, a
	## value whose `=` comes before its first `(`). Its storage and
	## `STATUS_MUST_USE` go first, then a leading `__attribute__((...))`; the
	## type is what is left before the name, `void` among them.
	function_head : List(U8) -> Try({ return_type : Str, name : Str }, [NoFunction])
	function_head = |code| {
		after_storage = code.drop_first(storage_end(code))
		head = after_storage.drop_first(attribute_end(after_storage))
		match Mask.byte_from(head, '(', 0) {
			Err(_) => Err(NoFunction)
			Ok(open) => {
				is_value = match Mask.byte_from(head, '=', 0) {
					Ok(equals) => equals < open
					Err(_) => Bool.False
				}
				before = Mask.trimmed(head.take_first(open))
				# `^(.*[\s*])([A-Za-z_]\w*)$`: the name is what follows the last
				# space or `*`.
				match before.find_last_index(|byte| Mask.is_space(byte) or byte == '*') {
					Ok(cut) if !(is_value) => {
						name = before.drop_first(cut + 1)
						return_type = Mask.trimmed(before.take_first(cut + 1))
						if is_name(name) and !(return_type.is_empty()) {
							Ok({ return_type: Mask.text(return_type), name: Mask.text(name) })
						} else {
							Err(NoFunction)
						}
					}
					_ => Err(NoFunction)
				}
			}
		}
	}

	## A `VEC_DEFINE(`, `MAP_DEFINE(` or `SLICE_TYPE(` line read as its macro,
	## the name it makes and the type it holds, or `NoGenerator` when it is
	## none or its arguments are not a name and a type:
	## `^(VEC_DEFINE|MAP_DEFINE|SLICE_TYPE)\(\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*([^)]*\S)\s*\)`.
	generator : List(U8) -> Try({ macro : Str, name : Str, held_type : Str }, [NoGenerator])
	generator = |code| {
		macros = ["VEC_DEFINE", "MAP_DEFINE", "SLICE_TYPE"]
		match macros.find_first(|macro| Mask.holds_at(code, 0, "${macro}(")) {
			Err(_) => Err(NoGenerator)
			Ok(macro) => {
				name_start = Mask.spaces_end(code, macro.count_utf8_bytes() + 1)
				name_end = Mask.word_end(code, name_start)
				comma = Mask.spaces_end(code, name_end)
				if name_end == name_start or code.get(comma) != Ok(',') {
					Err(NoGenerator)
				} else {
					held_start = Mask.spaces_end(code, comma + 1)
					match held_type_end(code, held_start) {
						Ok(held_end) => {
							name = Mask.text(code.sublist({ start: name_start, len: name_end - name_start }))
							held_type = Mask.text(code.sublist({ start: held_start, len: held_end + 1 - held_start }))
							Ok({ macro, name, held_type })
						}
						Err(_) => Err(NoGenerator)
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	## The name a data item's head declares: a function pointer's `(*name)`,
	## else the last word before its `=`, `[`, `;` or `{`, or "" for none.
	data_name : List(U8) -> Str
	data_name = |code|
		match Head.pointer_name(code, WithConst) {
			Ok(name) => name
			Err(_) => {
				is_stop = |byte| byte == '=' or byte == '[' or byte == ';' or byte == '{'
				head = match code.find_first_index(is_stop) {
					Ok(stop) => code.take_first(stop)
					Err(_) => code
				}
				trailing_word(Mask.trimmed(head))
			}
		}

	## The first function pointer's name in the text, `(*name)`, a `const`
	## before the name allowed when asked: `\(\s*\*\s*(const\s+)?(\w+)\s*\)`.
	pointer_name : List(U8), [WithConst, WithoutConst] -> Try(Str, [NoPointer])
	pointer_name = |code, consts| {
		var $at = 0
		while $at < code.len() {
			if code.get($at) == Ok('(') {
				star = Mask.spaces_end(code, $at + 1)
				if code.get(star) == Ok('*') {
					after = Mask.spaces_end(code, star + 1)
					is_const = consts == WithConst and Mask.holds_at(code, after, "const") and Mask.is_space_at(code, after + 5)
					with_const = if is_const {
						closed_word(code, Mask.spaces_end(code, after + 5))
					} else {
						Err(NoPointer)
					}
					match with_const {
						Ok(name) => return Ok(name)
						Err(_) =>
							match closed_word(code, after) {
								Ok(name) => return Ok(name)
								Err(_) => {}
							}
					}
				}
			}
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		Err(NoPointer)
	}

	## The type keyword a `typedef` or `enum` line opens with, after any
	## `typedef`: `^(typedef\s+)?(struct|enum|union)\b`.
	type_keyword : List(U8) -> [Struct, Enum, Union, NoKeyword]
	type_keyword = |code| {
		at = if Mask.holds_at(code, 0, "typedef") and Mask.is_space_at(code, 7) {
			Mask.spaces_end(code, 7)
		} else {
			0
		}
		is_keyword = |word| Mask.holds_at(code, at, word) and !(Mask.is_word_at(code, at + word.count_utf8_bytes()))
		if is_keyword("struct") {
			Struct
		} else if is_keyword("enum") {
			Enum
		} else if is_keyword("union") {
			Union
		} else {
			NoKeyword
		}
	}

	## The name a type's masked text declares last, before its closing `;`:
	## `(\w+)\s*(\[[^\]]*\])?\s*;\s*$`.
	declared_name : List(U8) -> Try(Str, [NoName])
	declared_name = |text| {
		match text.find_last_index(|byte| !(Mask.is_space(byte))) {
			Ok(semicolon) if text.get(semicolon) == Ok(';') =>
				match last_unspaced(text, semicolon) {
					Ok(before) if text.get(before) == Ok(']') => bracketed_name(text, before)
					Ok(before) if Mask.is_word_at(text, before) => Ok(word_ending_at(text, before))
					_ => Err(NoName)
				}
			_ => Err(NoName)
		}
	}

	## A named `enum`'s tag: `^enum\s+(\w+)`.
	enum_tag : List(U8) -> Try(Str, [NoTag])
	enum_tag = |code| {
		start = Mask.spaces_end(code, 4)
		end = Mask.word_end(code, start)
		if Mask.holds_at(code, 0, "enum") and Mask.is_space_at(code, 4) and end > start {
			Ok(Mask.text(code.sublist({ start, len: end - start })))
		} else {
			Err(NoTag)
		}
	}

	## A `#` line's directive and its first argument, "" for none:
	## `^#\s*(\w+)\s*(\w*)`.
	directive : List(U8) -> Try({ word : Str, argument : Str }, [NoDirective])
	directive = |code| {
		word_start = Mask.spaces_end(code, 1)
		word_end = Mask.word_end(code, word_start)
		argument_start = Mask.spaces_end(code, word_end)
		argument_end = Mask.word_end(code, argument_start)
		if code.get(0) == Ok('#') and word_end > word_start {
			word = Mask.text(code.sublist({ start: word_start, len: word_end - word_start }))
			argument = Mask.text(code.sublist({ start: argument_start, len: argument_end - argument_start }))
			Ok({ word, argument })
		} else {
			Err(NoDirective)
		}
	}

	## An `#include` line's path, from the raw line: `^#\s*include\s*["<]([^">]+)[">]`.
	include_path : List(U8) -> Try(Str, [NoPath])
	include_path = |raw| {
		keyword = Mask.spaces_end(raw, 1)
		open = Mask.spaces_end(raw, keyword + 7)
		is_open = raw.get(open) == Ok('"') or raw.get(open) == Ok('<')
		is_close = |byte| byte == '"' or byte == '>'
		is_framed = raw.get(0) == Ok('#') and Mask.holds_at(raw, keyword, "include") and is_open
		match raw.drop_first(open + 1).find_first_index(is_close) {
			Ok(length) if is_framed and length > 0 => Ok(Mask.text(raw.sublist({ start: open + 1, len: length })))
			_ => Err(NoPath)
		}
	}

	## A `TEST(name) {` line's name: `^TEST\(\s*(\w+)\s*\)\s*\{\s*$`.
	test_name : List(U8) -> Try(Str, [NoTest])
	test_name = |code| {
		start = Mask.spaces_end(code, 5)
		end = Mask.word_end(code, start)
		close = Mask.spaces_end(code, end)
		brace = Mask.spaces_end(code, close + 1)
		is_test =
			Mask.holds_at(code, 0, "TEST(")
				and end > start
				and code.get(close) == Ok(')')
				and code.get(brace) == Ok('{')
				and Mask.spaces_end(code, brace + 1) == code.len()
		if is_test {
			Ok(Mask.text(code.sublist({ start, len: end - start })))
		} else {
			Err(NoTest)
		}
	}

	## A test list's macro and its first argument, "" for none:
	## `^(\w+)\(\s*(\w*)`, of a line that starts with the macro and `(`.
	test_list : List(U8) -> { macro : Str, argument : Str }
	test_list = |code| {
		macro_end = Mask.word_end(code, 0)
		argument_start = Mask.spaces_end(code, macro_end + 1)
		argument_end = Mask.word_end(code, argument_start)
		{
			macro: Mask.text(code.take_first(macro_end)),
			argument: Mask.text(code.sublist({ start: argument_start, len: argument_end - argument_start })),
		}
	}
}

## Where `^static\s+(inline\s+)?(STATUS_MUST_USE\s+)?` ends, or 0.
storage_end : List(U8) -> U64
storage_end = |code|
	if Mask.holds_at(code, 0, "static") and Mask.is_space_at(code, 6) {
		after_static = Mask.spaces_end(code, 6)
		after_inline = word_and_spaces_end(code, after_static, "inline")
		word_and_spaces_end(code, after_inline, "STATUS_MUST_USE")
	} else {
		0
	}

## Past `word\s+` at `at`, or `at` when it is not there.
word_and_spaces_end : List(U8), U64, Str -> U64
word_and_spaces_end = |code, at, word| {
	after = at + word.count_utf8_bytes()
	if Mask.holds_at(code, at, word) and Mask.is_space_at(code, after) {
		Mask.spaces_end(code, after)
	} else {
		at
	}
}

## Where `^__attribute__\(\([\w\s,]*\)\)\s+` ends, or 0.
attribute_end : List(U8) -> U64
attribute_end = |code| {
	is_inside = |byte| Mask.is_word(byte) or Mask.is_space(byte) or byte == ','
	inside_start = 15
	inside_end = match code.drop_first(inside_start).find_first_index(|byte| !(is_inside(byte))) {
		Ok(length) => inside_start + length
		Err(_) => code.len()
	}
	is_attribute =
		Mask.holds_at(code, 0, "__attribute__((")
			and Mask.holds_at(code, inside_end, "))")
			and Mask.is_space_at(code, inside_end + 2)
	if is_attribute {
		Mask.spaces_end(code, inside_end + 2)
	} else {
		0
	}
}

## Whether the bytes are a C name: `[A-Za-z_]\w*`, whole.
is_name : List(U8) -> Bool
is_name = |bytes|
	match bytes.first() {
		Ok(first) => Mask.is_name_start(first) and bytes.all(Mask.is_word)
		Err(_) => Bool.False
	}

## The last byte of a generator's held type, from `start`: `([^)]*\S)\s*\)`,
## the longest run of no `)` whose last byte is no space and after which a
## `)` follows, past any spaces.
held_type_end : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [NoType])
held_type_end = |code, start|
	match Mask.byte_from(code, ')', start) {
		Err(_) => Err(NoType)
		Ok(first_close) => {
			var $end = first_close
			while $end >= start {
				closes = code.get(Mask.spaces_end(code, $end + 1)) == Ok(')')
				if !(Mask.is_space_at(code, $end)) and closes {
					return Ok($end)
				}
				if $end == 0 {
					return Err(NoType)
				}
				$end = $end - 1
			}
			Err(NoType)
		}
	}

## The word at `at`, when a `)` follows it past any spaces: `(\w+)\s*\)`.
closed_word : List(U8), U64 -> Try(Str, [NoPointer])
closed_word = |code, at| {
	end = Mask.word_end(code, at)
	if end > at and code.get(Mask.spaces_end(code, end)) == Ok(')') {
		Ok(Mask.text(code.sublist({ start: at, len: end - at })))
	} else {
		Err(NoPointer)
	}
}

## The `\w` run that ends the bytes, "" for none: `(\w+)$`.
trailing_word : List(U8) -> Str
trailing_word = |bytes|
	match bytes.find_last_index(|byte| !(Mask.is_word(byte))) {
		Ok(last_other) => Mask.text(bytes.drop_first(last_other + 1))
		Err(_) => Mask.text(bytes)
	}

## The last place before `end` that is no `\s`.
last_unspaced : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [Missing])
last_unspaced = |bytes, end|
	match bytes.take_first(end).find_last_index(|byte| !(Mask.is_space(byte))) {
		Ok(at) => Ok(at)
		Err(_) => Err(Missing)
	}

## The `\w` run that ends at `last`, whole.
word_ending_at : List(U8), U64 -> Str
word_ending_at = |bytes, last| {
	before = bytes.take_first(last + 1)
	trailing_word(before)
}

## The name before a `[...]` that closes at `close`: the leftmost `[` of the
## brackets (no `]` between it and `close`) with a word before it, past any
## spaces, is the match a leftmost search finds.
bracketed_name : List(U8), U64 -> Try(Str, [NoName])
bracketed_name = |text, close| {
	var $opens = []
	var $at = close
	var $is_open = Bool.True
	while $is_open and $at > 0 {
		$at = $at - 1
		byte = text.get($at) ?? 0
		if byte == ']' {
			$is_open = Bool.False
		} else if byte == '[' {
			$opens = $opens.prepend($at)
		}
	}
	for open in $opens {
		match last_unspaced(text, open) {
			Ok(before) if Mask.is_word_at(text, before) => return Ok(word_ending_at(text, before))
			_ => {}
		}
	}
	Err(NoName)
}

cookbook/c/items/Item.roc, 112 lines

## A top-level item of a file of Shale's C, as Split.items gives it: its
## kind, the name it declares, and its lines. Every field is set, so none is
## missing: a line field is 0 and a text field "" where the item has none.
##
##   kind           what it is (Item.Kind; Item.kind_name prints it);
##   name           the name it declares: a function's, a type's, a macro's,
##                  an include's path, a generator's type, a test's; a
##                  directive's word and first argument (`if defined`); an
##                  anonymous `enum`'s first enumerator;
##   first, last    its lines, from its opening line to its closing one;
##   comment_first, comment_last
##                  the `//` lines directly above it, no blank between;
##   sig_first, sig_last
##                  its head: a function's or a test's lines up to the one
##                  its body's `{` ends, a wrapped prototype's lines; else its
##                  first line alone;
##   body_first, body_last
##                  a function's or a test's body (both its line, when the
##                  body shares the head's line), a braced item's inside;
##   storage        `static inline`, `static` or "";
##   return_type    a function's or a prototype's return type, as written;
##   macro, held_type
##                  a generator's macro (`VEC_DEFINE`) and the type it holds;
##   makes          a generator macro's own functions, its `Name##_<x>(`
##                  suffixes (`make`, `push`);
##   enumerators    an enum's constants, in order;
##   uses           when asked for, the identifiers a function's, a test's or
##                  a test list's body names, sorted, each once.
Item := {
	kind : Item.Kind,
	name : Str,
	first : U64,
	last : U64,
	comment_first : U64,
	comment_last : U64,
	sig_first : U64,
	sig_last : U64,
	body_first : U64,
	body_last : U64,
	storage : Str,
	return_type : Str,
	macro : Str,
	held_type : Str,
	makes : List(Str),
	enumerators : List(Str),
	uses : List(Str),
}.{

	## The kinds of item the dialect has.
	Kind : [
		Function,
		Prototype,
		Data,
		Struct,
		Enum,
		Union,
		Typedef,
		Macro,
		Guard,
		Include,
		Directive,
		Generator,
		Test,
		TestList,
		StaticAssert,
	]

	## An item of a kind and a name over its lines, every other field empty:
	## the caller sets what its kind has.
	new : Item.Kind, Str, { first : U64, last : U64 } -> Item
	new = |kind, name, { first, last }| {
		kind,
		name,
		first,
		last,
		comment_first: 0,
		comment_last: 0,
		sig_first: first,
		sig_last: first,
		body_first: 0,
		body_last: 0,
		storage: "",
		return_type: "",
		macro: "",
		held_type: "",
		makes: [],
		enumerators: [],
		uses: [],
	}

	## A kind's name as the Shale original printed it: `function`,
	## `test_list`, `static_assert`.
	kind_name : Item.Kind -> Str
	kind_name = |kind|
		match kind {
			Function => "function"
			Prototype => "prototype"
			Data => "data"
			Struct => "struct"
			Enum => "enum"
			Union => "union"
			Typedef => "typedef"
			Macro => "macro"
			Guard => "guard"
			Include => "include"
			Directive => "directive"
			Generator => "generator"
			Test => "test"
			TestList => "test_list"
			StaticAssert => "static_assert"
		}
}

cookbook/c/items/Mask.roc, 229 lines

## The masker the splitter reads Shale's C with, and the byte classes it
## reads by. A line is its bytes, as Shale's strings are, so a column is a
## byte's place. The classes are the regular expressions' and the builtins'
## of cookbook/c/items.shale, the Shale original: `\s` is a space, a tab, a
## newline, a carriage return, a vertical tab or a form feed; `\w` an ASCII
## letter, a digit or `_`; `trim` takes a space, a tab, a carriage return
## and a newline.
Mask := [].{

	## The line with its strings, character literals and comments blanked,
	## each to spaces between its quotes (a comment wholly to spaces), so every
	## column stays where it was. The quotes go first, leftmost first, so a
	## `"` in `'"'` is the literal's and a `//` or a `/*` left after them is a
	## comment's; a quote that nothing closes is left as it is.
	masked : List(U8) -> List(U8)
	masked = |line|
		if line.contains('"') or line.contains('\'') or line.contains('/') {
			masked_slowly(line)
		} else {
			line
		}

	## A regular expression's `\s`.
	is_space : U8 -> Bool
	is_space = |byte|
		byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\n' or byte == '\r' or byte == 0x0b or byte == 0x0c

	## A regular expression's `\w`: an ASCII letter, a digit or `_`.
	is_word : U8 -> Bool
	is_word = |byte|
		Mask.is_name_start(byte) or (byte >= '0' and byte <= '9')

	## The first byte of a C name: an ASCII letter or `_`.
	is_name_start : U8 -> Bool
	is_name_start = |byte|
		(byte >= 'a' and byte <= 'z') or (byte >= 'A' and byte <= 'Z') or byte == '_'

	## Whether the byte at `at` is a `\w`, past the end being none.
	is_word_at : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
	is_word_at = |bytes, at|
		match bytes.get(at) {
			Ok(byte) => Mask.is_word(byte)
			Err(_) => Bool.False
		}

	## Whether the byte at `at` is a `\s`, past the end being none.
	is_space_at : List(U8), U64 -> Bool
	is_space_at = |bytes, at|
		match bytes.get(at) {
			Ok(byte) => Mask.is_space(byte)
			Err(_) => Bool.False
		}

	## The bytes without the spaces, tabs, carriage returns and newlines at
	## their ends, as Shale's `trim` takes them.
	trimmed : List(U8) -> List(U8)
	trimmed = |bytes|
		match bytes.find_first_index(|byte| !(is_blank(byte))) {
			Ok(start) => {
				end = bytes.find_last_index(|byte| !(is_blank(byte))) ?? start
				bytes.sublist({ start, len: end + 1 - start })
			}
			Err(_) => []
		}

	## The first place at `at` or after it that is no `\s`: the end of `\s*`.
	spaces_end : List(U8), U64 -> U64
	spaces_end = |bytes, at| {
		var $end = at
		while Mask.is_space_at(bytes, $end) {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		$end
	}

	## The first place at `at` or after it that is no `\w`: the end of `\w*`.
	word_end : List(U8), U64 -> U64
	word_end = |bytes, at| {
		var $end = at
		while Mask.is_word_at(bytes, $end) {
			$end = $end + 1
		}
		$end
	}

	## Whether the bytes hold the text at `at`.
	holds_at : List(U8), U64, Str -> Bool
	holds_at = |bytes, at, text| {
		wanted = text.to_utf8()
		bytes.sublist({ start: at, len: wanted.len() }) == wanted
	}

	## The place of the first two bytes `pair` at `from` or after it.
	pair_from : List(U8), (U8, U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [Missing])
	pair_from = |bytes, (first, second), from| {
		var $at = from
		while $at + 1 < bytes.len() {
			match Mask.byte_from(bytes, first, $at) {
				Ok(found) if bytes.get(found + 1) == Ok(second) => return Ok(found)
				Ok(found) => {
					$at = found + 1
				}
				Err(_) => return Err(Missing)
			}
		}
		Err(Missing)
	}

	## The place of the first `byte` at `from` or after it.
	byte_from : List(U8), U8, U64 -> Try(U64, [Missing])
	byte_from = |bytes, byte, from|
		match bytes.drop_first(from).find_first_index(|each| each == byte) {
			Ok(offset) => Ok(from + offset)
			Err(_) => Err(Missing)
		}

	## The bytes as text: Shale's C is UTF-8, and a mask cuts only at ASCII.
	text : List(U8) -> Str
	text = |bytes| Str.from_utf8_lossy(bytes)
}

## The masker's work on a line that holds a quote or a `/`.
masked_slowly : List(U8) -> List(U8)
masked_slowly = |line| {
	has_double = line.contains('"')
	has_single = line.contains('\'')
	quotes_blanked =
		if has_double or has_single {
			blank_quotes(line, { double: has_double, single: has_single })
		} else {
			line
		}
	comments_blanked =
		if Mask.pair_from(quotes_blanked, ('/', '*'), 0) != Err(Missing) {
			blank_block_comments(quotes_blanked)
		} else {
			quotes_blanked
		}
	match Mask.pair_from(comments_blanked, ('/', '/'), 0) {
		Ok(cut) => comments_blanked.take_first(cut).concat(List.repeat(' ', comments_blanked.len() - cut))
		Err(_) => comments_blanked
	}
}

## A byte Shale's `trim` takes off a text's ends.
is_blank : U8 -> Bool
is_blank = |byte| byte == ' ' or byte == '\t' or byte == '\r' or byte == '\n'

## The line with each string (`double`) or character literal (`single`)
## blanked between its quotes, leftmost first: a quote opens one, `\` and the
## byte after it are inside it, and the same quote closes it. One that the
## line does not close is no literal, and the search goes on after its quote.
blank_quotes : List(U8), { double : Bool, single : Bool } -> List(U8)
blank_quotes = |line, kinds| {
	count = line.len()
	var $out = line
	var $at = 0
	while $at < count {
		byte = line.get($at) ?? 0
		is_open = (byte == '"' and kinds.double) or (byte == '\'' and kinds.single)
		closed = if is_open {
			quote_close(line, $at, byte)
		} else {
			Err(Unclosed)
		}
		match closed {
			Ok(close) => {
				$out = blanked($out, { start: $at + 1, end: close })
				$at = close + 1
			}
			Err(_) => {
				$at = $at + 1
			}
		}
	}
	$out
}

## Where the literal opened by `quote` at `open` closes: `[^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)*"`.
quote_close : List(U8), U64, U8 -> Try(U64, [Unclosed])
quote_close = |line, open, quote| {
	count = line.len()
	var $at = open + 1
	while $at < count {
		byte = line.get($at) ?? 0
		if byte == quote {
			return Ok($at)
		}
		if byte == '\\' {
			# `\\.`: the escape takes any byte but a newline after it.
			if $at + 1 >= count or line.get($at + 1) == Ok('\n') {
				return Err(Unclosed)
			}
			$at = $at + 2
		} else {
			$at = $at + 1
		}
	}
	Err(Unclosed)
}

## The line with each `/* */` comment wholly spaces: `/\*[^*]*\*/`, so a
## comment that holds a `*` of its own is none.
blank_block_comments : List(U8) -> List(U8)
blank_block_comments = |line| {
	var $out = line
	var $at = 0
	while $at + 1 < line.len() {
		if line.get($at) == Ok('/') and line.get($at + 1) == Ok('*') {
			match Mask.byte_from(line, '*', $at + 2) {
				Ok(star) if line.get(star + 1) == Ok('/') => {
					$out = blanked($out, { start: $at, end: star + 2 })
					$at = star + 2
				}
				_ => {
					$at = $at + 1
				}
			}
		} else {
			$at = $at + 1
		}
	}
	$out
}

## The bytes with those from `start` up to `end` made spaces.
blanked : List(U8), { start : U64, end : U64 } -> List(U8)
blanked = |bytes, { start, end }|
	bytes.take_first(start).concat(List.repeat(' ', end - start)).concat(bytes.drop_first(end))

cookbook/c/items/Paths.roc, 23 lines

## How the C recipes read a file's path below the folder they walk: whether
## it is the tests', and whether it is under a folder named `out`, the
## build's output, which no recipe reads.
Paths := [].{

	## Whether `path`, below the folder, is the tests': in a `tests` folder,
	## or a file whose name starts with `test` (c/foundation/test.h, the
	## tests' runner).
	is_test_path : Str, Str -> Bool
	is_test_path = |folder, path| {
		below = Str.from_utf8_lossy(path.to_utf8().drop_first(folder.count_utf8_bytes() + 1))
		file_name = match below.split_on("/").last() {
			Ok(last) => last
			Err(_) => below
		}
		below.starts_with("tests/") or below.contains("/tests/") or file_name.starts_with("test")
	}

	## Whether a folder below `folder` on the way to `path` is named `out`.
	is_in_out_folder : Str, Str -> Bool
	is_in_out_folder = |folder, path|
		path.drop_prefix("${folder}/").split_on("/").drop_last(1).contains("out")
}

cookbook/c/items/Split.roc, 441 lines

## The splitter: a file of Shale's C split into its top-level items, in
## order. There is no C parser on the box, and none is wanted:
## c/check_discipline.shale holds the C to a shape a line reader can trust,
## and the build fails when a file breaks it, so the dialect is this
## reader's contract (c/docs/style.md, "The top level"):
##
##   - every line at column 0 opens a top-level item or closes one, and
##     everything inside an item is indented;
##   - every function starts at column 0 with `static` (or is `int main(`);
##   - an opening brace ends its line, and a declaration is one a line;
##   - comments are `//`, `/* */` only inside a macro; there are no tabs;
##   - a header is framed by `// <name>: ...`, its guard and `#endif`.
##
## Every line of the file is in exactly one item, or is blank, or is a `//`
## comment line between items. A line that is none of these is an error
## naming the file and its line, never a guess. It is cookbook/c/items.shale's
## `c_items`, the Shale original, which the C recipes not yet ported still
## read.
import Guard
import Head
import Item
import Mask
import Words

Split := [].{

	## The text's lines as Shale's `lines` splits them: at each newline, with
	## no empty last line after a final one.
	lines : Str -> List(List(U8))
	lines = |text| {
		bytes = text.to_utf8()
		if bytes.is_empty() {
			[]
		} else if bytes.last() == Ok('\n') {
			bytes.split_on('\n').drop_last(1)
		} else {
			bytes.split_on('\n')
		}
	}

	## The items of the C file at `path`, its text `text`, in order (Item has
	## their fields); `uses` fills each function's, test's and test list's
	## uses. A line the dialect does not account for is an error, the stop's
	## words: `<path>:<line>: <why>: <the line>`.
	items : { path : Str, text : Str, uses : Bool } -> Try(List(Item), Str)
	items = |{ path, text, uses }| {
		file = { path, lines: Split.lines(text) }
		count = file.lines.len()
		var $items = []
		var $comment_first = 0
		var $comment_last = 0
		var $at = 1
		while $at <= count {
			raw = line_at(file, $at)
			if raw.is_empty() {
				$comment_first = 0
				$at = $at + 1
			} else if raw.starts_with(['/', '/']) {
				if $comment_first == 0 {
					$comment_first = $at
				}
				$comment_last = $at
				$at = $at + 1
			} else if raw.starts_with([' ']) {
				return Err(unaccounted(file, $at, "an indented line outside every item"))
			} else {
				opened = item_at(file, $at, Mask.masked(raw))?
				commented =
					if $comment_first == 0 {
						opened
					} else {
						{ ..opened, comment_first: $comment_first, comment_last: $comment_last }
					}
				$items = $items.append(with_uses(file, commented, uses))
				$comment_first = 0
				$at = commented.last + 1
			}
		}
		if path.ends_with(".h") {
			Guard.framed(path, $items)
		} else {
			Ok($items)
		}
	}

	## The masked text of the file's lines from `first` to `last`, counted from
	## 1, joined by newlines: Shale's `c_masked_text`.
	masked_text : List(List(U8)), { first : U64, last : U64 } -> List(U8)
	masked_text = |file_lines, { first, last }| {
		var $text = []
		var $at = first
		while $at <= last {
			if $at > first {
				$text = $text.append('\n')
			}
			$text = $text.concat(Mask.masked(file_lines.get($at - 1) ?? []))
			$at = $at + 1
		}
		$text
	}
}

## A file being split: its path, for the errors, and its lines.
CFile : { path : Str, lines : List(List(U8)) }

## Line `number` of the file, counted from 1.
line_at : CFile, U64 -> List(U8)
line_at = |file, number| file.lines.get(number - 1) ?? []

## The error for line `number`, which the dialect does not account for: its
## place and why first, then the line.
unaccounted : CFile, U64, Str -> Str
unaccounted = |file, number, why|
	unaccounted_text(file, number, why, Mask.text(line_at(file, number)))

## The error for line `number`, with `shown` in place of the line.
unaccounted_text : CFile, U64, Str, Str -> Str
unaccounted_text = |file, number, why, shown|
	"${file.path}:${number.to_str()}: ${why}: ${shown}"

## The item's uses, when asked for and it is a function, a test or a test
## list with a body. A body on its head's line is what follows its `{`.
with_uses : CFile, Item, Bool -> Item
with_uses = |file, item, wanted| {
	has_body = item.body_first != 0
	is_code = item.kind == Function or item.kind == Test or item.kind == TestList
	if wanted and has_body and is_code {
		text = Split.masked_text(file.lines, { first: item.body_first, last: item.body_last })
		body =
			if item.body_first == item.sig_last and item.kind != TestList {
				match Mask.byte_from(text, '{', 0) {
					Ok(brace) => text.drop_first(brace)
					Err(_) => text
				}
			} else {
				text
			}
		{ ..item, uses: Words.uses(body) }
	} else {
		item
	}
}

## The line that closes the braced item opened at line `from`: the first
## line after it at column 0, which must start with `}`. A blank line, an
## indented one or a `#` directive (which C writes at column 0, as an
## `#ifdef` in a body is) is inside; anything else at column 0 is an error.
brace_close : CFile, U64, Str -> Try(U64, Str)
brace_close = |file, from, what| {
	count = file.lines.len()
	var $at = from + 1
	while $at <= count {
		match line_at(file, $at).first() {
			Ok('}') => return Ok($at)
			Ok(byte) if byte != ' ' and byte != '#' => {
				why = "a line at column 0 inside ${what} opened at line ${from.to_str()}, which only a `}` may close"
				return Err(unaccounted(file, $at, why))
			}
			_ => {}
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	Err(unaccounted(file, from, "${what} that no `}` at column 0 closes"))
}

## The last line of the parenthesized item that opens at line `from`: where
## its masked parentheses balance. A line after the first is indented, or
## starts with the closing `)` at column 0.
paren_close : CFile, U64 -> Try(U64, Str)
paren_close = |file, from| {
	count = file.lines.len()
	var $depth = 0
	var $at = from
	while $at <= count {
		raw = line_at(file, $at)
		if $at > from and !(raw.starts_with([' '])) and !(raw.starts_with([')'])) {
			return Err(unaccounted(file, $at, "a line at column 0 inside the parentheses opened at line ${from.to_str()}"))
		}
		code = Mask.masked(raw)
		opens = code.count_if(|byte| byte == '(').to_i64_wrap()
		closes = code.count_if(|byte| byte == ')').to_i64_wrap()
		$depth = $depth + opens - closes
		if $depth <= 0 {
			return Ok($at)
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	Err(unaccounted(file, from, "parentheses that never close"))
}

## The last line of a head that opens at line `from`: the first whose masked
## code ends with `{`, `;` or `}`. A line after the first is indented.
head_close : CFile, U64 -> Try(U64, Str)
head_close = |file, from| {
	count = file.lines.len()
	var $at = from
	while $at <= count {
		raw = line_at(file, $at)
		if $at > from and !(raw.starts_with([' '])) {
			return Err(unaccounted(file, $at, "a line at column 0 inside the head opened at line ${from.to_str()}"))
		}
		match last_code_byte(raw) {
			Ok(byte) if byte == '{' or byte == ';' or byte == '}' => return Ok($at)
			_ => {}
		}
		$at = $at + 1
	}
	Err(unaccounted(file, from, "a head that no `{` or `;` ends"))
}

## The last byte of a line's masked code, trimmed.
last_code_byte : List(U8) -> Try(U8, [ListWasEmpty])
last_code_byte = |raw| Mask.trimmed(Mask.masked(raw)).last()

## The item that line `at` opens, its masked code `code`.
item_at : CFile, U64, List(U8) -> Try(Item, Str)
item_at = |file, at, code| {
	raw = line_at(file, at)
	opens = |text| raw.starts_with(text.to_utf8())
	if opens("#") {
		hash_item(file, at, code)
	} else if opens("static inline ") {
		static_item(file, at, "static inline")
	} else if opens("static ") {
		static_item(file, at, "static")
	} else if opens("typedef ") or opens("enum ") {
		type_item(file, at, code)
	} else if opens("SLICE_TYPE(") or opens("VEC_DEFINE(") or opens("MAP_DEFINE(") {
		generator_item(file, at, code)
	} else if opens("TEST(") {
		test_item(file, at, code)
	} else if opens("TEST_MAIN(") or opens("TEST_PART(") or opens("TEST_PARTS_MAIN(") {
		test_list_item(file, at, code)
	} else if opens("_Static_assert(") {
		static_assert_item(file, at)
	} else if opens("int main(") {
		main_item(file, at)
	} else {
		Err(unaccounted(file, at, "a line at column 0 that opens no item the dialect knows"))
	}
}

## The `static` or `static inline` item at line `at`: a function, a
## prototype or data.
static_item : CFile, U64, Str -> Try(Item, Str)
static_item = |file, at, storage| {
	last = head_close(file, at)?
	flat = spaces_made_one(Split.masked_text(file.lines, { first: at, last }))
	ending = last_code_byte(line_at(file, last))
	match Head.function_head(flat) {
		Ok({ return_type, name }) => {
			head = { ..Item.new(Prototype, name, { first: at, last }), storage, return_type, sig_last: last }
			match ending {
				Ok(';') => Ok(head)
				Ok('}') => Ok({ ..head, kind: Function, body_first: last, body_last: last })
				_ => {
					close = brace_close(file, last, "the function `${name}`")?
					function = { ..head, kind: Function, last: close }
					if close > last + 1 {
						Ok({ ..function, body_first: last + 1, body_last: close - 1 })
					} else {
						Ok(function)
					}
				}
			}
		}
		Err(_) => {
			name = Head.data_name(flat)
			data = { ..Item.new(Data, name, { first: at, last }), storage, sig_last: last }
			if ending == Ok('{') {
				close = brace_close(file, last, "the data `${name}`")?
				Ok({ ..data, last: close, body_first: last + 1, body_last: close - 1 })
			} else {
				Ok(data)
			}
		}
	}
}

## The text with each run of `\s` made one space.
spaces_made_one : List(U8) -> List(U8)
spaces_made_one = |text|
	text.fold(
		[],
		|out, byte|
			if !(Mask.is_space(byte)) {
				out.append(byte)
			} else if out.last() == Ok(' ') {
				# A space is `\s`, so one that ends `out` is a run's already.
				out
			} else {
				out.append(' ')
			},
	)

## The `typedef` or `enum` item at line `at`.
type_item : CFile, U64, List(U8) -> Try(Item, Str)
type_item = |file, at, code| {
	kind = match Head.type_keyword(code) {
		Struct => Struct
		Enum => Enum
		Union => Union
		NoKeyword => Typedef
	}
	last = head_close(file, at)?
	headed = { ..Item.new(kind, "", { first: at, last }), sig_last: last }
	braced =
		if last_code_byte(line_at(file, last)) == Ok('{') {
			close = brace_close(file, last, "the ${Item.kind_name(kind)}")?
			{ ..headed, last: close, body_first: last + 1, body_last: close - 1 }
		} else {
			headed
		}
	text = Split.masked_text(file.lines, { first: at, last: braced.last })
	declared =
		if code.starts_with("typedef".to_utf8()) {
			match (kind, Head.pointer_name(text, WithoutConst), Head.declared_name(text)) {
				(Typedef, Ok(pointer), _) => pointer
				(_, _, Ok(name)) => name
				_ => ""
			}
		} else {
			Head.enum_tag(code) ?? ""
		}
	enumerators = if kind == Enum {
		Words.enumerators(text)
	} else {
		[]
	}
	name =
		match enumerators.first() {
			Ok(first) if declared == "" => first
			_ => declared
		}
	if name == "" {
		Err(unaccounted(file, at, "a ${Item.kind_name(kind)} whose name this reader can't find"))
	} else {
		Ok({ ..braced, name, enumerators })
	}
}

## The `#` item at line `at`: an include, a macro (to its last `\` line),
## the header's guard (Split.items frames it), or another directive.
hash_item : CFile, U64, List(U8) -> Try(Item, Str)
hash_item = |file, at, code| {
	count = file.lines.len()
	var $last = at
	while line_at(file, $last).last() == Ok('\\') and $last < count {
		$last = $last + 1
	}
	last = $last
	match Head.directive(code) {
		Err(_) => Err(unaccounted(file, at, "a `#` line with no directive"))
		Ok({ word, argument: _ }) if word == "include" =>
			match Head.include_path(line_at(file, at)) {
				Ok(path) => Ok(Item.new(Include, path, { first: at, last }))
				Err(_) => Err(unaccounted(file, at, "an `#include` with no path"))
			}
		Ok({ word, argument }) if word == "define" => {
			defined = Item.new(Macro, argument, { first: at, last })
			if last > at {
				makes = Words.suffixes(Split.masked_text(file.lines, { first: at, last }))
				Ok({ ..defined, body_first: at + 1, body_last: last, makes })
			} else {
				Ok(defined)
			}
		}
		Ok({ word, argument }) => {
			name = if argument == "" {
				word
			} else {
				"${word} ${argument}"
			}
			Ok(Item.new(Directive, name, { first: at, last }))
		}
	}
}

## The `VEC_DEFINE(`, `MAP_DEFINE(` or `SLICE_TYPE(` item at line `at`.
generator_item : CFile, U64, List(U8) -> Try(Item, Str)
generator_item = |file, at, code|
	match Head.generator(code) {
		Err(_) => Err(unaccounted(file, at, "a generator line whose name and type this reader can't find"))
		Ok({ macro, name, held_type }) => {
			close = paren_close(file, at)?
			Ok({ ..Item.new(Generator, name, { first: at, last: close }), macro, held_type })
		}
	}

## The `TEST(name) {` item at line `at`.
test_item : CFile, U64, List(U8) -> Try(Item, Str)
test_item = |file, at, code|
	match Head.test_name(code) {
		Err(_) => Err(unaccounted(file, at, "a `TEST(` line that is not `TEST(name) {`"))
		Ok(name) => {
			close = brace_close(file, at, "the test `${name}`")?
			test = Item.new(Test, name, { first: at, last: close })
			if close > at + 1 {
				Ok({ ..test, body_first: at + 1, body_last: close - 1 })
			} else {
				Ok(test)
			}
		}
	}

## The `TEST_MAIN(`, `TEST_PART(` or `TEST_PARTS_MAIN(` item at line `at`,
## named for its macro, or a `TEST_PART(` for its part.
test_list_item : CFile, U64, List(U8) -> Try(Item, Str)
test_list_item = |file, at, code| {
	head = Head.test_list(code)
	close = paren_close(file, at)?
	name = if head.macro == "TEST_PART" and head.argument != "" {
		head.argument
	} else {
		head.macro
	}
	Ok({ ..Item.new(TestList, name, { first: at, last: close }), body_first: at, body_last: close })
}

## The `_Static_assert(` item at line `at`, named for its first name that is
## not `_Static_assert` or `sizeof`.
static_assert_item : CFile, U64 -> Try(Item, Str)
static_assert_item = |file, at| {
	close = paren_close(file, at)?
	names = Words.names(Split.masked_text(file.lines, { first: at, last: close }))
	name = names.find_first(|each| each != "_Static_assert" and each != "sizeof") ?? ""
	Ok(Item.new(StaticAssert, name, { first: at, last: close }))
}

## The `int main(` function at line `at`.
main_item : CFile, U64 -> Try(Item, Str)
main_item = |file, at| {
	last = head_close(file, at)?
	close = brace_close(file, last, "the function `main`")?
	main = { ..Item.new(Function, "main", { first: at, last: close }), return_type: "int", sig_last: last }
	if close > last + 1 {
		Ok({ ..main, body_first: last + 1, body_last: close - 1 })
	} else {
		Ok(main)
	}
}

cookbook/c/items/Words.roc, 292 lines

## The words of an item's masked text: its names, the names its body uses,
## an enum's constants and a generator macro's own functions, each the
## regular expression of cookbook/c/items.shale, the Shale original, done by
## hand.
import Mask

Words := [].{

	## The names in the text, in order, each as often as it is there:
	## `\b[A-Za-z_]\w*`, a `\w` run that starts with a letter or `_`.
	names : List(U8) -> List(Str)
	names = |text| {
		var $names = []
		var $at = 0
		while $at < text.len() {
			end = Mask.word_end(text, $at)
			if end > $at {
				if Mask.is_name_start(text.get($at) ?? 0) {
					$names = $names.append(Mask.text(text.sublist({ start: $at, len: end - $at })))
				}
				$at = end
			} else {
				$at = $at + 1
			}
		}
		$names
	}

	## The identifiers the text names, sorted, each once: no keyword, no
	## number, no member after `.` or `->`, and no directive's own word
	## (`ifdef`), though the names a directive tests are uses.
	uses : List(U8) -> List(Str)
	uses = |text| {
		bare = without_directive_words(without_members(text))
		sorted = Words.names(bare)
			.keep_if(|name| !(keywords.contains(name)))
			.sort_with(Words.byte_order)
		sorted.fold(
			[],
			|once, name|
				if once.last() == Ok(name) {
					once
				} else {
					once.append(name)
				},
		)
	}

	## An enum's constants, from its masked text: each name that starts an
	## item of its braces, `^\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)` in each part between commas.
	enumerators : List(U8) -> List(Str)
	enumerators = |text|
		match Mask.byte_from(text, '{', 0) {
			Err(_) => []
			Ok(open) =>
				match Mask.byte_from(text, '}', open + 1) {
					Err(_) => []
					Ok(close) => {
						inside = text.sublist({ start: open + 1, len: close - open - 1 })
						inside.split_on(',').fold(
							[],
							|found, part|
								match leading_name(part) {
									Ok(name) => found.append(name)
									Err(_) => found
								},
						)
					}
				}
		}

	## A generator macro's own functions, its `Name##_<x>(` suffixes, from its
	## definition's masked text, each once, in order: each match of
	## `static\s[^(]*##_(\w+)\s*\(`.
	suffixes : List(U8) -> List(Str)
	suffixes = |text| {
		var $found = []
		var $at = 0
		while $at < text.len() {
			match suffix_at(text, $at) {
				Ok({ suffix, open }) => {
					if !($found.contains(suffix)) {
						$found = $found.append(suffix)
					}
					$at = open + 1
				}
				Err(_) => {
					$at = $at + 1
				}
			}
		}
		$found
	}

	## Two texts in the order of their bytes, a text before every longer one
	## it starts, as Shale's `sort` puts strings.
	byte_order : Str, Str -> [Before, Same, After]
	byte_order = |first, second| {
		pairs = List.map2(first.to_utf8(), second.to_utf8(), |x, y| (x, y))
		match pairs.find_first(|(x, y)| x != y) {
			Ok((x, y)) =>
				if x < y {
					Before
				} else {
					After
				}
			Err(_) =>
				if first.count_utf8_bytes() < second.count_utf8_bytes() {
					Before
				} else if first.count_utf8_bytes() > second.count_utf8_bytes() {
					After
				} else {
					Same
				}
		}
	}
}

## C's keywords and the words of its types and storage, which are no use of
## a name.
keywords : List(Str)
keywords = [
	"auto",
	"break",
	"case",
	"char",
	"const",
	"continue",
	"default",
	"do",
	"double",
	"else",
	"enum",
	"extern",
	"float",
	"for",
	"goto",
	"if",
	"inline",
	"int",
	"long",
	"register",
	"restrict",
	"return",
	"short",
	"signed",
	"sizeof",
	"static",
	"struct",
	"switch",
	"typedef",
	"union",
	"unsigned",
	"void",
	"volatile",
	"while",
	"_Alignof",
	"_Bool",
	"_Static_assert",
	"bool",
	"true",
	"false",
	"NULL",
]

## The text with each member after `.` or `->` made one space:
## `(\.|->)\s*[A-Za-z_]\w*`.
without_members : List(U8) -> List(U8)
without_members = |text| {
	var $out = []
	var $at = 0
	while $at < text.len() {
		byte = text.get($at) ?? 0
		after = if byte == '.' {
			$at + 1
		} else if byte == '-' and text.get($at + 1) == Ok('>') {
			$at + 2
		} else {
			0
		}
		start = Mask.spaces_end(text, after)
		if after > 0 and Mask.is_name_start(text.get(start) ?? 0) {
			$out = $out.append(' ')
			$at = Mask.word_end(text, start)
		} else {
			$out = $out.append(byte)
			$at = $at + 1
		}
	}
	$out
}

## The text with each directive's `#` and word gone, at the start or after a
## newline, the newline kept: `(^|\n)#\s*\w+`.
without_directive_words : List(U8) -> List(U8)
without_directive_words = |text| {
	var $out = []
	var $at = 0
	while $at < text.len() {
		byte = text.get($at) ?? 0
		match directive_word_end(text, $at) {
			Ok(end) => {
				$at = end
			}
			Err(_) =>
				if byte == '\n' {
					match directive_word_end(text, $at + 1) {
						Ok(end) => {
							$out = $out.append('\n')
							$at = end
						}
						Err(_) => {
							$out = $out.append(byte)
							$at = $at + 1
						}
					}
				} else {
					$out = $out.append(byte)
					$at = $at + 1
				}
		}
	}
	$out
}

## Where `#\s*\w+` at `at` ends, at the text's start or after a newline; the
## start alone is asked of at 0.
directive_word_end : List(U8), U64 -> Try(U64, [NoDirective])
directive_word_end = |text, at| {
	is_line_start = at == 0 or text.get(at - 1) == Ok('\n')
	word_start = Mask.spaces_end(text, at + 1)
	word_end = Mask.word_end(text, word_start)
	if is_line_start and text.get(at) == Ok('#') and word_end > word_start {
		Ok(word_end)
	} else {
		Err(NoDirective)
	}
}

## The name an enum's part starts with, past any spaces.
leading_name : List(U8) -> Try(Str, [NoName])
leading_name = |part| {
	start = Mask.spaces_end(part, 0)
	end = Mask.word_end(part, start)
	if end > start and Mask.is_name_start(part.get(start) ?? 0) {
		Ok(Mask.text(part.sublist({ start, len: end - start })))
	} else {
		Err(NoName)
	}
}

## The suffix of `static\s[^(]*##_(\w+)\s*\(` at `at`, and its `(`: the last
## `##_` before the first `(` after `static`, which only a name and spaces
## may follow up to that `(`.
suffix_at : List(U8), U64 -> Try({ suffix : Str, open : U64 }, [NoSuffix])
suffix_at = |text, at| {
	after = at + 7
	if !(Mask.holds_at(text, at, "static")) or !(Mask.is_space_at(text, at + 6)) {
		return Err(NoSuffix)
	}
	match Mask.byte_from(text, '(', after) {
		Err(_) => Err(NoSuffix)
		Ok(open) => {
			span = text.sublist({ start: after, len: open - after })
			match last_paste(span) {
				Err(_) => Err(NoSuffix)
				Ok(paste) => {
					start = after + paste + 3
					end = Mask.word_end(text, start)
					if end > start and Mask.spaces_end(text, end) == open {
						Ok({ suffix: Mask.text(text.sublist({ start, len: end - start })), open })
					} else {
						Err(NoSuffix)
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

## The place of the last `##_` in the bytes.
last_paste : List(U8) -> Try(U64, [Missing])
last_paste = |bytes| {
	var $at = bytes.len()
	while $at >= 3 {
		$at = $at - 1
		if Mask.holds_at(bytes, $at - 2, "##_") {
			return Ok($at - 2)
		}
	}
	Err(Missing)
}

## The splitter the recipes that read Shale's C share: a file of Shale's C
## split into its top-level items, from the dialect c/check_discipline.shale
## holds. A recipe names it by a relative path in its app's header (`items:
## "../items/main.roc"`, then `import items.Split`). It reaches no effect:
## a recipe reads the file and hands Split.items its text.
##
##   Split   the splitter, Shale's `lines` and an item's masked text
##   Guard   a header's guard, framed
##   Item    an item and its kinds
##   Mask    the masker, and the byte classes the readers read by
##   Head    the readers of an item's opening line or head
##   Words   the names in an item's text: its uses, an enum's constants
##   Paths   a file's path read: the tests', or under a folder named `out`
package [Guard, Head, Item, Mask, Paths, Split, Words] {}
